props.name: nav
props.doc: The places of the app, in groups; an empty `label` draws none.

props.name: brand
props.doc: The app's name: the logo when `#logo` is not given, and the name of the link home; unset, a translated "App".

props.name: home
props.doc: Where the logo leads; the item on it is the current page only on it, not under it. A `javascript:` or `data:` address is refused, as for the places.

props.name: current
props.doc: The path of the page shown (`useRoute().path`): it lights its item and closes the sheet.

props.name: collapsed
props.doc: Desktop: only the icons show. Bound to a value, the shell follows it and only asks through `update:collapsed`; unbound or `undefined`, it keeps its own.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The places are on their way: with `nav` still empty, the sidebar draws rows in their shape.

events.name: update:collapsed
events.doc: The sidebar was collapsed or opened out: its button or Ctrl or ⌘ B.

slots.name: logo
slots.doc: The logo in the sidebar's head and in the narrow bar: a mark and the name.

slots.name: mark
slots.doc: The mark alone, for the collapsed sidebar: a 24px glyph or image, over the button. Without it the collapsed head holds the button alone.

slots.name: banner
slots.doc: A band under a line at the foot of the sidebar: a goal with its bar, a notice. Its words stand on the places' icons. The collapsed sidebar has no room for it.

slots.name: footer
slots.doc: The foot of the sidebar: the person signed in, a switch of theme.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The page.

UiAppShell.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: The frame of an app, a sidebar of its places with the page beside it. It is the root of the app's layout, with UiToaster and UiConfirm mounted beside it.

decisions.label: Sidebar
decisions.text: The sidebar holds the logo (a link home), the places in groups (`nav`, each a link of the panel list's rows, `utils/panelList`, with a Lucide icon, a label cut to one line, and a count), `#banner` above the foot (a goal, a notice), and `#footer` at the bottom.

decisions.label: Current place
decisions.text: One place is lit, its label semibold: the one whose `to` is `current` itself (a section of one page, `#billing`), else the deepest whose `to` contains its path, a trailing slash no part of it; `home` and the root `/` are lit only on themselves, and of two places with one address the first. The app passes `current`, since the shell knows no router. Under forced colors the current place takes the highlight.

decisions.label: Collapsing
decisions.text: On desktop the sidebar collapses to its icons, by the button beside the logo (under `#mark`, or alone when collapsed) or by Ctrl or ⌘ B; each icon is named by a UiTooltip. Collapsed without `#mark` there is no link home, so the app lists home among its places; dev warns when it does not, and when `current` is not given. `v-model:collapsed` keeps the state where the app wants it; keeping it across visits is the app's: write it on `update:collapsed` (a cookie) and read it in setup, so the first paint is already right, on the server too; read after mount, the sidebar opens out and slides back. When it is bound, the shell follows it and only asks for a change.

decisions.label: Narrow
decisions.text: Narrow means the shell's own width is under 768px. There a bar holds the menu button and the logo, and the sidebar slides in from the start as a sheet (by the menu button, or Ctrl or ⌘ B). The focus moves in and stays; Escape or the backdrop closes the sheet, and so does a new `current`.

decisions.label: Keys
decisions.text: The keys do nothing under a window or a panel. With two shells, they reach the one the focus is in, else the first. In Firefox, Ctrl or ⌘ B is the bookmarks sidebar's too: where the shell acts on the key it takes it, held as well.

decisions.label: Loading
decisions.text: While the app's places are on their way (`loading`, `nav` still empty) the sidebar draws five rows in their shape, a glyph's square and a line; the logo, the collapse button and `#footer` are there at once, and `#banner` waits. Collapsed, the rows are their squares alone. When the places come nothing moves: the rows are the places' height, the sidebar its width; for places in one group without a heading, since a second group or a heading moves the rows under the first. With places already in view `loading` changes nothing: a sidebar is not dimmed for a refresh.

decisions.label: Height
decisions.text: The page scrolls inside the shell, which is as tall as the window unless `--ui-shell-height` says otherwise. A new path opens the page at its top; a new hash, a section of the same page, keeps the place.

doc.keyboard:
The first stop is a skip link, shown only while focused. Then come the link home, the collapse button and the places, each a link.
- `Enter`: on the skip link, puts the focus on the page.
- `Ctrl+B` `Meta+B`: Ctrl or ⌘ B collapses the sidebar, or opens and closes the sheet while the shell is narrow; not while typing in a text field or an editor, not under a window or a panel, and a held key toggles once.
In the sheet, where the focus moves in:
- `Tab`: stays inside.
- `Escape`: closes it, as the backdrop does, and the focus returns to the menu button.
Collapsing from the link home or from `#banner` hands the focus to the collapse button, so it is never dropped.
doc.reader:
- Skip link: comes first.
- Sidebar: a navigation landmark, and the sheet a modal dialog of the same name.
- Group: its heading names its list, open and collapsed.
- Current place: `aria-current="page"`.
- Collapsed row: named by its label and its count; the count on the icon's corner is a mark the reader skips.
- Buttons: the collapse and menu buttons say what they open (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`).
- Logo: a link named by the brand and "home".
- Loading: a status region, always there, says "Loading…" while the places come; the navigation is busy (`aria-busy`), so the sheet opened meanwhile says it too; the rows in their shape are hidden.
doc.states: Desktop open; desktop collapsed to icons, each named by a tooltip, with `#banner` gone; narrow, with the sheet closed or open, showing the full sidebar even when the desktop one is collapsed; loading, open and collapsed, with rows in the places' shape. On a row: hover, focus, and the current place, which takes the highlight under forced colors. In dev, a missing `current` and a collapsed head with no way home warn.
doc.notFor:
- A set of panes on one screen: UiTabs.
- A window or a panel over the page: UiModal or UiDrawer.
- The name of the page inside the main area: UiHeader `page`.
- Places inside a section of a page: UiListItem links in a UiList.

props.name: x
props.doc: The time axis: one date per point, `2026-09` a month, `2026-09-24` a day; text that is not a date stays as it is.

props.name: series
props.doc: The series, in the order they take the chart colors, five at most. Each is `key`, `label` and `values`; `variant: 'line'` draws it unfilled, `dashed` for a figure of another kind, `total: false` keeps its sum out of the legend.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: What the chart shows, for a screen reader: "Spending and income by month".

props.name: grain
props.doc: What one point stands for: the labels and the tooltip read the dates by it; `weekday` names a day of one week, "Tue".

props.name: format
props.doc: How values read in the legend, the tooltip and the table; `money` writes the currency code after the digits, `1,234.00 USD`. The axis prints compact figures (or percents) without the unit.

props.name: curve
props.doc: `smooth` bends through the points without passing them, `linear` joins them, `step` holds each value.

props.name: height
props.doc: The height in pixels, the time axis included; the legend is below it.

props.name: yAxis
props.doc: The value axis with its grid; off for a chart that only shows a shape.

props.name: legend
props.doc: The legend with each series' total, a press shows one series alone.

props.name: tooltipTotal
props.doc: A sum of some series under them in the tooltip and the table: `{ label: 'Revenue', of: ['orders', 'events'] }`.

props.name: partial
props.doc: The last point is a period still going: its segment is dashed, its label and tooltip say so.

props.name: highlight
props.doc: The index of the point in light, the one the card's headline speaks of: a dot on each series there.

UiAreaChart.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: Values over time as areas and lines. Take it for a flow over time, usually in the body of a UiChartCard.

decisions.label: Data
decisions.text: `x` is the time axis: dates that the library labels by `grain`, with the year on the first label shown and where it changes. Names that are not dates (regions, products) are categories: UiBarChart labels each. Each series is its `values` in that order. A `null` is a gap where the line breaks, never a zero.

decisions.label: Series
decisions.text: A series is an area, or a `line`; `dashed` marks a figure of another kind (a profit over revenue). A `muted` series is drawn in gray behind the rest, as a period to compare with, and takes no color.

decisions.label: Value axis
decisions.text: The value axis covers every value shown, losses included, and draws the zero line when the values cross it.

decisions.label: Legend
decisions.text: The legend names each series with its total. Pressing one shows it alone and fits the axis to it; pressing it again shows all. `tooltipTotal` adds a sum under the series in the tooltip, hidden while one series stands alone.

Partial and highlight. `partial` says the last point is a period still going: its segment is dashed, and its label and tooltip say so. `highlight` puts a dot on each series at one point, the month the card's headline talks about.

decisions.label: Drawing
decisions.text: The SVG stretches in one viewBox and keeps its stroke widths. Every word is HTML over it, and the width changes only how many time-axis labels show, so what the server renders is what the browser keeps. A label that would still run into the next one or out of the plot is left out; the newest always stays. It takes the whole width of its host, even in a centering row.

decisions.label: Points
decisions.text: Each point is a row of the hidden table and a word of the axis. Measured in Chromium (production build, two series): 500 points draw about 2,600 elements and a pointer move reaches the screen within a frame; 1,000 take about 20 ms, 2,000 about 50 ms and 10,000 over half a second. Past 500, group the days into weeks or months; in development the chart warns once.

In a card. In a UiChartCard it draws its own shape pale on the card's first load, and holds that shape still when there is nothing to draw. Alone, with no point or no value that is a number, it says "No data for this period" in its own place. When the card bleeds it to the sides, it keeps its words on the gutter, drops the value axis and draws the focus ring inside; on the card's floor it keeps the gutter under its legend.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a UiChartCard's body, under the card's headline, with a UiDelta in the card's actions. Alone it fills its host, a page section or a panel.

doc.keyboard:
The plot is one tab stop; an empty chart is no tab stop.
On the plot:
- `Tab`: reaches it; focus shows the newest point, or the one last visited.
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: step from point to point; each point is read out.
- `Home` `End`: jump to the first and the last point; each point is read out.
- `Alt` `Ctrl` `Meta`: a chord with them stays the browser's.
On the legend, whose chips are buttons when there are two series or more:
- `Tab`: reaches each chip.
- `Enter` `Space`: shows that series alone; a second press shows all.
A finger scrolls the page over the plot, and a tap keeps its point until a tap elsewhere.
doc.reader:
- Plot: an image named by `ariaLabel`.
- Point: only a point reached by the keyboard is read, in a polite live region, as "September 2026: Spending 3,640, Income 5,100", followed by the sum of `tooltipTotal`.
- Table: a hidden table, captioned with the chart's name, holds every point, every series and the sum, including a series shown alone; `partial` says "in progress" with the last point.
- Legend: a group named "Series; press one to show it alone", each chip `aria-pressed`.
- Hidden: the tooltip, the dots, the labels and the axis.
- Empty: alone, a group named by `ariaLabel` that says there is no data.
doc.states: Rest, a point under the pointer or the keys (the line, the dots and the tooltip), one series alone, `partial` with its dashed tail, `highlight` dots until the cursor takes over, a `muted` series behind the rest, a gap and a lone point with its dot, a loss with the zero line, nothing to draw alone. In a UiChartCard: its first load as a pale line, nothing to draw held still, a refresh dimmed by the card, bled to the sides without a value axis.
doc.notFor:
- Amounts per period: UiBarChart.
- The parts of a whole: UiDonutChart.
- A trend with no axes beside a number: UiSparkline.
- The card with its title, headline and data states: UiChartCard around it.

props.name: ratio
props.doc: Width divided by height, finite and above zero. Examples: `16 / 9`, `1`, `4 / 3`.

props.name: fit
props.doc: How media meets the box: `cover` crops it to fill, `contain` shows it whole.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The media. A lone child fills the box; beside an overlay, an image, a picture, a video, an iframe, a canvas or a link still fills it.

UiAspectRatio.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A box of fixed proportions for a photo, a video or an iframe. Take it wherever media must not move the page as it loads.

decisions.label: Fit
decisions.text: `fit` crops the media to fill the box (`cover`) or shows it whole (`contain`).

decisions.label: Your part
decisions.text: You write the `alt`, paint the background shown while loading and in the bands of `contain`, and place any overlay with `absolute`; a badge, a link or an image placed that way keeps its own size.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It stands alone in a grid of media, or in the `#image` of a framed UiCard. The card squares the image's corners, clips it, and draws the ring itself for a focused linked image. Beside the card's body it fills the column, and `ratio` does not apply. Anywhere else the box rounds its own corners, and the link's focus halo shows round it.

doc.keyboard:
Not interactive: the box takes no focus.
- `Tab`: reaches a link in the slot, which keeps its own tab stop. While that link is focused, the box lets the halo show outside it, and the link clips the image instead.
doc.reader: - Media: nothing of its own; a screen reader hears the media, so the `alt` you write on the image is all there is.
doc.states: `cover` crops the media; `contain` shows it whole between bands of your background, which also shows while the media loads. A linked image dims a little on hover and rings on focus. A ratio that is not a finite number above zero falls back to 16 / 9 and warns in dev.
doc.notFor:
- An avatar: UiAvatar.
- A block holding the page's shape while loading: UiSkeleton.
- A chart: UiChartCard.

props.name: name
props.doc: Whose it is; the initials come from its first two words ("Anna Petrova" is "AP").

props.name: src
props.doc: A photo; when it is missing or fails to load, the initials stand in.

props.name: alt
props.doc: Alone, what it shows ("Anna Petrova"); beside the name leave it empty: it is decoration.

props.name: size
props.doc: `xs` 24, `sm` 32, `md` 40: beside a dense row, a row, a page row.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The plate behind the initials.

UiAvatar.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A round mark for a person or a thing, with a photo or initials. Take it beside a name: in a card header, a table cell or a UiListItem's `#media`.

decisions.label: Look
decisions.text: The photo from `src` lies over the initials of `name`, on a pale plate in the tone. While the photo loads, and when it fails, the initials show at the same size. With no name and no photo it shows a person glyph.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In the `#media` of a UiListItem, beside a name in a card header, in a table cell, and as the `xs` actor node of a UiLog beside the log line.

decisions.label: Mark
decisions.text: A UiIndicator with `round` marks it: `sm` on the `xs` and `sm` sizes, `md` on `md`.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: no tab stop, no keys.
doc.reader:
- Beside a name: hidden (`aria-hidden`); the name beside it is what is read.
- Alone: with `alt` or a caller's `aria-label`, an image (`role="img"`) with that name.
- Photo and glyph: the photo has an empty `alt` and the person glyph is hidden, so nothing is read twice.
doc.states: Initials on the plate, a photo over them, a photo loading or failed (the initials show at the same size), no name and no photo (a person glyph); three sizes and the tones, with a UiIndicator mark. No hover or focus state of its own.
doc.notFor:
- A state mark on it: UiIndicator `round`.
- A state word: UiBadge.
- A count: UiCount.
- A glyph that acts: UiIconButton.

props.name: label
props.doc: Text of the label; the default slot overrides it.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Meaning: a verdict, `brand` for the product's own marks, or `neutral` for a category.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Form: `soft` pale pill, `inline` dot with text, `outline` pale plate with a border.

props.name: dot
props.doc: Indicator dot before the text; `inline` always has one. The text still names it: a dot alone is color.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Work in progress: a spinner stands where the dot or the icon would.

props.name: size
props.doc: Scale: `sm` for dense tables and long lists, `md` beside a title.

props.name: removable
props.doc: Close button: an applied filter, an added tag.

props.name: removeLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the close button; the default names the label.

events.name: remove
events.doc: The close button of a `removable` badge was pressed: once per double click; the host removes the badge and moves focus. Carries the click (`detail` tells a double click's second from a key's).

slots.name: default
slots.doc: Label text instead of the `label` prop.

slots.name: icon
slots.doc: Glyph before the text.

UiBadge.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A short word for a state or a tag. Take it for a status in a row, a tag you picked or a state in a card's head, in one of three forms; a number is UiCount.

decisions.label: Forms
decisions.text: `tone` is the meaning and `variant` the form: `soft` is a pale pill, `inline` a dot with text for a table row, `outline` a pale plate with a border. `size` `sm` makes every form compact.

decisions.label: Loading
decisions.text: `loading` puts a spinner where the dot or the icon stands and sets `aria-busy` on the root, and the text says what is happening ("Syncing"). The spinner is 14px with a heavier stroke, since at 12px the ring breaks into pixels. It is seen, not heard: a host that must announce it puts the words in its own live region.

decisions.label: Remove
decisions.text: `removable` adds a close button in the plate's own ink and corner, the one interactive part, with a 24px touch target. A double click fires it only once, and it works again after 500 ms (for example, after a canceled confirm), but not while a `loading` the host set from the click is running. The badge unmounts on remove, so the host moves the focus.

decisions.label: Long labels
decisions.text: A long label is cut the way UiTruncate cuts it, with the whole text in a tooltip; a slot handles its own cut. The text is its name: a badge without text is a bare color.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits in a table's status column, in UiLog's changed value, as UiSelect's picked tags, under UiDelta, and in the `#actions` of UiCard, the `#actions` of UiListItem and a drawer's `#status`. The root is a `<span>`.

doc.keyboard:
Not interactive: the badge takes no focus. `removable` adds the one tab stop, the cross, a native button:
- `Tab`: reaches the cross.
- `Enter` `Space`: press the cross.
It fires `remove` once per double click, and the host moves the focus, since the badge unmounts.
doc.reader:
- Name: the text; the dot, the icon and the spinner are hidden.
- Loading: says busy (`aria-busy`), and the text says what is happening.
- Cross: named "Remove" with the label: the words on screen when the slot gives them, or `removeLabel`.
- Cut label: keeps the whole text in a tooltip.
- No text: a badge without text is a bare color and warns in dev.
doc.states: Six tones in three forms, `soft`, `inline` and `outline`, at `sm` and `md`; `dot` before the text; `loading`, the spinner where the dot or the icon stands; `removable`, the cross, with its hover plate only when enabled; a long label cut with an ellipsis.
doc.notFor:
- A number: UiCount.
- A change against the value before: UiDelta.
- A mark on the corner of an icon or an avatar: UiIndicator.
- A notice with words and an action: UiListItem in a `tone`.

props.name: x
props.doc: The periods: one date each, `2026-09` a month, `2026-09-24` a day; text that is not a date stays as it is.

props.name: series
props.doc: The series, in the order they take the chart colors, five at most; each is `key`, `label` and `values`.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: What the chart shows, for a screen reader: "Revenue by month".

props.name: grain
props.doc: What one period stands for: the labels and the tooltip read the dates by it; `weekday` names a day of one week, "Tue".

props.name: format
props.doc: How values read in the legend, the tooltip and the table; `money` writes the currency code after the digits, `1,234.00 USD`. The axis prints compact figures without the unit.

props.name: height
props.doc: The height in pixels, the time axis included; the legend is below it.

props.name: yAxis
props.doc: The value axis with its grid; off for a chart that only shows a shape.

props.name: legend
props.doc: The legend with each series' total, a press shows one series alone.

props.name: highlight
props.doc: The period in light, or several (the months that met a plan); the others go quiet.

props.name: stack
props.doc: The series stand one on another, the parts of a whole; without it they stand side by side.

props.name: labels
props.doc: `value` prints the value over each period: the bar's, a stack's sum, or the tallest of bars side by side.

props.name: marks
props.doc: Lines of reference across the plot, each at a value with a label: `[{ at: 1100, label: 'Plan' }]`.

props.name: tooltipTotal
props.doc: A sum of some series under them in the tooltip and the table: `{ label: 'Revenue', of: ['orders', 'events'] }`.

props.name: partial
props.doc: The newest period with data is still going: its bar is hatched, its tooltip and table say so, and the empty periods after it are to come.

UiBarChart.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: Values by period as bars. Take it for amounts per period rather than a flow over time, usually in the body of a UiChartCard.

decisions.label: Data
decisions.text: `x` is the periods: dates that the library labels by `grain`, with the year on the first label shown and where it changes. Names that are not dates are categories: each keeps its label, cut to its band, and the tooltip says it whole. Each series is its `values` in that order. One series draws one bar per period; several stand side by side, or on top of each other with `stack` (the parts of a whole).

decisions.label: Values
decisions.text: A `null` is no data yet: its place keeps a thin gray stub, never a zero bar. A zero keeps a sliver of its color on the zero line. A loss stands below the zero line. In a stack only values at zero or above are drawn and counted, so the stack's label, the legend total and the tooltip sum agree with the bars; a period of zeros is a sliver whose sum is 0.

decisions.label: Emphasis
decisions.text: `highlight` lights one period or several and quiets the rest to a pale bar with a line at its height. `marks` draws a reference line (a plan), named under the chart. `labels="value"` prints the value over each period, thinned the same way as the axis labels.

decisions.label: Legend
decisions.text: The legend names each series with its total; a press shows one series alone. `tooltipTotal` adds a sum under the series in the tooltip.

decisions.label: In progress
decisions.text: `partial` says the newest period with data is still going: its bar is hatched and read as in progress, and the empty periods after it are dashed outlines, meaning still to come, not missing.

decisions.label: Drawing
decisions.text: Bars are HTML boxes in bands, so their corners stay round at any width; the width changes only how many time-axis labels show. A label that would still run into the next one or out of the plot is left out; the newest always stays.

decisions.label: Periods
decisions.text: Each period is a band, a bar per series and a row of the hidden table. Measured in Chromium (production build, two series): 500 periods draw about 7,000 elements and a pointer move reaches the screen within a frame or two; 1,000 take about 45 ms, 2,000 over 60 ms and 10,000 over half a second. Past 500, group the days into weeks or months; in development the chart warns once.

In a card. In a UiChartCard's body, under the headline, with a UiDelta in the card's actions; or alone in its host. In the card it draws pale bars on the first load and holds them still when there is nothing to draw. Alone, with no period or no value that is a number, it says "No data for this period" in its own place. When the card bleeds it, it keeps its words on the gutter, drops the value axis and draws the focus ring inside.

doc.keyboard:
The plot is one tab stop; an empty chart is no tab stop.
On the plot:
- `Tab`: reaches it; focus shows the newest period, or the one last visited.
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: step from period to period; each period is read out.
- `Home` `End`: jump to the first and the last period; each period is read out.
- `Alt` `Ctrl` `Meta`: a chord with them stays the browser's.
On the legend, whose chips are buttons when there are two series or more:
- `Tab`: reaches each chip.
- `Enter` `Space`: shows that series alone; a second press shows all.
A finger scrolls the page over the plot, and a tap keeps its period until a tap elsewhere.
doc.reader:
- Plot: an image named by `ariaLabel`.
- Period: only a period reached by the keyboard is read, in a polite live region, as "September 2026: Orders 1,240, Events 380", followed by the sum of `tooltipTotal`, and "in progress" for the period still going.
- Table: a hidden table holds every period and every series, including a series shown alone; its caption is the chart's name and each mark ("Plan 1,100").
- Legend: a group named "Series; press one to show it alone", each chip `aria-pressed`.
- Hidden: the bars, the values over them, the tooltip and the marks' names.
- Empty: alone, a group named by `ariaLabel` that says there is no data.
doc.states: Rest, a period under the pointer or the keys (the tooltip), one series alone, side by side and `stack`, a loss below the zero line, a zero as a sliver and a `null` as a gray stub, `highlight` with the rest quiet, `marks` named under the chart, `labels="value"`, `partial` with its hatched bar and the dashed periods to come, nothing to draw alone. In a UiChartCard: its first load as pale bars, nothing to draw held still, a refresh dimmed by the card, bled to the sides without a value axis.
doc.notFor:
- A flow over time: UiAreaChart.
- The parts of a whole at one moment: UiDonutChart.
- A trend with no axes beside a number: UiSparkline `bar`.
- The card with its title, headline and data states: UiChartCard around it.

props.name: type
props.doc: Native type; `submit` sends the form the button sits in. A link has none.

props.name: to
props.doc: A route or a URL: the button becomes a link. An absolute address opens in a new tab; `javascript:` and `data:` are refused, and it stays a button.

props.name: target
props.doc: With `to`: `_blank` or `_self` decides the tab; unset, a new tab for an absolute address only.

props.name: rel
props.doc: With `to`: replaces the default `noreferrer` (`nofollow`, `sponsored`); `noopener` stays on a new tab.

props.name: loading
props.doc: A request is running: spinner, `aria-busy`, no clicks; it wins over `disabled`.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Natively disabled: a flat plate, out of the Tab order; with `disabledReason`, focusable and saying why. A link turns back into a button.

props.name: disabledReason
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, while `disabled`: it stays in the Tab order, refuses the press, and says the reason in a tooltip on hover, focus, a press and a tap, and as its description to a screen reader. A blank one is none.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Weight of the presentation: brand fill, gray plate, white with a border, or quiet.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Meaning of the action; `brand` means none in particular. Every variant supports every tone.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder: `xs` 28px for a micro action, `sm` 36px, `md` 44px for forms. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

props.name: block
props.doc: Full width, as in a drawer footer.

props.name: loadingText
props.doc: Label while loading; the default is a translated "In progress…". Empty, the spinner stands alone (a glyph button).

props.name: pressed
props.doc: A toggle: `aria-pressed`, and on, a check and the brand frame. Unset, it is no toggle. A primary button is never one.

slots.name: loading
slots.doc: Replaces the label while loading.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The label; a glyph goes here too, before the text. The button sizes it.

UiButton.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A button for an action, with loading and toggle states. With `to` it renders a link styled as a button.

decisions.label: Look
decisions.text: `variant` is the weight of the presentation, `tone` is the meaning.

decisions.label: Loading
decisions.text: `loading` shows a spinner in place of the label and refuses a second click, including one meant for your own handler. The width holds, also with the text of the `#loading` slot; an empty `loadingText` leaves the spinner alone.

decisions.label: Toggle
decisions.text: `pressed` makes it a toggle: `aria-pressed`, a check before the label, and the brand frame. It is for a chip that turns on and off by itself, as a filter (Unpaid, Overdue, Mine); one choice among a few is UiRadioGroup `segmented`. Off, it holds the room of its check, so pressing it moves nothing beside it.

decisions.label: Disabled
decisions.text: `disabled` alone is the native state: a flat plate, out of the Tab order, and silent, so a person cannot learn why it does not press. With `disabledReason` it keeps the same plate but stays in the Tab order, refuses the press (a submit too, and a menu it would open, by the arrows as well), and says why: in a tooltip on hover, keyboard focus, a press and a tap, and as its description to a screen reader ("Add the client's email first"). The tooltip stands inside the button, loaded the first time it is off with a reason, so the button stays its one element: a reason that comes or goes under the focus keeps it, and a ref or a UiTooltip around it still reaches the button; while it is off, the reason shows in place of that UiTooltip's words. With `to`, the link turns into a button when disabled, a new element, so the focus does not stay.

decisions.label: Links
decisions.text: With `to` it renders a RouteLink that looks like a button. Another site, or `target="_blank"`, opens in a new tab and says so: an arrow for the eye, a phrase for a screen reader. A `javascript:` or `data:` address is refused: it stays a button, and dev warns.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits in the footers of a drawer and a confirm, in toolbars beside a search, and in the triggers of filters, periods and columns. One `primary` to a surface, last in its footer: it is the step the surface is for. UiCopyButton is built on it, and UiButtonGroup joins it with its neighbors into one capsule.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Anything else passed to it lands on the root element: native button and form attributes, `aria-*`, `data-testid`.

doc.keyboard:
- `Tab`: reaches it.
- `Enter` `Space`: press it; not while `loading`, nor while disabled with a reason, which the focus still reaches. A held Enter is one press: its repeats press nothing.
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`: as a menu's trigger, open it; not while it refuses the press.
With `to`, a link:
- `Enter`: follows it; `Space` does not, as in the browser.
doc.reader:
- Name: the label; a lone glyph is UiIconButton, which carries its own name.
- Loading: says busy (`aria-busy`); the label is hidden from the reader and the loading text becomes the name: "In progress…" by default, `loadingText` or the `#loading` slot. The spinner is hidden. With an empty `loadingText` the label stays the name, unseen but still read, so the button is never nameless.
- Pressed: `pressed` is `aria-pressed`.
- Disabled with a reason: `aria-disabled`, and the reason is its description, read once.
- New tab: said in words after the label, where the eye sees an arrow.
doc.states: Rest, hover on a device that hovers, focus, disabled, disabled with a reason (the plate, the focus, the hint), loading and pressed, in both themes. A loading button keeps its width, so nothing beside it moves.
doc.notFor:
- Text inside prose: UiLink.
- A lone glyph: UiIconButton.
- A choice among options: UiRadioGroup `segmented`.
- Buttons joined into one capsule: UiButtonGroup around them.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Name of the group for a screen reader: "Pagination", "Period". Inside `UiField group` the legend names it.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Controls in a row or in a column.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: Bordered controls of one size, a nested group, a `UiSeparator`.

UiButtonGroup.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: Bordered controls of one size joined into one capsule (`outline`, never `ghost`). Take it for a few related actions side by side in a toolbar, or to join a search with its button.

decisions.label: Nesting
decisions.text: A nested group is spaced, not joined. A `UiSeparator` between nested groups draws a line across the row; between two joined buttons, their shared border is the line.

decisions.label: Filled buttons
decisions.text: Filled buttons (`primary`, `secondary`) have no border to share, so two of them side by side are split by a 1px seam instead.

decisions.label: Split button
decisions.text: A split button is a primary UiButton next to a primary UiIconButton with a chevron that opens a UiMenu, as in a UiCrudDrawer's footer; an `outline` button and an `outline` arrow make the quieter one. In a row, a UiIconButton last and right after a button with text is that arrow, and the group draws it narrower than a square: a part of the button beside it, not a button of its own.

decisions.label: Children
decisions.text: A child in error is lifted over its neighbors, so its red frame shows whole. Children must be direct: a button inside a wrapper cannot be joined. The size is each child's, or the app's step for all of them, so give one `size` to every child or to none. `orientation` makes the group vertical.

doc.keyboard: None of its own: Tab walks its children one by one, each with its own keys, and the focused child is lifted over its neighbors, so its ring shows whole.
doc.reader:
- Group: a `group` named by `ariaLabel`.
- In a field group: inside a `UiField group`, the legend names it (`aria-labelledby`) and the field's text describes it (`aria-describedby`), with its own `ariaLabel` winning.
- In a plain field: inside a plain UiField, the input in the group is the control and the group takes nothing.
- Nested: a nested group keeps its own name.
- No name: a group with no name warns in dev.
doc.states: No state of its own; it shows its children's: a focused or hovered child lifted; a child in error lifted over its neighbors with its red frame whole; a disabled child beside a filled one, with a reason too, not lifted on hover; a link child joined as a button is. Horizontal or vertical (`orientation`), on every step of the size ladder, nested with a gap.
doc.notFor:
- One choice among a few: UiRadioGroup `segmented`.
- A lone action: UiButton.
- The search and the filters over a list: UiTableToolbar.

props.name: min
props.doc: The first day that can be picked, inclusive.

props.name: max
props.doc: The last day that can be picked, inclusive.

props.name: marked
props.doc: Days with a dot under the number: a day, or `{ day, tone }` for a colored dot; a day listed twice has two dots, two at most. `grani.calendar.marked` says what they mean (the app's `translate` words it).

props.name: unavailable
props.doc: Days that cannot be picked though they fall within `min` and `max` (booked, closed): struck through.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: A name for the whole calendar where two stand on one page ("Check-in"); the grid keeps the month as its name.

props.name: range
props.doc: Pick a span of days, two presses in either order, instead of one day.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The chosen day as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or with `range` the span `{ from, to }` (`v-model`); `null` for none and for an open end.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: A day was picked, or with `range` a whole span: a half-made span is not sent.

UiCalendar.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A month to pick a day from. Take it on a page of its own, or inside a picker's popover.

decisions.label: Value
decisions.text: The value is an ISO day (`2026-09-24`): a day, not a moment.

decisions.label: Today
decisions.text: Today is marked on the client only, because the server's today may be another day.

decisions.label: Weekend
decisions.text: The names of the days of rest in the header are bold, as the locale counts them: Saturday and Sunday in most places, Friday and Saturday in Israel or Saudi Arabia. A due day put on a day off is seen by its column, and the days themselves stay as they are, so nothing competes with the chosen day, today, a span or the marks.

decisions.label: Window
decisions.text: Days outside `min` and `max` cannot be picked, and the arrows stop at them. When the calendar opens on a month outside them, the arrows can always walk back into the window.

decisions.label: Marks
decisions.text: Taken days (`unavailable`) are struck through, and `marked` days carry a dot; a screen reader hears both in words.

decisions.label: Range
decisions.text: With `range` the value is a span, `{ from, to }`, and the calendar picks it: the first day pressed starts a span, the second ends it, in either order, and only then is the span sent. A half-made span is the calendar's own: a span set from outside drops it. TypeScript checks the value against `range` written as it is (`range` or none), so a calendar whose `range` changes at run time is two tags, one under `v-if` and one under `v-else`: `:range="flag"` does not compile.

decisions.label: Preview
decisions.text: Before the second press the band runs from the first day to the day under the pointer, or to the day with the keyboard focus, and the line under the month counts its days ("7 days"), so a week that came out eight days long is seen before it is set. Only a day the second press can pick ends it, and nothing is sent until that press. A taken day (`unavailable`) stops a span: while it waits, the days past the nearest taken day on either side cannot end it and show disabled, so a booking never takes in a day already booked. The line says the next step while no span is drawn and the length of a picked span after; it is always there, so the month does not move.

decisions.label: Size
decisions.text: It has one step, `sm`, whatever the app's step: the day cells are 36 px and the header matches them.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In the popover of UiDatePicker, as the second step of UiDateRange's popover, or on a page of its own, beside what the host puts under it (a value, quick picks, a time).

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: No day is `null`; in a span, an open end is `null`.

doc.keyboard:
The keys follow the WAI-ARIA date grid. One day is the tab stop.
In the days:
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: move a day toward that side. On a right-to-left page the week runs from the right, so `ArrowRight` moves to the day before.
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown`: move a week.
- `Home` `End`: go to the ends of the week.
- `PageUp` `PageDown`: move a month.
- `Shift+PageUp` `Shift+PageDown`: move a year.
- `Enter` `Space`: pick the day in focus.
- `Escape`: belongs to the host.
- `Alt` `Ctrl` `Meta`: a chord with them stays the browser's, in the days and in the months.
A move that starts inside the window stops at its edge.
The caption opens the months of the year, to jump far. There:
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight` `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown`: walk the 3 × 4 grid. On a right-to-left page the grid runs from the right, so `ArrowRight` moves to the month before.
- `Home` `End`: go to its ends.
- `Escape`: goes back to the days.
The header arrows page by a month, or by a year in the months view; when an arrow turns off at the window's edge, the focus moves to the caption. On a right-to-left page the previous arrow stands at the right and points there.
doc.reader:
- Grid: named by the month shown, from a live caption, so a page turn is read out; with `range` it is `aria-multiselectable`.
- Day: a button named by its full date, then by what its dots mean and, when it is taken, by the word unavailable.
- Today: `aria-current="date"`.
- Weekend: a header cell is named by its day's full name; its weight is for the eye alone.
- Chosen day: `aria-selected` on its cell.
- Disabled day: a day that cannot be picked is `aria-disabled`.
- Month: a month button says its month and year; the month shown is `aria-current`.
- Range: with `range` a live region says "Choose the first day", then "Now choose the last day".
- Preview: while a span waits for its end, the focused day says after its date how long the span to it would be ("7 days"); the line under the month is hidden, since it says the same.
- Two calendars: when two stand on one page, `ariaLabel` names each whole calendar as a group; the grid keeps the month as its name.
doc.states: Empty (it opens on today, or on the window's nearest day), a chosen day, a span, a span drawn to the pointed or focused day before its second press with its length under the month, days outside `min` and `max` (disabled; a chosen day out there keeps a frame), taken days struck through, marked days with one or two dots, today in the brand ink, the names of the days of rest in bold, and the months view. The months view is as tall as the days, so nothing jumps when you switch.
doc.notFor:
- A day in a form field: UiDatePicker, which wraps this.
- A period in a toolbar: UiDateRange.
- A time of day: UiTimePicker beside it.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading of the card; its level follows the nesting: `h2` on a page, `h3` in a card, and so on.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title that says what the card holds.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `outline` is the framed surface; `plain` has no frame, no fill, no padding of its own: the three parts alone, on the gutter around it.

props.name: size
props.doc: The gutter: `sm` is `--space-surface` (16, the default), `md` is `--space-surface-md` (24). Rows, separators and lists inside line up on it.

props.name: divided
props.doc: The line under the header; on by default for a framed card, off for a section of an overlay (the overlay draws the lines between sections). `false` lets the body follow the title directly.

props.name: padded
props.doc: The body's padding; `false` runs it edge to edge, for rows, a table or an image. Rows keep their text on the gutter.

props.name: align
props.doc: `center` stands the body's content in the middle, with room around it: a 404; `empty` puts `#empty` there.

props.name: imagePosition
props.doc: Where `#image` stands: above the header, below the footer, or beside the card at the `start` or the `end`.

props.name: footerVariant
props.doc: `muted` fills the footer; `plain` keeps it on the surface. The line above it stays either way.

props.name: footerPadded
props.doc: The footer's padding; `false` runs its children edge to edge, sharing the width: split buttons, tabs.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Meaning of the frame: `danger` for a card in trouble (a failed connection), `warning` for one that needs a look. The words say it too: a badge in `#actions`.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The card cannot be used now: its words go muted and it is a disabled group named by its title. Controls inside are the caller's to disable.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The body is on its way. With nothing in the body yet (the first load) a skeleton stands in its place; over content (a refresh) the content stays, dimmed to 60% with the title, under one spinner in the card's middle; `#actions`, a whole `#header` and `#footer` keep their color and still work. `aria-busy` either way. Bind it (`false` too) where the card loads, so its live region is there before the words. A body with a shape of its own (a table, a chart) draws its own skeleton.

props.name: empty
props.doc: There is nothing to show: `#empty` stands in the body's place, in the middle. A first load's skeleton wins over it; a later load leaves it as it is: give its Retry `loading`.

slots.name: header
slots.doc: The whole header in place of the title line: a tab strip, a toolbar. It runs edge to edge.

slots.name: media
slots.doc: Before the title: a glyph plate, an avatar. Glyphs are 20px.

slots.name: actions
slots.doc: At the end of the header, on the center of the title and its line: a button, a badge, a switch, a UiMenu.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The body of the card.

slots.name: empty
slots.doc: In the body's place while `empty`: a UiNoData, which drops its own frame in a card.

slots.name: image
slots.doc: Media edge to edge at `imagePosition`: an image in a UiAspectRatio, a gradient.

slots.name: footer
slots.doc: Under a line: the actions stand at the end; a note or a total takes `me-auto`.

slots.name: divider
slots.doc: In place of the line above the footer, edge to edge: a UiProgress `h-1`, whose track is the line's color.

UiCard.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A surface with an optional header, body and footer, each filled by you. Take it to group related content on a page.

decisions.label: Header
decisions.text: The header is a title with a description, with `#media` before it and `#actions` beside it (centered on the title and its line), or a whole `#header` (a tab strip, a toolbar) running edge to edge. A line stands under the header by default; `:divided="false"` drops it. A body that opens with a UiHeader legend gets no line, since the legend is the line.

decisions.label: Body
decisions.text: The body is padded, or runs edge to edge without `padded` (rows, a table, an image). `align="center"` puts its content in the middle (a 404), and `empty` puts `#empty` there.

decisions.label: Image
decisions.text: `#image` puts media at the `top`, `bottom`, `start` or `end`, edge to edge. A side image stands above or below the body when the card is under 384px wide, at the media's own height; a card with a side image takes its parent's width.

decisions.label: Footer
decisions.text: The footer stands under a line, with its actions at the end, plain or `muted`. A full-width action alone in it (`block`) stands on the body's gutter, lined up with the fields above. `#divider` takes the place of that line (a progress bar). Without `footerPadded`, the footer's children run edge to edge and share the width (split buttons, tabs).

decisions.label: Gutter
decisions.text: The card passes its gutter (16, or 24 at `md`) to what is inside, so a UiList of rows or a separator lines up with the title. A body that ends in a UiList drops its bottom gutter, so the last row stands on its own inset as the rows above it do. A section of a drawer runs a UiList that is its first or last child to its line.

decisions.label: Plain
decisions.text: `variant="plain"` drops the frame: the three parts alone, 16 apart, with no line under the header unless `divided`. The footer keeps its own line.

decisions.label: Overlays
decisions.text: In the body of a drawer or a popover, a card is a flat section (no frame, no padding), with a UiSeparator the overlay places between sections. A window frames its cards.

decisions.label: Title
decisions.text: The title is the card's one heading, and its level follows the nesting. A long word in the title breaks inside its column, beside the action.

decisions.label: Hosts
decisions.text: UiChartCard, UiDataTable and UiListField are built on it; UiFilter and UiCrudDrawer take cards as their sections.

decisions.label: Status
decisions.text: `tone` colors the frame of a card in trouble, and a badge in `#actions` says it in words; a toned card with neither `#actions` nor `#header` warns in development. `disabled` mutes the words and makes the card a disabled group. `loading` and `empty` stand in for the body.

doc.keyboard:
Not interactive: the frame takes no focus.
- `Tab`: reaches the controls you put in `#actions`, `#header`, the body and `#footer`, which keep their own tab stops, in the order they stand.
A tab in a whole `#header` and a button in an edge-to-edge footer ring inward, inside the frame.
A focused linked image in `#image` rings the card, not itself. While the card loads, `#empty` stays, so a focus on its Retry stays too; when the content takes its place, the focus goes to the card, never to the page.
doc.reader:
- Title: a heading whose level follows the nesting: `h2` on a page, `h3` in a card; the description follows it.
- Loading: `loading` marks the card `aria-busy`, and a live region says it is loading, or updating when there is content. Bind `loading` where the card loads, so the region is in place before the words.
- Disabled: `disabled` makes the card a group named by its title, `aria-disabled`.
- Whole header: a whole `#header` replaces the title and names nothing inside.
- Tone: `tone` colors the frame only: the words are a badge in `#actions`.
doc.states: Rest; `loading` on a first load, a skeleton of three lines; `loading` over content, the content kept and not mounted again, dimmed to 60% with the title, the card's own controls not, and one spinner in the card's middle; `empty`, with `#empty` in the middle (a first load's skeleton wins over it, a later load leaves it as it is); `disabled`, muted words on a muted surface; `tone` `danger` or `warning` on the frame; `plain`, no frame; a flat section inside an overlay. A side image stands above the body when the card is under 384px wide.
doc.notFor:
- A list screen with a toolbar and pages: UiDataTable.
- A chart with its figure: UiChartCard.
- One row of text with a thing at its end: UiListItem.
- A choice among cards: UiRadioGroup `card`.
- A notice with an action: UiListItem in a `tone`.

props.name: title
props.doc: What the chart shows: "Spending and income by month".

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title: what is counted, what is left out.

props.name: size
props.doc: The gutter, as UiCard's: `sm` 16, `md` 24.

props.name: value
props.doc: A headline over the chart, a total: a number in `format`, or text already written. `null` keeps its line while it loads, and blank while there is nothing to draw.

props.name: caption
props.doc: A line under the headline: the shares, the span it covers. `null` keeps its line as `value` does.

props.name: format
props.doc: How a number `value` reads, `money` with the currency code after the digits; the chart inside takes its own.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Data is on its way: a skeleton while there is none yet, the chart dimmed over data already shown.

props.name: empty
props.doc: There is no data to draw: with `loading` it is the first load, without it `#empty`.

props.name: bleed
props.doc: The chart runs to the card's `sides`, its words on the gutter, or to the floor as well (`full`, with no footer); for a chart without a value axis.

props.name: error
props.doc: Why the data did not load, in words for the reader, shown with Retry; an empty string fails with a general reason. Over a chart already shown: "Not updated" on the title line.

events.name: retry
events.doc: Retry was pressed after a failed load or refresh.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The chart. It reads the card's first load and draws its own skeleton; anything else here is shown as it is.

slots.name: actions
slots.doc: On the title line, at the end: a link to the details, a UiMenu.

slots.name: footer
slots.doc: A note under the chart: an average, the span it covers. Bare text is a note at the start, in a note's size and color; markup lays itself out, a `me-auto` note before its actions at the end.

slots.name: empty
slots.doc: In the chart's place when there is nothing to draw: a UiNoData that says why, with the next step in its `#actions`. It may be taller than the chart; the card grows to it.

UiChartCard.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A card around a chart that handles its data states, so the chart only draws. Take it for a chart on a page, alone or in a grid of cards.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.text: A title with its description, with `#actions` on the same line (a link, a UiDelta); an optional headline (`value` in the chart's format, with a `caption` under it); the chart in the body; a note in `#footer`. There is no line under the title: the headline and the chart follow it on one surface.

decisions.label: Data states
decisions.text: One `loading` and one `empty` tell the states apart, as in a table. A figure beside the chart follows its data: a UiDelta in `#actions` draws nothing on a first load, with nothing to draw and after a failed load, and a note given as bare text in `#footer` becomes a held line of its own height; a control, a link and a footer of markup stay. A refresh keeps everything, and a failed refresh keeps it beside "Not updated".

decisions.label: First load
decisions.text: Skeletons take the place of the headline and the note. The chart in the slot reads `CHART_SKELETON` and draws its own skeleton; for a chart that has none, the card draws a band of bars. A refresh keeps the chart, dimmed to 60%, with a spinner in the middle of the card.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: Nothing to draw keeps the chart's place: the chart reads `CHART_EMPTY` and holds its first-load shape, unseen. `#empty` (a UiNoData that says why and what to do next, or the card's own words) stands in the same cell, and the taller of the two sets the height. A slot whose content is switched off by `v-if` counts as no slot.

decisions.label: Errors
decisions.text: A failed load holds the place the same way, with UiNoData `danger`, the reason and Retry in the cell. A failed refresh keeps the chart and says "Not updated" on the title line, with Retry as a reload glyph; the reason is in its tooltip and in the one live region of the title line. Retry asks for nothing while `loading`.

decisions.label: Bleed
decisions.text: `bleed="sides"` runs the chart to the card's sides and hands it the gutter through `CHART_BLEED`, so the chart keeps its legend and axis ends on the gutter. `bleed="full"` takes the bottom edge too when there is no footer. A bled chart has no value axis.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: On UiCard, beside other cards in a page's grid, with UiDelta in `#actions`. A single figure with a trend is this card with `bleed="full"`. Rows with small lines are UiListItem rows in its body.

doc.keyboard:
The card takes no tab stop of its own.
- `Tab`: walks what is in it: the controls in `#actions`, the Retry glyph of a failed refresh, the chart's plot and legend, the Retry of a failed load.
- `Enter` `Space`: press a Retry.
When a Retry disappears under the focus, the focus goes to the Retry that took its place, or to the card, never to the page. A focus on a chart control stays where it is when the error clears.
doc.reader:
- Status: one status region on the title line, present in every state, says "Loading the chart…" on the first load, "Updating…" on a refresh, and "Could not refresh chart data" with the reason after a failed refresh.
- Retry: the glyph of a failed refresh is a button named "Retry" with the reason in its tooltip.
- Failed load: UiNoData `danger`, "The chart did not load", the reason and Retry.
- Empty: nothing to draw is "No data for this period", or the caller's `#empty`.
- Busy: while loading, the card is `aria-busy`; a chart held under the words is hidden and inert.
doc.states: Rest, the first load (a skeleton for the headline, the note and the chart's own), a refresh (the chart and the headline dimmed to 60%, a spinner in the middle), nothing to draw (`empty`, the chart's place kept), a failed load (`error` with `empty`), a failed refresh ("Not updated" on the title line, the chart kept); with and without a headline, a caption and a footer note, `bleed="sides"` and `bleed="full"`.
doc.notFor:
- A chart alone in a page section: the chart itself, UiAreaChart, UiBarChart or UiDonutChart.
- Rows with small lines: UiListItem rows in a UiList.
- A change against the period before: UiDelta in `#actions`.
- A table of the figures: UiTable.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: Whether the checkbox is checked (`v-model`).

props.name: indeterminate
props.doc: Shows a mixed state when some of the items it represents are checked. Display only.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name for forms.

props.name: value
props.doc: Native value submitted with the form when checked.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id when standalone. Inside UiField, the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents toggling.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control as invalid. Inside UiField, the error state sets this automatically.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when the slot is empty and there is no field label; slot text wins over it.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: the box must be checked, said to a reader and to a form (native `required`), with a star after its text. Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder: the box is 16, 18 or 20 px beside `text-sm`. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The checkbox was toggled.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: Label text displayed next to the checkbox. Clicking the label toggles the checkbox.

UiCheckbox.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A native checkbox with its text in the slot, for a yes or no in a form. The whole row is the label, so a click on the text toggles it too.

decisions.label: Mark
decisions.text: The box is drawn as the library's 18px mark. It stands at the first line (18px in a 20px line, 1px down), so a long label wraps beside it.

decisions.label: Model
decisions.text: The box shows the model: when the parent refuses a change, or a form resets, the box goes back to the model.

decisions.label: Mixed
decisions.text: `indeterminate` is the mixed state of a "select all" box. It is display only: a press ends it only when the parent says so.

decisions.label: Standalone
decisions.text: It takes `ariaLabel` (the slot text wins when both are given) and `invalid`. `invalid` draws a red border and sets `aria-invalid`; put the reason beside it, or use UiField. With no text of its own, as in a table's rows, the box takes a press in a 24px square around it.

decisions.label: Size
decisions.text: `size` is the step of the control ladder: the box is 16, 18 or 20 px, the text stays `text-sm` and the box stands at its first line.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Inside UiField it reads id, error and required from the field. When the field has a `label`, the slot text names the box and the field label heads the row.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes and listeners land on the input; `class` and `style` on the label.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: Beside UiSwitch and UiRadio in a form column. The first column of UiTable is this component, and the rows of a multiple UiSelect and of UiFilterList draw the same mark from `utils/checkMark`.

doc.keyboard:
A native checkbox.
- `Tab`: reaches it.
- `Space`: toggles it; `disabled` blocks it.
A press on a mixed box leaves it mixed unless the parent resolves it. When the parent refuses a press, the box goes back to the model.
doc.reader:
- Name: a checkbox named by the slot text, else by `ariaLabel`, else by the field's label: one name, never two. A box with no name warns in dev.
- State: checked, not checked, or, with `indeterminate`, mixed.
- Errors: `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`; inside UiField the description and the error are read with it.
- Required: inside UiField `aria-required` says it is required, except in a group, where the legend says it once.
doc.states: Unchecked, checked, mixed, hover (an empty box darkens), focus, disabled (a solid plate, not a fade), invalid (a red border, kept under the pointer), and required, with the star after its own text when no field label carries it.
doc.notFor:
- A setting applied at once: UiSwitch.
- One answer out of a few: UiRadioGroup.
- Several picks from a list in a panel: UiSelect `multiple`.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The entered code (`v-model`); empty is `''`.

props.name: length
props.doc: Number of characters in the code, a whole number from 1 to 100; anything else is held to that and warned about in development.

props.name: inputMode
props.doc: Keyboard shown on a phone. `numeric` for SMS, PIN, and authenticator codes. `text` for codes with letters.

props.name: pattern
props.doc: Allowed characters, tested one character at a time (not the whole code). A RegExp or its source. When omitted, `numeric` allows digits and `text` allows letters and digits.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents entering and editing the code.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control as invalid. Inside UiField, the error state sets this automatically.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: a value is needed, said to a reader and to a form (native `required`). Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name for forms.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id when standalone. Inside UiField, the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder for the cells.

props.name: separator
props.doc: Shows a short rule between the code groups.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The code changed.

events.name: complete
events.doc: The code reached its length.

UiCodeInput.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A field for a one-time code, drawn as one cell per character. Take it for a sign-in or confirm step.

decisions.label: One input
decisions.text: One real input lies invisible over the cells and holds the value. So the label, autofill of a code from SMS (`one-time-code`, which a caller's `autocomplete` replaces), paste and Backspace all work as the browser does them; the cells only draw the characters. The lit cell follows the real focus through `:focus-within`, and the hover is drawn from the root, since the input covers the cells.

decisions.label: Caret
decisions.text: The caret stays at the end: a click moves it there, and so does the next character after any key or touch that moved it. A selection (double click, drag, select all) is left alone, so the code can be copied.

decisions.label: Characters
decisions.text: `inputMode` picks the keyboard, `pattern` the allowed characters. A pasted text longer than the code is filtered first, then cut, so a code inside an SMS survives. A whole code pasted over characters already typed takes their place.

decisions.label: Size
decisions.text: Cells stand on the control ladder, `md` by default, because it is the one control on its screen.

decisions.label: Complete
decisions.text: `complete` fires once when typing, paste or autofill fill the code. A value set from outside is filtered and cut like a typed one but does not fire it, so a restored draft never submits itself.

decisions.label: Model
decisions.text: The input shows the model: when the parent refuses a change, or a form resets, it goes back to the model. The parent clears a wrong code to `''`, so the same code can be typed again.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Standalone it takes `invalid` (a red border and halo, and `aria-invalid`; put the reason beside it) and `ariaLabel`; inside UiField it reads id, error and required.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes and listeners land on the input, `class` and `style` on the root.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: Alone in a sign-in or confirm step, or in a UiField on a card or in a window, after the password.

doc.keyboard:
One real input over the cells: typing fills the next cell, and a paste or an autofill fills the code at once, dropping characters the pattern refuses.
- `Backspace`: removes the last character.
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight` `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown` `Home` `End`: do not move the caret, with `Ctrl` or `Meta` too.
- `Alt+ArrowLeft` `Alt+ArrowRight`: stay the browser's, a page back or forward; on a Mac, where they jump a word in a text box, the caret comes back to the end.
Nothing is emitted while an IME composes. `disabled` blocks the input, and `focus()` does nothing on it then.
doc.reader:
- Field: one text box named by `ariaLabel` or the field's label, with a hint read with it that says how many characters the code has. A code with no name warns in dev.
- Cells: hidden from a screen reader; the input holds the value.
- Errors: `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`; inside UiField the description and the error are read with it, and `aria-required` says it is required.
doc.states: Rest, focus (the cell for the next character lit, the last one on a full code), partly filled, full, hover (the border drawn from the root), disabled (muted, inert), invalid (red border and halo on the cells, `aria-invalid` on the input), and two halves with `separator`.
doc.notFor:
- A password: UiInput `type="password"`.
- A number or a text of any length: UiInput.
- A code shown to copy and never typed: UiCopyButton.

UiConfirm.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: The host of `useConfirm`, mounted once at the app root beside UiToaster. Take it to ask a yes-or-no question before an action.

decisions.label: Root
decisions.text: A question asked in an app without one is never shown and never answered, and dev says so once.

decisions.label: Window
decisions.text: It asks in a UiModal with `role="alertdialog"`. A press on the backdrop does not answer; Escape and the cross answer no. Asked from a window, it hides that window until it is answered; the window then comes back, with the focus on what asked.

decisions.label: Action
decisions.text: With an `action`, the window sends the request, waits for it, and closes into a toast. If the request fails, the toast's Retry asks the question again. A new question answers the open one `false`; an action already on its way then reports nothing. Remove a row inside `action`, so the Retry after a failure removes it too; a UiTable then takes the focus from the window to the same button of the row now in its place. Every way out is refused while the request runs, so one that never settles holds the window open: give the `action` a timeout of its own, which fails it into the error toast.

decisions.label: Leaving
decisions.text: A question is never left hanging. When the app has a router and the page changes, or when UiConfirm itself unmounts, the open question is answered no. A question whose action is already running is not cut off: the request's outcome answers it.

doc.keyboard:
The window's keys; the focus starts on the cancel button, and so does a new question asked in place of an open one.
- `Tab`: goes round the two buttons.
- `Enter` `Space`: press the one in focus.
- `Escape`: answers no; while the action is running, it is refused with a shake.
While the action is running, a second press on the confirm button sends nothing. On close the focus returns to what asked.
doc.reader:
- Window: an alert dialog (`role="alertdialog"`, `aria-modal`) named by `title` ("Are you sure?" when there is none) and described by `message`, the sentence in its body.
- Confirm button: while the action runs, says busy (`aria-busy`) under its spinner.
- Outcome: a failure is announced at once as an error toast with Retry; a success is announced only with `success`.
doc.states: Asked, with Cancel and Confirm; `tone="danger"`, with a red confirm button; busy, with the confirm button loading and every close refused; answered, closed with nothing more, or with a success toast when `success` is set; failed, closed into an error toast whose Retry asks again. A new question, a change of page or an unmounted host answers the open one with `false`.
doc.notFor:
- A short form or a detail: UiModal.
- A question with a field in it (a reason to type): UiModal `role="alertdialog"`.
- A record: UiCrudDrawer.
- An outcome with nothing to answer: a toast from `useToast` in UiToaster.

UiConfirm.about: The host of `useConfirm`, mounted once at the app root beside UiToaster. Take it to ask a yes-or-no question before an action.

props.name: value
props.doc: What goes to the clipboard, whole. Empty, the button is off and says there is nothing to copy.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible text beside the glyph, and the name as it is ("Copy link"); for a value shown as itself pass `ariaLabel` too. It wins over `truncate`.

props.name: truncate
props.doc: Shows `value` cut in the middle to about this many characters, in monospace; the copy is still whole.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `ghost` is text alone, its glyph on hover, for an id in a table; `outline` is a framed button with its glyph always shown; `inline` is text inside a line of text, its size and ink, with a small glyph after it.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

props.name: flush
props.doc: In a cell: the text starts on the column line, the button's own padding and border taken back. `ghost` only.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: No copy; the button stays in place.

props.name: disabledReason
props.doc: Why it cannot copy now, while `disabled`: it stays in the Tab order and says the reason in a tooltip and as its description, as UiButton's. An empty `value` says "Nothing to copy" by itself.

props.name: toast
props.doc: Also say a success as a toast, where the button leaves the view once pressed; a failure always is one.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name; defaults to "Copy" for a glyph alone and "Copy <text>" for a truncated value.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The glyph at rest, a Lucide component; `Copy` when unset. Two copy buttons side by side tell what they copy by it: `Code`, `Bot`.

events.name: copy
events.doc: The value reached the clipboard (`true`) or the clipboard refused (`false`).

UiCopyButton.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A button that copies `value` to the clipboard and shows a check for 1.2 s. Take it beside an id, a key or any value a person copies.

decisions.label: Outcome
decisions.text: A failure marks the glyph for 1.2 s, as a success shows its check, and also shows an error toast in the app's UiToaster, so mount one; a success shows a toast only with `toast`, since the check in view has already said it. The toast is not read aloud, because the live region has said it. Every copy button on the page refreshes the one toast instead of piling up more. Where the browser has no Clipboard API (a page over plain HTTP), the copy goes through a field no one sees, and the focus comes back.

decisions.label: Shapes
decisions.text: Without text it is an icon button named "Copy", with the `Copy` glyph or your `icon`. With `label` or `truncate` it is a button with text; `truncate` shows the value cut in the middle in monospace (`613aa1…4510e0`) and copies it whole. A line break or another control character in the kept half of a cut value draws as a mark (`⏎`, a control picture), never left invisible: it still copies with the character itself. A `label` is a few words, as a button's; a value too long for its place is shown with `truncate`, cut in the middle.

decisions.label: Ghost
decisions.text: A `ghost` one is text with no plate. Its glyph appears on hover and focus of this button only (always on a screen without hover), so a column of ids stays quiet. In a cell, `flush` pulls it back by its own padding and border, so the text starts on the column line. Beside a neighbor it keeps its box, because a negative margin there would overlap the neighbor.

decisions.label: Outline
decisions.text: An `outline` one is a framed button: plate, frame and glyph always shown, since a frame around an empty space reads as a hole.

decisions.label: Inline
decisions.text: An `inline` one is a word inside a line of text (the small line of a drawer's header): no plate, no height, no padding, the line's size and ink, and a small glyph always after it, since a glyph that waits for hover leaves a gap. It needs a `label` or `truncate`. A label longer than the line is cut with an ellipsis, whole in a tooltip (UiTruncate), and the glyph stays.

decisions.label: Secrets
decisions.text: `label` and `truncate` put the text on the screen and in the accessible name, so a secret goes in with neither.

decisions.label: Off
decisions.text: An empty `value` keeps the button in the Tab order and says "Nothing to copy", as a `disabledReason` says yours (UiButton's): in a tooltip and as its description. `disabled` alone takes it out of the Tab order.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits in a table's copy column (named "Copy" and the value), in a UiInput's `#end`, in a drawer's header line, and beside UiPasswordField's input, before its generate button. Beside other copy buttons, each one takes its own `ariaLabel`, which holds the text it shows: a voice command says what it sees. A cut value is named by its cut by default ("Copy 613aa1…4510e0").

doc.keyboard:
A native button in every shape.
- `Tab`: reaches it, an empty `value` too; `disabled` takes it out, unless it has a `disabledReason`.
- `Enter` `Space`: copy; the focus stays on it after the copy.
A `ghost` one shows its glyph on keyboard focus, as on hover.
doc.reader:
- Name: "Copy" for a glyph alone, "Copy" and the visible text for a cut value, `label` as it is, or `ariaLabel`; "Copied" never joins the name.
- Outcome: "Copied" or "Could not copy" (when the clipboard refuses), from one polite live region outside the button, inside an open modal window when the button is in one, since the window hides the page from a reader. It is heard even after the button has left the view, and said again for a second copy in the same window.
- Off with a reason: `aria-disabled`, and "Nothing to copy" or the `disabledReason` is its description.
- Glyph: hidden.
- Toast: not read, since the region has said it.
doc.states: At rest: a glyph alone, a cut id in monospace, or a label. Copied: a check for 1.2 s. Refused: an alert glyph for 1.2 s, no check, "Could not copy" and an error toast. Nothing to copy (an empty `value`) or `disabled`: the disabled ink, the reason in a tooltip. A long `inline` label: cut, whole in a tooltip. `ghost` shows the glyph on hover and focus only (always on a screen without hover), `outline` always, `inline` a small one after the word; `flush` in a cell; `xs`, `sm` and `md`; joined in a UiButtonGroup; a success toast with `toast`.
doc.notFor:
- A glyph that does anything else: UiIconButton.
- An action with text: UiButton.
- A value cut to fit with nothing to copy: UiTruncate.
- A secret shown as text on the screen: never; it is copied with neither `label` nor `truncate`.

props.name: count
props.doc: The number. `0` is shown; hide it with `v-if` when zero means nothing.

props.name: max
props.doc: The largest count shown as is; above it the count reads `{max}+`. A whole number from 1.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Meaning: `brand` for the product's own counts, a verdict, or `neutral`.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `soft` pale plate for a quiet total, `solid` saturated fill for a count that calls; `warning` is always solid, its pale plate reads muddy.

props.name: size
props.doc: `sm` 16px for a corner mark or a dense row, `md` 20px on a button, a tab or a navigation row.

props.name: dot
props.doc: A dot without a number: there is something new, how much does not matter. 8px, 6px at `sm`.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: The name of a count that stands alone, the number with its unit: "4 unread". In a tab, a row or a button their label names it.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: A short mark instead of the number, such as "!"; it takes the same circle.

UiCount.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A number beside a label. Take it for the count on a tab, a button or a row; on the corner of an icon or an avatar take UiIndicator.

decisions.label: Shape
decisions.text: One digit sits in a circle, more digits in a capsule, and above `max` it shows `{max}+`. `soft` is quiet; `solid` draws attention.

decisions.label: Values
decisions.text: A fraction is rounded down, an infinite count shows the overflow, a negative or missing one is `0`, and one that is not a number draws nothing: unknown is not empty.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits on a button's label, a tab (UiTabs), a navigation row (UiAppShell) and a UiFilter trigger, and serves as the mark of UiIndicator. The root is a `<span>`.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: it takes no focus, and reaches the keyboard only through its host, a button, a tab or a row.
doc.reader:
- Name: a bare number means nothing: the host names it with its label ("Inbox, 4"); standing alone, `ariaLabel` makes it an image named with its unit ("4 unread").
- Dot: a `dot` is hidden.
- Change: not announced.
doc.states: One digit in a circle, more in a capsule, `{max}+` above `max`, `0` shown; `soft` pale or `solid` saturated, `warning` always solid; `dot`, with no number; `sm` 16px and `md` 20px.
