No hover or focus of its own. A count that is not a number draws nothing; a bad `max` falls back. Both warn in dev, once per value.
doc.notFor:
- A label: UiBadge.
- A change against the value before: UiDelta.
- A count on the corner of an icon or an avatar: UiIndicator around it.

props.name: title
props.doc: The record's name, the dialog's name for a screen reader: "Santa", not "Edit operation".

props.name: description
props.doc: What the record is and a detail: "operation · 31 Aug".

props.name: loading
props.doc: The record is still loading: a skeleton in the body, Save held.

props.name: submitting
props.doc: Saving: a spinner on Save, Cancel held, and no way to close until it ends.

props.name: submitDisabled
props.doc: Save is held: nothing to save yet, or the form cannot be sent for a reason of your own; a load that failed is `error`.

props.name: persistent
props.doc: Unsaved input on this level: the backdrop and Escape are refused with a shake; Cancel and the cross still close.

props.name: persistentAbove
props.doc: At a step: a level above holds unsaved input. The cross, which closes them all, shakes instead; ‹, Escape and Cancel go one up as ever.

props.name: error
props.doc: Why the record could not be loaded, in words for the reader: the body says it with Retry (`retry`), the header keeps the title alone, Save is held and nothing is guarded.

props.name: submitLabel
props.doc: Save's label; defaults to "Save".

props.name: saveAnother
props.doc: A menu on Save with "Save and add another", for a batch of new records: the parent saves (setting `submitting` while it does), clears the form and keeps the drawer open; once the form changed from what was sent, the cursor goes to its first field, a default kept in it or not.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.doc: Cancel's label; defaults to "Cancel".

props.name: path
props.doc: The levels above this one, from the top: `['Groceries', 'Fruit']`. Set, the header shows ‹, named by the last.

props.name: index
props.doc: The record's place in the list it was opened from, from 0, across its pages; with `total`, the header walks the list.

props.name: total
props.doc: How many records the list holds: two or more, the header of the record shows ↑ ↓, which emit `move`; a step shows none.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: Nothing on this level waits for Save, every row goes at once: the footer holds only the way back; at the top there is no footer, the cross closes.

props.name: divided
props.doc: A line between neighboring sections, the default; `false` parts them by their titles and the gap: a long form of different parts.

props.name: size
props.doc: The panel's width: `md` 512px for a record, the default; `lg` 768px for what reads wide, a text or a code.

events.name: submit
events.doc: Save was pressed or Enter was hit in a single-line field; once per request. `another` is true from "Save and add another": save, then clear the form for the next record and keep the drawer open.

events.name: retry
events.doc: Retry of a load that failed was pressed; the parent loads the record again.

events.name: update:open
events.doc: The new value of `open`, for `v-model:open`.

events.name: close
events.doc: The drawer closed: Cancel, the cross, the backdrop or Escape.

events.name: back
events.doc: The way up was asked for: ‹, Escape, the backdrop or Cancel at a step. `to` is the index in `path` to show; the parent swaps the level.

events.name: move
events.doc: The up or down button in the header: `to` is the index of the record to show in the drawer; the parent loads it.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The form: fields, or UiCard sections separated by the drawer. No `<form>` of your own.

slots.name: status
slots.doc: Beside the title, for a record whose status is the point; a status as usual is a small mark in `#description`.

slots.name: description
slots.doc: The small line under the title in your own markup, in place of `description`: an id to copy (UiCopyButton), facts. One line.

slots.name: actions
slots.doc: Icon buttons before the cross: open as a page, more actions. Ghost UiIconButton.

slots.name: loading
slots.doc: While `loading`, a skeleton in the geometry of the form that comes, so nothing moves when it does; two fields by default.

UiCrudDrawer.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A record opened for editing in a side panel, over the list it came from, laid over UiDrawer. Take it to edit a row opened from a UiDataTable without leaving the list.

decisions.label: Surface
decisions.text: The panel is UiDrawer: its width, header, gutter, stack, scroll lock and focus kept in. The record adds the form round the body and the footer, Save and Cancel, the loading and the failed states, the steps of `path` and the walk through the list, and leads the exits: Escape and the backdrop go a level up at a step, the cross is refused while a level above holds input.

decisions.label: Kept pages
decisions.text: In a page that a `KeepAlive` keeps, an open record stays open when the page is deactivated, as UiDrawer's panel does. Close it (`open` false) when the route changes.

decisions.label: Header
decisions.text: `title` names the record ("Northwind Studio"). The small line under it (`description`, or a `#description` built from the library's parts) starts with the status as a small mark (UiBadge `inline` `sm`), then an id to copy (UiCopyButton `inline`), then a fact, cut when long and shown whole on hover. `#status` beside the title is for the rare record whose status is the point. `#actions` takes at most one icon button of your own, before the cross. With `index` and `total` (two records or more), ↑ and ↓ walk the list (`move`); they are refused while input is unsaved. The walk is the record's: at a step they are gone, since a level above may hold unsaved input, and the way up comes first. The parent loads the record; at the edge of a page it turns the list's page and keeps the opened row marked. At the end of the list, the arrow that can go no further hands the focus to the other arrow.

decisions.label: Gutter
decisions.text: The drawer's: the body is padded by `--space-drawer` (24px, 16 in a dense product), and the lines inside it keep the same space.

decisions.label: Body
decisions.text: The body is a form. After a refused save, Save is ready again as soon as the person moves to fix the field, whatever the control (a select fires no typing). The footer is pinned and holds Cancel and Save; with `saveAnother`, Save carries a menu with "Save and add another", for entering a batch of new records. That is why `submit` carries `{ another }` (true from "Save and add another": save, clear the form, keep the drawer open), where UiModal's `submit` carries nothing: a window sends one way. An action that sends a request by itself (delete, archive, a status) stays in the body: a card of UiListItem `as="button"` rows in a UiList after the fields, with the dangerous one last in `tone="danger"`. The body is a chain of UiCard sections, direct children of the slot, separated in one of two ways. By default a line stands between neighbors, and the sections need no titles. With `:divided="false"`, each section after the head of the record starts with a UiHeader `legend`, the line and the title in one, and the sections stand 48 apart, the step between blocks; a dev warning names a section without its legend. Do not put a form of your own in the slot.

decisions.label: Delete
decisions.text: An action that takes the record from the list closes the drawer first, waits a tick (`await nextTick()`), then removes the row: a UiTable then hands the focus to the same control of the row now in its place. A delete asked through UiConfirm with an `action` does the same inside the action, so a Retry deletes too; the question gives the focus back to the drawer's row, and the table hands it to the row now in its place.

decisions.label: Steps
decisions.text: A record with records inside opens them as steps of the same drawer, never as a second drawer. The parent swaps the body and the title and passes the levels above in `path`; the header shows a ‹ button named by the level above. ‹, Escape and the backdrop emit `back` with the level to go to, and Cancel goes one level up, so leaving a step never drops the input of a level above. A `persistent` step refuses with a shake. The cross closes the whole drawer; with `persistentAbove` (a level above holds unsaved input) it shakes instead. `error` works at a step as it does at the top. The focus goes to the first field of a new step, and back to its row on the way up. Each level has one job. A record is a form with a card of its actions (UiListItem `as="button" step` rows). What a record holds is a `readonly` list level (UiListField over the rows). A level that decides (a queue) is `readonly` with the verdict in the body, and a decline opens its note first. `readonly` keeps only the way back in the footer, and at the top level not even that. A path the header cannot name in one line needs a page instead.

doc.keyboard:
- `Enter`: in a single-line field, saves; in a text box it breaks the line.
- `Meta+Enter` `Ctrl+Enter`: save from a text box too (`Meta` is Cmd).
- `Escape`: closes, or goes one level up at a step; shakes instead while input is unsaved.
- `Tab`: stays inside the panel.
A refused save puts the focus on the first field in error. The up and down buttons in the header of the record walk the list when `index` and `total` are given. The focus goes to the first field once the record is in, and returns to the opener on close. It never lands on a button that sends a decision: on a level with no field, the panel takes it.
doc.reader:
- Window: a modal dialog named by the record's title (`aria-labelledby`).
- Body: says it is loading (`aria-busy`); a refused save marks the field in error (`aria-invalid`).
- Way up: at a step, a button named by the level above.
- Refused way out: a close, a step or the list's arrows; a shake for the eye, and the reader keeps the focus where it was and hears why: input not saved, or a request still on its way.
doc.notFor:
- A panel to read or to set at once, with no form: UiDrawer.
- A short task that is not a record: UiModal.
- A question about the record (delete it?): UiConfirm above the drawer.
- A second drawer over the first: never; in UiCrudDrawer a record inside a record is a step of the same drawer (`path`).
doc.states: `loading` shows a skeleton and holds Save; `#loading` gives one in the form's own geometry. A failed load (`error`) shows UiNoData `tone="danger"` with Retry in the body; the header keeps only the title, and Save is held. Pass `error` with the words and listen to `retry`. `submitting` spins Save and refuses every close. A submit the host refuses by marking a field as it gets it shakes the drawer, as a refused close does, and the focus goes to that field. `persistent` guards unsaved input on this level: the backdrop and Escape shake instead of closing. These guard only the drawer's own exits. A close from outside (`open` set to false, for example by the browser's Back on a deep link) is for the host to guard, before it changes `open`.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The columns in order, each with how its values are drawn: fixed; or the state from `useTableColumns` over them, and then the table draws its `visible` and the toolbar gets the columns button.

props.name: items
props.doc: Rows of the current page.

props.name: total
props.doc: Records in the whole list; gives the count and the pages. Unset, there is no footer. Leave it unset until the first answer (a 0 would move a linked page back to one) and keep the last value while a page loads.

props.name: page
props.doc: Current page, from 1 (`v-model:page`). A new search or sort asks for 1; a page past the last asks for the last once the list is not loading.

props.name: pageSize
props.doc: Records per page; the count and the pages are derived from it.

props.name: rowLabel
props.doc: Names a row for its checkbox: "Select Anna" instead of "Select row".

props.name: rowKey
props.doc: What tells rows apart; `id` when unset.

props.name: sort
props.doc: The current sort (`v-model:sort`); the parent orders the rows.

props.name: selectable
props.doc: A checkbox on every row; the selection strip replaces the toolbar while rows are selected.

props.name: selection
props.doc: Keys of the selected rows (`v-model:selection`).

props.name: isRowSelectable
props.doc: Which rows can be selected.

props.name: search
props.doc: The search text (`v-model:search`); the field is always there.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.doc: What the search looks in: its placeholder and its name. Unset, "Search" and the table's `aria-label` ("Search Invoices"), so two lists on one page keep their searches apart.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the toolbar row: `xs` for a dense row, `sm` (36 px), `md` for a comfortable one; unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`). The slots get it as `{ size }`.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Rows are on their way.

props.name: error
props.doc: Why the rows could not be loaded, in words; shown with a retry.

props.name: filtered
props.doc: A filter of the page's own is on: an empty page says so and offers "Reset filters", which sends `reset-filters`. A UiFilter in `#filters` and the block's own search count by themselves.

props.name: clickable
props.doc: Rows answer a click with `row-click`. The keyboard reaches a record through a control in `#row-actions`.

events.name: retry
events.doc: The retry of a failed load was pressed.

events.name: update:page
events.doc: Asks for a page: a pressed number or arrow, page one after a new search or sort, the last page when the list shrank under the current one.

events.name: update:sort
events.doc: Asks for a sort: a column and its direction, or `null` to drop it; the parent orders the rows.

events.name: update:selection
events.doc: A new set of the selected keys; the old set is never changed in place.

events.name: update:search
events.doc: The search text: after a pause in typing, at once on Enter or on clearing it.

events.name: row-click
events.doc: A row was clicked with `clickable` on.

events.name: reset-filters
events.doc: "Reset filters" in the empty state was pressed: the UiFilter components in `#filters` are reset already, the page clears its other filters.

slots.name: filters
slots.doc: What narrows the list, after the search: a period, filters.

slots.name: actions
slots.doc: What acts on the list: catalog buttons, then the main action last (the columns menu comes from `columns`).

slots.name: bulk
slots.scope: { count: number; selection: Set<string | number>; size: ControlSize; }
slots.doc: What acts on the selected rows; shown in the selection strip.

slots.name: row-actions
slots.doc: Controls of one row, in a column kept at the end.

slots.name: empty
slots.doc: Instead of the empty-page text.

slots.name: empty-actions
slots.scope: { searched: boolean; filtered: boolean; size: ControlSize; }
slots.doc: The app's next step for an empty list: beside Clear search and Reset filters when nothing matched, alone under "No records yet".

UiDataTable.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A whole list screen in one card: the toolbar, the table, the selection strip, and a footer with the count and the pages. Take it for a list page that searches, sorts, selects and pages.

decisions.label: State
decisions.text: It draws what it is given and owns no state. The page, the sort, the selection and the search are `v-model`s; the rows and the total come from outside. It knows no router, API or storage: a page or an engine wires those. The selection stays as the page, the search and the filters change: the strip counts rows out of view, and `#bulk` gets their keys too. A page that wants only what is in view clears the selection on those changes.

decisions.label: Columns
decisions.text: A column's `type` says how its values are drawn: money, date, status, copy or progress, text by default. A `#cell.<key>` slot draws a domain cell and wins over the type. A money column stands at the end, digit under digit, unless it says `align: 'start'`. `columns` is the list, fixed; or the state from `useTableColumns` over it, as UiTableToolbar's `columns` is, and then the table draws the visible ones and the toolbar gets the columns button.

decisions.label: Hidden sort
decisions.text: The sort is the list's order, as a link made it; the columns are the person's view. A sort on a column they hid stays, and a line above the table tells it ("Sorted by Amount, descending"), since no header can.

decisions.label: Slots
decisions.text: `#filters` narrows the list, `#actions` acts on it, `#bulk` acts on the selection, and `#row-actions` acts on one row.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: No empty list is a dead end. A search or a filter that found nothing offers its way back, Clear search and Reset filters; `#empty-actions` adds the app's own step beside them, such as creating what was searched for. With no records yet the table can offer nothing of its own, so `#empty-actions` is the step there, such as adding the first record; `#empty` replaces it all.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: They reach the table, so `aria-label` names the table, its page checkbox, its scroll box and its pages; `class` and `style` stay on the card.

decisions.label: Built from
decisions.text: One card of UiTableToolbar, UiTable and UiPagination, standing straight on a page.

decisions.label: Pages
decisions.text: A new search, a new sort, or a choice the person changes in a UiFilter of `#filters` asks for page one; a value the app sets from outside does not, so a linked page keeps its place. A page past the last (after a delete, or on a narrower list) asks for the last.

decisions.label: Loading
decisions.text: The page loads the rows, and the page drops an answer that is not for its latest query, as First table in the README does: the table shows the rows it is given. While loading, the table keeps the last `total`. The page fetches when its models change, not inside the `update:search` handler: that handler runs before the move to page one that follows it. A new search draws skeleton rows at once, as many as were in view; a sort or a page of the same search keeps the rows, dimmed. A filter of the page's own empties `items` while its answer is out, in the same step that sets `loading`, and the skeleton takes their place too. The table stands on a floor its skeleton, its empty answer and its failed load share, so nothing under it moves while the person types; the search field keeps the focus and shows no spinner.

doc.keyboard:
- `Tab`: walks the toolbar, then the page checkbox, a sortable header, each row's checkbox and the controls in `#row-actions`, then the pages.
- `Enter` `Space`: on a sortable header, a button, turn it.
- `Escape`: clears the search.
A row is reached through a control in `#row-actions`, never by a click on the row alone. Rows marked by the app while the focus is in the toolbar hand it to the strip's clear button, as the strip covers the toolbar; the strip gone, the focus goes to the page checkbox.
doc.reader:
- Table: named by the `aria-label` the page gives it.
- Sortable header: says its direction (`aria-sort`); a sort a press asked for is said once the app sends it back.
- Row checkbox: named by `rowLabel`.
- Selection strip: says how many rows are selected through a live region. Its count, the range and the pager's page count are written as the app's language groups digits ("1,234").
- Refresh: says it is updating (`aria-busy`), then the range the load brought ("1–20 of 57").
- Empty page: says why.
- Failed load: says why and offers Retry.
doc.states: Loading (a skeleton on a first load), loaded, refreshing (the rows kept, dimmed to 60%), empty with nothing yet, empty because of a filter (change or reset the filters), failed (the words and Retry), a selection with its strip, and a page past the last, which asks for the last. A page is drawn whole, not windowed. Measured in Chromium (production build, six typed columns and checkboxes): 250 rows mount in about 70 ms and 1000 in about 320 ms, a third of it the browser's layout, and a sort redraws 1000 rows in about 150 ms. Past a few hundred rows, page.
doc.notFor:
- A table with no toolbar and no pages: a bare UiTable.
- A list of names that grows from its last row: UiListField.
- Rows of settings or actions: UiListItem rows in a UiList.

props.name: value
props.doc: An ISO string with a time or a day alone, a Date, or a timestamp. A time with no zone is read in the app's zone. Empty or unreadable prints a dash.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Which fact leads: `time` on top for a list within a day, `day` on top for a list across months.

props.name: context
props.doc: What the lower line answers: how long ago (`relative`), or which day of the week (`weekday`).

UiDateCell.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A date in a table column, on two lines: the exact value on top, its context under it. Take it for any column of dates or times.

decisions.label: Look
decisions.text: The exact value is in monospace, the context in small capitals, with no rule between them.

decisions.label: Which leads
decisions.text: `variant` sets which fact goes on top. `time` is for a list within a day: the time on top, the day under it. `day` is for a list across months: the full date on top, the time under it.

decisions.label: Context
decisions.text: `context` sets the lower line. `relative` says how long ago (Today, Yesterday, then the short day); `weekday` names the day of the week in full. The two lines always carry the whole value: under a leading time, the weekday line adds the day; over a weekday line, the leading date adds the time.

decisions.label: Days
decisions.text: A value without a time (`2026-09-24`) is a calendar day: it always leads with the day, and no time zone of the app moves it to the day before or after. A day of another year shows its year. Today and Yesterday are read on the calendar the digits are shown in: the app's zone (`createGrani({ timeZone })`), or the device's without one.

decisions.label: Times
decisions.text: An ISO day and time with no zone (`2026-09-24T10:00`, or `2026-09-24 10:00:00` as a database writes it) is the reading of a clock, read in the app's zone, where it is shown: 10:00 shows as 10:00 on every device. A reading the clock skips on a spring night (02:30 in New York) shows as the hour after the jump, and one it shows twice on an autumn night is its first time, as the device takes them. Without the app's zone it is read and shown on the device's clock. A day or a time that does not exist (February 30, 25:00) prints a dash. A value with `Z` or an offset, a Date and a timestamp are moments, shown in the app's zone.

decisions.label: Tooltip
decisions.text: The full date shows in a UiTooltip only while the two lines hide it, that is, under a leading time over Today or Yesterday.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: An empty or unreadable value prints the dash a table prints.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: They land on the cell's span.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: the cell takes no tab stop, and its tooltip opens on hover and on a tap.
doc.reader:
- Lines: read as text in the order they stand: the exact value, then its context.
- Tooltip: while it shows, the full date in it describes the cell (`aria-describedby`); it shows only while the lines hide the date, under a leading time over Today or Yesterday.
- Empty value: read as the dash.
doc.states: None of its own: the row and the table carry hover, selection, loading and failure. The cell has two leads (`time`, `day`), two contexts (`relative`, `weekday`), a day without a time, a time with no zone, a day of another year, and an empty or unreadable value as a dash.
doc.notFor:
- An amount: UiMoneyCell.
- A day to pick: UiDatePicker.
- A period to filter by: UiDateRange.
- The moment of an event on a timeline: UiLog's own time.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The day, `YYYY-MM-DD` (`v-model`); `null` for none.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown while empty; defaults to "Choose a date".

props.name: min
props.doc: The first day that can be picked, inclusive.

props.name: max
props.doc: The last day that can be picked, inclusive.

props.name: presets
props.doc: Days from today under the field, as one-click picks: `true` for the default seven, or a list of ids and `{ label, days }`.

props.name: clearable
props.doc: A cross that empties the field, as UiSelect's; never shown on a required field.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: empty is an error, said to a reader, and no cross. Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The field cannot be changed: a disabled plate, no calendar, nothing sent with a form.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Standalone only: the value is wrong. Inside UiField the field's error says so.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Standalone only: the accessible name. Inside UiField the label names it.

props.name: name
props.doc: Sends the day with a form, under this name.

props.name: id
props.doc: Id of the button, standalone; inside UiField the field's id wins.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: A day was picked, or `null` when cleared.

UiDatePicker.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A form field for one day, in the input capsule on the control ladder. Type the day, or open a calendar to pick it from.

decisions.label: Value
decisions.text: The value is an ISO day (`2026-09-24`); the field shows it in the locale's format with its day of the week, and its year only when it is not this one ("Thu, Sep 24" this year, "Thu, Mar 12, 1987"), so a due date put on a Saturday, or a day one off, is seen before it is kept. Cut in a narrow column, the whole day shows in a tooltip on hover; a screen reader hears it whole. Without `presets` the field runs no clock: a page left open past New Year shows last year's days without their year until the field is created again, as when the page is reloaded; a typed day reads today as it is at the key. `focus()` puts the focus on the field.

decisions.label: Popover
decisions.text: The capsule's button opens a UiPopover with a UiCalendar on the chosen day, or on today. A pick closes it.

decisions.label: Typing
decisions.text: A digit typed on the field starts a day as the app's language writes one: its parts in the locale's order (`12.03.1987` in Russian, `03/12/1987` in American English), any mark between them, or digits alone (`12031987`, `120387`); a part left out is today's (`12.03` is this year's) and a two-digit year is the nearest one at most ten years ahead. The field shows what was typed, and the calendar opens on the day it reads, chosen and in focus, or shows no day while it reads none. Enter takes it; a day that does not exist, or one outside `min` and `max`, is not taken, never guessed: the field is marked invalid until the text changes, and a reader hears why. A press away from the field and its calendar takes it too when it is written in full, day, month and a four-digit year or eight digits, as a text field keeps what was typed; a stray digit or a year half typed (`03/12/19`) is dropped there, not guessed into a day, and a reader hears why. Escape drops it, as do the cross and a preset. Digits of other scripts (`٢٤`, `۲۴`, `２４`) count as theirs, eight of them make a day whatever marks stand between, and a year in the locale's calendar (`2530` in Thai) is read as that calendar's; a calendar whose months differ (Persian, Hijri) takes no typing, its calendar is the way in.

decisions.label: Clear
decisions.text: `clearable` adds a cross that empties the field, as in UiSelect. A required field never gets it: there, empty is an error, not a state.

decisions.label: Presets
decisions.text: `presets` puts days counted from today under the field: one click instead of the calendar, for the days people enter most often. `true` gives Today, Yesterday, A week ago, Tomorrow, In 3 days, In a week and In 2 weeks; a list picks among them by id (`['today', 'yesterday', 'weekAgo']` for a day spent, `['tomorrow', 'inAWeek']` for a deadline) or adds the app's own, `{ label, days }`, with `days` from today, negative for the past; one whose days are not a finite number, or reach past the year 9999, is left out and said in development, as an id the field does not know is. They move on at midnight while the page stays open. A preset is an action, not a toggle: the field says the day it set, and no button holds room for a check, so three stand on one line.

decisions.label: Window
decisions.text: `min` and `max` are read as the calendar reads them: a malformed bound counts as no bound, and bounds given backwards make the same window. A day outside them is kept and reads invalid; a preset outside them is disabled.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: No day is `null`: the field sends `null` when cleared and reads `null` (or an empty string) as no day.

decisions.label: Standalone
decisions.text: It takes `invalid`, `required` and `ariaLabel`; inside UiField it reads id, error and required from the field.

decisions.label: Width
decisions.text: The field keeps its width when a day is picked or cleared and when it turns disabled: the text is sized to the widest date the locale prints, and the cross keeps its place.

decisions.label: Combobox
decisions.text: The button is a combobox, as in UiSelect: the chosen date is its value, and the capsule draws the focus ring. ArrowDown or Alt+ArrowDown opens the calendar.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: `class` and `style` land on the root, everything else on the button. The root is the capsule, or, with `presets`, a column that holds the capsule and the presets under it. Without presets the capsule is the root, so a UiButtonGroup can join it to a UiTimePicker or a button.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a form column under UiField, beside UiInput and UiSelect on the same ladder step, before a UiTimePicker for a day and its hours; in a window's or a drawer's form as well as on a page.

doc.keyboard:
The button is a combobox.
- `Tab`: reaches it; the presets are buttons that it reaches too.
- `Enter` `Space` `ArrowDown` `Alt+ArrowDown`: open the calendar; `Ctrl` or `Meta` with an arrow stays the browser's.
- `0–9`: starts a typed day and opens the calendar on it.
While a day is typed, on the field or in the panel:
- `0–9` `.` `/` `-` `Space`: go on typing it.
- `Backspace`: takes back the last key.
- `Enter`: takes the day it reads and closes; a day that does not exist is not taken. On a day the arrows moved to it picks that day, as the calendar does.
In the panel the focus lands on the day it opens on, and the calendar's keys apply:
- `Tab`: cycles inside the panel.
- `Escape`: closes it, drops a day being typed, and returns the focus to the button; a pick does the same, inside a window too.
The cross clears the value and leaves the focus on the button, also while the calendar is open.
When the field turns disabled, the calendar closes and the focus stays on the field.
doc.reader:
- Field: a combobox named by `ariaLabel` or the field's label. Its value is the chosen date as the locale prints it, or the placeholder.
- Errors: `required` sets `aria-required`; a day outside the window, a typed day refused, or a field error sets `aria-invalid`; the field's description and error are read with it.
- Panel: named by the field's label; the calendar in it speaks as UiCalendar does.
- Presets: a group named in words, each a button that sets its day; the field says the day.
- Clear: the cross has a name.
- Typing: the field says what is typed; the focus stands on the day it reads, named by its full date; a refused Enter says "Not a date" or that the date is outside the allowed range.
doc.states: Empty, a day picked, open (the calendar on the chosen day, on today, or on the window's nearest day), disabled (the plate, no calendar, no cross, nothing sent), invalid (standalone, or from a field error), a day outside `min` and `max` (kept, reads invalid), a preset outside the window (disabled), and `clearable` with a day. The width stays the same in all of them.
doc.notFor:
- A period in a toolbar: UiDateRange.
- A month on a page with no field: UiCalendar alone.
- A time of day: UiTimePicker beside it.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The period (`v-model`): `from` and `to` as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `null` for no bound, and `preset`, the named period or `custom` for days picked on the calendar. A named one wins over the days: they are counted again from today. A `null` preset makes days `custom` and none All time.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id of the button, for a label elsewhere. Inside UiField, the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: align
props.doc: Which edge of the button the panel lines up with.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: What the button filters by, read before the days: "Period" by default, "Paid" for a column of payment days.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder, as the rest of the toolbar row. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

props.name: min
props.doc: The first day a period can reach, inclusive: a preset partly before it is cut there, one wholly before it is disabled.

props.name: max
props.doc: The last day a period can reach, inclusive: a preset partly after it is cut there, one wholly after it is disabled.

props.name: stepper
props.doc: Two arrows before the button that move the period back or forward by its own length: a month by a month, a week by seven days.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The period cannot be changed: the button and the arrows are off, and an open panel closes.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The whole period at once: a preset, a span picked on the calendar (`custom`), or a named preset counted again from today.

UiDateRange.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A toolbar filter by period, with named presets and a custom range. Take it in a table toolbar to narrow a list by dates.

decisions.label: Button
decisions.text: The button shows the days ("Aug 1 – 31"), with the year only when it is not this year. A whole year shows as the year ("2025"), and no bounds show as All time. One bound reads "From Aug 1" or "Until Aug 31". The button is as wide as its widest named period, so picking among them never moves the row.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.text: The panel is a UiPopover with a list edge to edge, as in UiSelect, from the shortest period to the longest: Today, Yesterday, This week, Last 7 days, then the months with Last 30 days among them, then the years and All time. The chosen preset is checked in the list. Each preset shows the days or the months it covers, a week from the day the language's week starts; a pick applies it and closes the panel. "Custom range…", under a line, turns the panel into a calendar on the current span. The first day picked starts a span; the second ends it, applies it as `custom` and closes the panel. The row above the calendar goes back to the list. No fields appear beside the button, so the toolbar keeps its width.

decisions.label: Window
decisions.text: `min` and `max` bound what can be picked: a preset partly outside them is cut at the bound ("This month" with `max` today runs to today), one wholly outside is disabled, and the calendar stops at them. All time stays no bounds.

decisions.label: Stepper
decisions.text: `stepper` puts two arrows before the button that move the period back and forward by its own length: a month or a quarter by whole months, a week or a custom span by its days. They stand before it, so at the start of a row (a toolbar's `#start`) a longer label, a week across the turn of the year, never moves them from under the pointer. The step lands on a preset's name when it matches one, so stepping forward from last month gives This month, which rolls with today; where two presets share the days, the one the period last had wins. An arrow is disabled when there is nowhere to go: All time, one bound, or past the window. A step the window cuts keeps only the days inside it, and the next step moves by those. A step counts from the model, so a host that applies it late takes two quick presses as one.

decisions.label: Model
decisions.text: One `v-model` holds what a URL carries, `{ from, to, preset }` (`DateRangeValue`): ISO days, `null` for no bound, and the named preset, `null` for none. A pick sends the whole period at once. A named preset wins over its days: in the browser its days are counted again from today, so "Last month" opened next month shows the new last month. `custom` keeps its days. With no `preset`, the days decide: days mean `custom`, no days mean All time. For a query, `periodBounds(value, { timeZone, locale, min, max })` gives the moments the period covers, its last day whole by the app's clock, a named preset counted from today as the button shows it, on the server too: ask for `at >= start && at < end`.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a table toolbar, beside the search, UiFilter and UiTableColumns; or in a form under a UiField label.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Inside UiField the field's label is its name, read before the days, for the button, its panel and the arrows' group; a click on the label opens the panel. The field's id, error and words reach the button.

decisions.label: Disabled
decisions.text: `disabled` turns off the button and both arrows, and closes the panel if it is open.

doc.keyboard:
On the button:
- `Tab`: reaches it.
- `Enter` `Space`: open the panel on the list, with the chosen preset highlighted.
On an arrow (`stepper`):
- `Tab`: reaches them, before the button.
- `Enter` `Space`: move the period; the focus stays on the arrow, or goes to the button when the arrow turns off at the window's end.
In the list:
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`: move, passing over a preset outside the window.
- `Home` `End`: jump.
- `Enter` `Space`: apply the preset and close the panel.
- `ArrowDown`: past the last preset, reaches "Custom range…".
On "Custom range…":
- `ArrowUp`: goes back to the list.
- `Enter` `Space`: open the calendar with the focus on its day.
In the calendar, which takes UiCalendar's keys and picks the span:
- `Enter` `Space`: on the row above it, go back to the list, on the custom row.
Anywhere in the panel:
- `Escape`: closes the panel and returns the focus to the button, as a pick does; a half-picked span is dropped on close.
doc.reader:
- Button: its name comes before its days, "Period, Aug 1 – 31", or `ariaLabel` in its place, or the field's label inside UiField, with `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`.
- Panel: a dialog with the same name.
- Presets: a listbox with that name, each option with the days or months it covers, the chosen one selected and one outside the window disabled.
- Custom row: marked as the current choice (`aria-current`), and its days describe it.
- Calendar: a live region says "Choose the first day", then "Now choose the last day".
- Row above the calendar: named "Custom range, back to the list".
- Arrows: named "Previous period" and "Next period", in a group with the button's name ("Issued, group"), so two on one page are told apart; after a step the new days are said, since the focus stays on the arrow.
doc.states: A named preset, a custom span, one bound ("From Aug 1", "Until Aug 31"), a whole year, All time; the list open, the calendar with a first day picked; a period set from outside while the panel is open, which moves the highlight and drops a half pick; presets cut by the window and one disabled outside it; the arrows, one disabled at the window's end; the whole control disabled; the button at `xs`, `sm` and `md`.
doc.notFor:
- One date in a form: UiDatePicker.
- A day alone on a page: UiCalendar.
- Filters by other dimensions: UiFilter.
- A date in a column: UiDateCell.

props.name: current
props.doc: The value now.

props.name: previous
props.doc: The value it is compared with; `null`, missing, zero or not finite draws nothing.

props.name: invert
props.doc: Lower is better: a fall is `success`, growth `danger`.

props.name: label
props.doc: What it is compared with, shown after the badge: "vs August". A screen reader reads it as text after the verdict.

props.name: size
props.doc: `sm` on a chart card's title line, in a row or a cell; `md` beside a larger heading.

UiDelta.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A badge with the signed percent a value moved against the one before. Take it beside a number, beside a UiSparkline, or on a chart card's title line.

decisions.label: Counting
decisions.text: The library counts the percent against the size of `previous`, so a smaller loss reads as growth. No previous value, a zero one, or a change over 10 000% draws nothing.

decisions.label: Meaning
decisions.text: Growth is `success` and a fall is `danger`; `invert` swaps them when lower is better. The sign and a word for a screen reader ("better", "worse") carry the meaning, so it does not rest on color alone.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: On a UiChartCard's title line, beside a UiSparkline in a UiListItem row's `#actions`, and beside a number. On a chart card it reads the card's state as the chart does: while the card has no data (a first load, nothing to draw, a failed load) it draws nothing, and comes back with the data; a refresh keeps it. The badge never shrinks, so a long label beside it cannot cut off the sign or the digits; the label wraps when the host is narrow. The root is a `<span>`.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: no tab stop, no keys.
doc.reader:
- Value: the percent is hidden and a verdict is read in its place, the change and a word: "+12%, better" or "-8%, worse"; no change is read as 0% with no verdict.
- Label: the label after the badge is read as text, after the verdict.
doc.states: Growth (`success`), a fall (`danger`), the two swapped by `invert`, no change (`neutral`, 0%), and nothing drawn: no `previous`, a zero one, a change past 10 000%, or a chart card around it with no data. Two sizes, `sm` and `md`; no hover or focus state of its own.
doc.notFor:
- The trend itself: UiSparkline beside it.
- A state word: UiBadge.
- A count: UiCount.
- A share of a whole: UiProgress.

props.name: parts
props.doc: The parts, in the order they go round the ring and take the chart colors: the caller sorts. Past five, the fifth is "Other", the sum of the rest.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: What the chart shows, for a screen reader: "Spending by category, September".

props.name: totalLabel
props.doc: What the total in the middle counts: "Visitors"; "Total" when unset.

props.name: format
props.doc: How values read in the middle, the legend and the table; `money` writes the currency code after the digits, `1,234.00 USD`.

props.name: height
props.doc: The diameter of the ring in pixels.

props.name: legend
props.doc: The legend beside the ring, each part with its value and share.

UiDonutChart.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: The parts of a whole as a ring, with the total in the middle. Take it for a breakdown at one moment.

decisions.label: Parts
decisions.text: Each part is a `key`, a `label` and a `value`, drawn clockwise from twelve o'clock in the order given, so the caller sorts them. Colors follow that order, five at most: past five, the fifth part is "Other", the sum of the rest, in the gray used for leftovers.

decisions.label: Small values
decisions.text: A part that is not a positive number takes no room and shows 0%. A real part under half a percent shows "<1%" and an arc no thinner than the gap between arcs. A whole of nothing is the bare ring with a total of 0; no data at all is a dash.

decisions.label: Legend
decisions.text: The legend stands beside the ring, or under it when the host is narrow, and gives each part its value and its share.

decisions.label: Shown part
decisions.text: A shown part widens, and the middle says its name, value and share, sized to fit the hole; a figure too long for it is written short there ("5.3T"), whole in the legend and the table; a `format` function is asked for that short figure with `{ compact: true }`. The pointer over a part or its legend row shows that part, and a tap keeps it shown until a tap elsewhere.
In a card. In a UiChartCard it draws a pale ring on the card's first load and holds it still when there is nothing to draw. When the card bleeds it, the legend keeps to the gutter.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a UiChartCard's body, under its headline or in place of one, since the total is in the ring; or alone in a page section.

doc.keyboard:
The ring is one tab stop; an empty ring is no tab stop.
- `Tab`: reaches the ring; focus shows the first part.
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: step through the parts, stopping at the first and the last; each part is read out.
- `Home` `End`: jump to the first and the last part; each part is read out.
- `Alt` `Ctrl` `Meta`: a chord with them stays the browser's.
A tap on an arc or a legend row shows that part and hands the focus to the ring, so it stays until a tap elsewhere; the legend takes no focus of its own.
doc.reader:
- Ring: an image named by `ariaLabel`.
- Part: a part reached by the keyboard is read in a polite live region as "Groceries: 1,240, 34%".
- Table: a hidden table, captioned with the chart's name, holds every part with its value and share, each part folded into Other on a row of its own ("Other: Taxi"), and the total in its footer.
- Hidden: the middle of the ring and the legend, since the table says the same.
doc.states: Rest with the total in the middle, a part shown (it widens, the middle says its name, value and share, its legend row is marked), more than five parts with Other, a part of nothing at 0%, a real part under half a percent as "<1%", a whole of nothing as the bare ring and 0, no data at all as a dash; with and without the legend, which goes under the ring when the host is narrow. In a UiChartCard: its first load as a pale ring, nothing to draw held still, a refresh dimmed by the card.
doc.notFor:
- The parts period by period: UiBarChart with `stack`.
- One share of a whole: UiProgress.
- A flow over time: UiAreaChart.
- The card with its title and data states: UiChartCard around it.

props.name: title
props.doc: The panel's name, read first by a screen reader; required, a dialog without one is mute.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title, read right after it.

props.name: size
props.doc: The panel's width: `md` 512px, the default; `lg` 768px for what reads wide, a text or a code.

props.name: persistent
props.doc: Unsaved input: the backdrop and Escape are refused with a shake; the cross still closes.

props.name: submitting
props.doc: A request is out: every close is refused with a shake.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the panel is open (`v-model:open`); every way out sets it false and emits `close`.

events.name: update:open
events.doc: The new value of `open`, for `v-model:open`.

events.name: close
events.doc: The panel closed: the cross, the backdrop or Escape.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The body. It scrolls when long; the header and the footer stay. UiCard sections are parted by a line.

slots.name: description
slots.doc: The line under the title in your own markup, in place of `description`: a status mark, an id to copy. One line.

slots.name: actions
slots.doc: Icon buttons before the cross: open as a page, copy a link. Ghost UiIconButton.

slots.name: footer
slots.doc: Actions, sharing the footer's width in equal parts: the cancel is `secondary` and first, the main action last. Leave it out for a panel that applies at once.

UiDrawer.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A panel at the inline end of the screen, full height, over the page it came from. Take it for what is read or set beside a list without leaving it: the settings of a view, the details of a row.

decisions.label: Closing
decisions.text: `title` names the panel and `description` describes it. The backdrop, Escape and the cross close it. Escape works only while the panel is the top layer, so a confirm over it closes first. `persistent` guards unsaved input: the backdrop and Escape are refused with a shake, but the cross still closes, since pressing it is an explicit intent. `submitting` refuses every close while a request is out. These guard only the panel's own exits; `open` set to false from outside is for the host to guard.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.text: Attributes land on the dialog. The panel takes the full height at the inline end (the left in a right-to-left page), `md` 512px wide or `lg` 768px for what reads wide, and the whole width on a narrow screen. The page under it does not scroll; a long body scrolls between the header and the footer. The body is padded by `--space-drawer`; the header and the footer stand on it at the sides, so the title, the content and the footer's buttons share one edge. The footer's buttons share its width, as in a window. Cards in the body are its sections, flat, with a line between neighbors drawn by UiSeparator.

decisions.label: Kept pages
decisions.text: In a page that a `KeepAlive` keeps, a panel left open stays open when the page is deactivated: its layer, its Escape and its scroll lock go on over the next page. Close it (`open` false) when the route changes.

decisions.label: Header
decisions.text: The title is one line, cut when long and shown whole on hover. The line under it is `description`, or `#description` in your own markup: a status mark, an id to copy. `#actions` takes an icon button or two before the cross.

Changes at once. A panel whose controls apply as they change (a setting, a filter) has no footer: there is nothing to confirm, and the cross closes it. A footer is for a panel that sends something. A filter that covers the list it narrows is that case: its ticks wait in a draft, the footer's button says what applying will show ("Show 12 invoices"), and closing any other way drops the draft.

doc.keyboard:
The focus starts on the first field (a drawn select, date, switch, scale, drop zone or date range too), not on the cross. With no field it starts on a body longer than the panel, so the arrows scroll it at once, else on the panel itself.
- `Tab`: goes round inside the panel; a body longer than the panel is one of its stops.
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown` `PageUp` `PageDown` `Home` `End`: scroll that body once it holds the focus.
- `Escape`: closes the panel, only while it is the top layer; `persistent` answers it with a shake, and `submitting` refuses it.
On close the focus returns to where it was.
doc.reader:
- Window: a modal dialog (`aria-modal`) named by `title` (`aria-labelledby`) and described by the line under it.
- Cross: named "Close".
- Long body: a region named by the title, so the reader says what the keys scroll through.
- Refused close: a shake for the eye; the reader keeps the focus where it was and hears why, from a status region inside the drawer: input not saved, or a request still on its way.
doc.states: A settings panel that applies at once, with no footer; a read-only detail of rows; a panel with a footer; `persistent` shaking at the backdrop and Escape; a long body that scrolls between the header and the footer; a narrow screen, where the panel takes the whole width.
doc.notFor:
- A record to edit or create: UiCrudDrawer, with Save, loading and steps, built on this panel.
- A short task for the person's whole attention: UiModal.
- A small panel of controls under a button: UiPopover, with the page live.
- A second panel over this one: never; what opens from it is a UiModal for a short task, or a step of the same panel. Development warns when a drawer opens over another; a window or a question over it is fine.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The chosen files (`v-model`); always an array, one entry at most without `multiple`.

props.name: accept
props.doc: Accepted file types, native `accept` syntax: `image/*`, `.pdf,.docx`, `application/pdf`.

props.name: multiple
props.doc: Allows choosing several files; without it a new file replaces the old one.

props.name: maxFiles
props.doc: Maximum number of files, with `multiple`; ignored without it.

props.name: maxSize
props.doc: Maximum file size in bytes; also said under the main line unless `#hint` is given.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents choosing, dropping and removing.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control as invalid. Inside UiField, the error state sets this automatically.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name of the file input: a plain form submit sends the listed files.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id when standalone. Inside UiField, the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Name when there is no visible label; the browse button reads it followed by its own words, "Choose a file" or "Choose files".

props.name: progress
props.doc: Upload progress 0 to 100 shown with `busy`; `null` when unknown. The files listed when it reaches 100 are marked uploaded.

props.name: busy
props.doc: Work in progress: the rows not yet uploaded carry it, choosing and removing wait until it ends.

props.name: failed
props.doc: The last upload failed: the rows not uploaded say so, with this reason when it is a string, and offer Retry.

props.name: removable
props.doc: Whether the files can be removed. `auto`: yes, except the ones a finished upload marked.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The chosen files changed: added, replaced or removed.

events.name: retry
events.doc: Retry was pressed on a row a failed upload left: start the upload again.

events.name: reject
events.doc: Files refused on choose or drop, with the reason each (`FileRejection` from `types/ui`).

events.name: cancel
events.doc: The cross of an uploading row was pressed: stop the upload and end `busy`.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The main line: what to drop here.

slots.name: hint
slots.doc: The second line: the constraints, by default the size limit.

UiDropzone.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A form control for choosing files, by drag and drop or with a Browse button. It lists the chosen files, each with a remove button.

decisions.label: Model
decisions.text: `v-model` holds the chosen files and is always an array. The file input follows the model, a form reset included.

decisions.label: Limits
decisions.text: It accepts files by `accept`, `maxSize` (bytes) and `maxFiles`. A refused file is named with the reason, and `reject` is emitted.

decisions.label: Upload
decisions.text: The consumer uploads the files. Bind `progress` to show the upload and `busy` to block changes meanwhile. The rows not yet uploaded carry it: a spinner in the glyph's place, the percent in the size's, and the row filling behind its words with a quiet plate; with no percent the spinner turns and nothing fills. Browse holds, refusing, and the zone keeps its height. With no row to carry it, a bar runs along the bottom of the zone. The cross of an uploading row emits `cancel`: one upload runs for all the files it carries, so the app stops it and ends `busy`. An upload that ends at 100 with no `failed` marks its files uploaded and is announced, with the number it delivered; a later upload carries only the files not yet uploaded. A cancel the app has answered is announced too. A failure is `failed`, once `busy` ends, at any percent, 100 included: the rows the upload carried and did not deliver take an alert glyph, the reason (the string given, or Not uploaded) and Retry, which emits `retry`, and give up their size to make room; a folded list opens on them. A file added after it is a new file. Cancel and Retry ask once, until the app answers by changing `busy` or `failed`.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Inside a UiField it reads id, error and required; standalone it takes `invalid` and `ariaLabel`.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Listeners and `aria-*` land on the Browse button, other attributes on the file input that the form submits, `class` and `style` on the root. A native `required` keeps a form from sending with no file: Browse says it in words, and the form's check puts the focus on Browse, turns the zone invalid and says why under it, until a file comes.

decisions.label: Page drops
decisions.text: While it is mounted, a file dropped anywhere on the page outside a drop target does not open in the browser.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a form column under a UiField label, beside UiInput and UiTextarea, on a page, in a window or in a drawer's section.

doc.keyboard:
- `Tab`: reaches Browse, a native button; the file input itself is out of the tab order.
- `Enter` `Space`: on Browse, open the file dialog.
Each listed file's cross is a button. A remove from the keyboard keeps the focus inside the card:
on the row now in its place, the one above, or Browse. A folded list opens on its row, which is a button too. Dropping is for the pointer. `disabled` and `busy` block Browse and the remove crosses, and Browse keeps the focus while busy; an uploading row's cross cancels the upload, and a failed row's Retry is a button.
doc.reader:
- Browse: named by `ariaLabel` or the field's label, then by its own word; the file input under it is hidden from a screen reader.
- Description: the hint, the field's words, a required field (in words, since a button takes no `aria-required`) and the last refusal describe Browse; `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` on it.
- Status: a status region, in the DOM from the start, says what was added, removed and uploaded, that an upload is running, and why it failed.
- Refusal: an alert that names the files.
- Files: a list; an uploaded row says so in words, an uploading row's percent is a progress named by its file, and a failed row reads its reason after its name.
- Dragging: dragging over changes the words, not only the color.
doc.states: Rest, dragging over (the zone lights up and the words change), busy (each pending row a spinner, a filling plate, the percent and a cross that cancels; no fill while the percent is unknown; the layout kept), uploaded (a check on each row and on the folded line, no cross unless `removable` allows it), failed (an alert glyph, the reason with no size, Retry and the remove cross on each row the upload left), refused (the reason under the list, by name), with files (a row per file, folded past three with `multiple`), invalid (a red dashed border), and disabled (the plate, an inert button, no drop).
doc.notFor:
- Names typed or pasted one per line: UiListField.
- A typed value: UiInput.
- Files already on a record: UiListItem rows in a UiList, listed without choosing.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label above the control.

props.name: description
props.doc: Supporting text below the control: a format, a limit, a unit. Hidden while `error` is present.

props.name: error
props.doc: Error text below the control, one string; it marks the control invalid. Empty means valid. Read out when it appears.

props.name: required
props.doc: An asterisk after the label and `aria-required` on the control; in a group the legend says it once.

props.name: for
props.doc: Id of the control the label points to; the description and error ids derive from it. Generated when omitted.

props.name: group
props.doc: The control is a group of controls (radios, checkboxes): the field is a `fieldset`, the label its `legend`, and the group takes `labelId` for `aria-labelledby`. No `#meta`.

slots.name: default
slots.scope: { id?: string | undefined; labelId?: string | undefined; describedBy?: string | undefined; invalid: boolean; required: boolean; }
slots.doc: The control. A grani control connects through `useField`; a bare element takes the slot props.

slots.name: meta
slots.doc: Content at the right end of the label row, aligned with the label: a counter, a hint icon. Read with the control as a description.

UiField.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: The words around one form control: a label above, a description or an error below. Take it around a control that needs a label, and with `group` around a group of them.

decisions.label: Wiring
decisions.text: It connects the words to the control by id, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`. Grani's own controls read it by themselves; a bare element takes the slot props.

decisions.label: Groups
decisions.text: One field holds one control. A group of controls (radios, checkboxes, a UiButtonGroup row) takes `group`: the field becomes a fieldset named by its legend. A bare element in a group takes `labelId` for its `aria-labelledby`.

decisions.label: Required
decisions.text: Required shows a star. For a screen reader it is `aria-required` on a single control, or a word in the legend of a group, never on each control in it.

decisions.label: Disabled
decisions.text: The label mutes when the control inside is disabled. The field judges by the control, not by a button in `#meta`.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a form column, a window or a drawer body.

doc.keyboard: No keys of its own: Tab reaches the control inside it. The label is a native label: a click on it presses the control, as it puts the cursor in an input, so a select opens its list and a dropzone its file dialog.
doc.reader:
- Label: names the control, through `for` and the id, or through `labelId` for a control that cannot take a label.
- Description: the description, the error and `#meta` are read with the control (`aria-describedby`).
- Error: announced when it appears (`role="alert"`); it marks the control `aria-invalid`.
- Required: `required` is `aria-required` on a single control.
- Group: a `group` is a fieldset named by its legend, which says "required" once, in words, and never on each control.
doc.states: Rest, required (a star), with a description, in error (the error replaces the description; the label keeps its ink), disabled (the label mutes with the control), and `group`.
doc.notFor:
- Words on the left and the control on the right: UiListItem `as="label"`.
- A control that carries its own words: UiCheckbox, UiRadio or a UiSwitch with text keeps them in its slot.
- A title over a section of fields: UiHeader `legend`.

props.name: label
props.doc: The dimension, on the button: "Categories".

props.name: items
props.doc: One dimension: its options, as a select's (`SelectOption`).

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: One dimension: the chosen values.

props.name: count
props.doc: Several dimensions: how many of them have a value (status and channel is 2), for the button and Reset. Required with sections: without it the button shows nothing chosen and Reset stays held.

props.name: loading
props.doc: One dimension: the options are on their way. With none yet, rows in their shape; with options in view, they stay, held and dimmed. Several: each list takes its own.

props.name: align
props.doc: Which edge of the button the panel lines up with.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder, as the rest of the toolbar row. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

events.name: reset
events.doc: Reset was pressed; one dimension clears itself as well.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: One dimension: the chosen values.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: Several dimensions: UiCard sections without a title, each with a UiFilterList named by `ariaLabel`. Leave empty for one.

UiFilter.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A toolbar button that narrows a list by one dimension, or by several at once. Take it in a table toolbar, after the search.

decisions.label: Button
decisions.text: It shows a filter glyph, its label and a chevron. Once something is chosen, the count replaces the glyph in a slot of the same width, on a pale plate (up to 9, then "9+"), so the button keeps its size. Attributes land on the button.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.text: The panel under the button is a UiPopover. Reset stands in its footer under a line and is held while nothing is chosen, so the list above does not move under the pointer when the first box is ticked.

decisions.label: One dimension
decisions.text: Pass `items` and `v-model`; the filter counts and resets itself. A value counts once, however often `v-model` holds it. A value with no option among `items` (an option the server dropped, an old link) still counts and still filters: no row shows it, and Reset clears it.

decisions.label: Several dimensions
decisions.text: Put UiCard sections in the default slot, each with a UiFilterList and no title (a popover has no heading), and name each list by its `ariaLabel`; a line parts two neighbors, as in every overlay. The slot is read once, when the filter is made: the sections may change, but whether there are any may not. The lists mount only while the panel is open, so the host does the rest: it passes `count`, the number of dimensions with a value (status and channel make 2), holds each list's `loading`, and clears the lists on `reset`.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a table toolbar's `#start` (UiDataTable `#filters`), after the search and beside UiDateRange. Bind the slot's `size` on it.

decisions.label: Table
decisions.text: In UiDataTable's `#filters`, a choice the person changes (a tick, Only, Reset) starts the list on page one, and an empty list the filter narrowed offers "Reset filters"; a value the app sets moves no page.
Options that failed to load. The filter has no error of its own: the host sets `disabled` on it, so the button does not open, and says what failed where the list's own error stands.

doc.keyboard:
On the button:
- `Tab`: reaches it.
- `Enter` `Space`: open the panel; the focus goes to the list, or to its search when there are six options or more.
In the panel, where the list is one tab stop and Reset the next; from six options up the search takes the list's tab stop, and its cross is one more once it holds text:
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`: move the highlight.
- `Home` `End`: jump.
- `Enter` `Space`: tick.
- `A–Z`: jumps to the first option that starts with the letter.
- `Enter`: in the search, ticks the highlighted row (the first match once there is text) and does not submit a form around the filter.
- `Escape`: clears a search that has text and stays in the panel; otherwise closes the panel and returns the focus to the button, as a pick and close does.
doc.reader:
- Button: the label, "Categories", and, once something is chosen, the count in words after it (", 2 active"; the digit on the badge is hidden), with `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`. An `aria-label` of the caller's replaces the whole name, the count included.
- Panel: a dialog named by the button, the count in words included.
- List: one multi-select listbox named by the label, each option saying whether it is ticked; with sections, each list is named by its `ariaLabel`.
- Nothing found: a status region that is always present and is filled when the search leaves nothing.
doc.states: Rest, open, something chosen (the count in place of the glyph), Reset held while nothing is chosen, `loading`: a first load in the options' shape, a refresh with the rows held and dimmed; a search from six options and its empty result, several dimensions in sections; the button at `xs`, `sm` and `md`.
doc.notFor:
- A period: UiDateRange.
- The columns a table shows: UiTableColumns.
- One value in a form: UiSelect (`multiple` for several).
- Commands: UiMenu.

props.name: items
props.doc: The options, as a select's: a value (as in the URL) and a label; `disabled` shows one fixed as it is, `description` puts a word at its end.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The chosen values.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The options are being replaced: the rows are held.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: A name for the list; inside a UiCard with a title the title names it.

props.name: groups
props.doc: From six options, where the chosen stand first: a name over them and over the rest, a line between. Unset, they stand first without names.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The chosen values after a tick.

UiFilterList.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: The checklist of one filter dimension, where each tick applies at once. Take it inside the panel of a UiFilter or UiTableColumns.

decisions.label: Behavior
decisions.text: It follows UiSelect with `multiple`: a listbox of check-mark rows that runs edge to edge across the panel.

decisions.label: Search
decisions.text: With more than five options, a search row at the top narrows the list, by label and by an option's `keywords`, and says when nothing is found; it leaves the accents of Latin and Cyrillic letters out, so "munchen" finds München. Its cross clears the text. When the options drop to five or fewer the search leaves with its text, and the focus it held goes to the list; when they grow to six the focus the list held goes into the new search.

decisions.label: Chosen first
decisions.text: From six options, the ones chosen when the list opens stand at its top, in their own order, so a long list shows what is chosen without scrolling; the order stays while the list is open, so a tick never moves a row under the pointer. Five or fewer keep their order, which is read at a glance and may mean something. With `groups`, a name stands over the chosen and over the rest, a line between them, so the order explains itself.

decisions.label: Only
decisions.text: The highlighted row (the one under the pointer, the one a tap ticked, the one the keys lit) offers "Only", which keeps that option alone and unticks the others; a fixed option stays as it is. A list of one or two options offers none: a single tick does the same.

decisions.label: Options
decisions.text: `loading` with no options yet draws five rows in their shape, a box and a line; a list of up to five takes their place, a longer one adds its search above them, since the count is not known before they come. With options in view it is a refresh: they stay, held and dimmed. An option can be `disabled` (shown, but fixed as it is) and can carry a `description` at its end. The highlight stays on a row that is drawn when the options change. The chosen values should be among the options: a value with no option has no row.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: `class` and `style` land on the root, other attributes on the listbox.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In the panel of a UiPopover (UiFilter, UiTableColumns), alone or as a flat UiCard section. It needs a name: `ariaLabel`, or the title of its card; in development an unnamed list warns.

doc.keyboard:
The list is one tab stop, or its search is when it has one.
In the list:
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`: move the highlight.
- `Home` `End`: jump.
- `Enter` `Space`: tick the highlighted row; a `Space` after letters typed over the list belongs to the word.
- `Alt` `Enter`: keep the highlighted option alone, unticking the others.
- `A–Z`: jumps to the first option that starts with the letter; the same letter again goes on to the next, and letters typed together find a word.
In the search:
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`: move the highlight too.
- `Enter`: ticks the first match.
- `Alt` `Enter`: keeps the highlighted option alone.
- `Escape`: clears the text and stays in the panel.
- `Space` `A–Z`: type.
A press on a row ticks it without taking the focus.
doc.reader:
- List: a multi-select listbox (`aria-multiselectable`) named by `ariaLabel`, or by the title of the UiCard it stands in.
- Row: an option that says whether it is ticked (`aria-selected`), is held when `disabled` or `loading` (`aria-disabled`), and has its `description` read at its end.
- Highlight: `aria-activedescendant`, on the list or on the search, which controls the list (`aria-controls`).
- Only: the list and the search carry `aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+Enter"`; the word on the row is for the pointer and hidden.
- Nothing found: read from a status region that is always present and is filled when the search leaves no row.
- Loading: `aria-busy` on the root; the first load is said in the status region ("Loading options…"), its rows in the options' shape hidden.
doc.states: Rest, a highlighted row, ticked rows, a `disabled` row with its note, a first load in the options' shape, a refresh with every row held and dimmed, a search from six options, a narrowed list and its empty result; a list cut at five and a half rows that scrolls inside itself.
doc.notFor:
- The button and the panel around it: UiFilter or UiTableColumns.
- One value: UiSelect.
- A box or two in a form: UiCheckbox.
- A list of names that grows: UiListField.

props.name: title
props.doc: The name: the page's `h1`, or the section's title on its line.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under a page's title. A list page has none: the title names the list. A legend has none.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `page` is the first line of a page; `legend` names a section on the line above it.

slots.name: actions
slots.doc: Actions of the page, right of the title: a primary button, a menu. A legend holds none.

UiHeader.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: The name of a page (`page`) or of a section (`legend`). Take `page` once at the top of a page, `legend` over each part of a long form or a card.

decisions.label: Page
decisions.text: `page` is the `h1` at the top of UiAppShell's main area, with one line under it and the actions on the right, centered vertically on the title and its line together, as in UiListItem. It does not go inside a card, a modal or a drawer, which name themselves.

decisions.label: Legend
decisions.text: `legend` is a small title in capitals on a line, like a fieldset's legend, beside the fields or rows it names. In a surface, the line runs to its edges and the title sits on the gutter, where the fields start. In a body that runs edge to edge, it sits on its rows' text, with 16 above it when it comes first. First in a UiCrudDrawer section with `:divided="false"`, it stands in for the section's title. Under the title of a window, a drawer or a card, it is one level deeper (`h3` under their `h2`).

decisions.label: Spacing
decisions.text: A page header has no margin of its own: it and the page's content stand in a UiStack, `gap="title"`, 24 apart. A legend after other content opens a new section, so it adds 32px above itself. On top of the 16 gap of a `flex` or `grid` column, that puts it 48 below the content above, the step between blocks.

doc.keyboard:
Not interactive: the title takes no focus.
- `Tab`: reaches the controls in `#actions`, which keep their own tab stops, after the title in the reading order; a legend holds none.
doc.reader:
- Page: `page` is the one `h1` of the page, and its description is a paragraph under it.
- Legend: `legend` is a heading whose level follows its place: `h2` alone, the card's level in an untitled card, one level deeper under the title of a card, a window or a drawer.
- Lines: borders that say nothing.
doc.states: None of its own: a long title wraps, and the line keeps a stub beside it. In dev, a `page` header inside a card, a modal or a drawer warns, and a `legend` with a description or an action warns and drops them.
doc.notFor:
- The title of a card, a window or a drawer: UiCard, UiModal or UiDrawer carry it themselves (`title`).
- The name of a field: UiField.
- A strip of tabs over a block: UiTabs.
- A row with a thing at its end: UiListItem.

props.name: type
props.doc: Native type; `submit` sends the form the button sits in.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A Lucide icon component, e.g. `Pencil` from `@lucide/vue`.

props.name: variant
props.doc: Presentation: `primary` is the brand fill (the arrow of a split button), `outline` a white square with a border, `ghost` only the glyph until hovered.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Meaning of the glyph: gray, brand, or a dangerous action. `pressed` on overrides it with the brand frame.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: The accessible name, for a screen reader; no hint shows it, so wrap the button in UiTooltip where a sighted user needs it. Required: the button has no visible text.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Natively disabled: out of the Tab order, grayed; with `disabledReason`, focusable and saying why.

props.name: disabledReason
props.doc: Why it cannot be pressed now, while `disabled`, as UiButton's: it stays in the Tab order, refuses the press, and says the reason in a tooltip and as its description.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder: `xs` 28px for a dismiss in a corner, `sm` 36px, `md` 44px for forms. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

props.name: loading
props.doc: A request is running: spinner instead of the glyph, `aria-busy`, no clicks; focus stays, as in `UiButton`.

props.name: pressed
props.doc: A toggle (pin, bookmark), as UiButton's `pressed`: `aria-pressed`, and on, the brand frame and plate. Unset, it is no toggle. A `primary` square is never one.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: A glyph in place of `icon`; the button sizes it.

slots.name: trailing
slots.doc: A short tail after the glyph, such as a count; the square grows wider on one line.

UiIconButton.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A button for an action, drawn as a single Lucide glyph in a square target.

decisions.label: Look
decisions.text: The button sizes the glyph; `variant` is the presentation, `tone` the meaning.

decisions.label: Name
decisions.text: Its name is `ariaLabel`, a required prop rather than the native attribute, since the button has no text to be named by; an empty one warns in dev. No hint shows the name: where a sighted user needs it, wrap the button in a UiTooltip, which then does not read the name twice.

decisions.label: Toggle
decisions.text: `pressed` makes it a toggle, as on UiButton: `aria-pressed`, the brand frame and plate, and the system highlight under forced colors. A `primary` square is never a toggle.

decisions.label: Split
decisions.text: Last in a row of UiButtonGroup, right after a button with text, it is the arrow of a split button, `primary` or `outline`: the group draws it narrower than a square (28 wide at `sm`), its glyph unchanged, so it reads as a part of the button beside it. A `#trailing` tail keeps its pill.

decisions.label: Tail
decisions.text: A `#trailing` tail (a count) keeps its width while loading.

decisions.label: Disabled
