decisions.text: As on UiButton: `disabled` alone takes no focus and says nothing; with `disabledReason` the square keeps the focus, refuses the press, and says why in a tooltip and as its description ("Paid invoices cannot be deleted"). A UiTooltip around it for its name keeps naming it while it works; while it is off, the reason shows instead.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits in the header of a modal or a drawer (the close cross and the record arrows), in a table row's actions, in a capsule's `#end` beside the value (a clear button), on a pager and as a calendar's arrows, in a toast's corner, in a UiListItem's `#actions`, and as the trigger of a popover or a menu. A `primary` one is the arrow of a split button, beside a primary UiButton in a UiButtonGroup. Its neighbors are UiButton (with text) and UiCopyButton, whose glyph-only form is one of these.

doc.keyboard:
A native button.
- `Tab`: reaches it; `disabled` takes no focus, unless it has a `disabledReason`.
- `Enter` `Space`: press it. `loading` refuses the press before your handler sees it, and keeps the focus. A held Enter is one press: its repeats press nothing.
`type="submit"` sends the form it sits in.
doc.reader:
- Name: `ariaLabel`, which is required; the glyph is hidden (`aria-hidden`).
- Loading: says busy (`aria-busy`) and disabled (`aria-disabled`) while the button keeps its name.
- Pressed: `pressed` is `aria-pressed`, only on a toggle.
- Disabled with a reason: `aria-disabled`, and the reason is its description, read once.
- Hint: none shows the name; a UiTooltip you wrap around it shows it to the eye, and it is not read twice.
doc.states: Rest; hover; focus (a `danger` one keeps the red ring); pressed (the brand frame and plate, the system highlight under forced colors); loading (a spinner one step larger than the glyph, the color kept, the width kept with a `#trailing` tail); disabled (the glyph grayed, the shape kept), with a reason the focus kept and the hint shown. `primary`, `outline` and `ghost` in `neutral`, `brand` and `danger`; `xs`, `sm` and `md`; with a tail, a pill that keeps its height; in both themes.
doc.notFor:
- Text: UiButton.
- Copying a value: UiCopyButton.
- A choice among options: UiRadioGroup `segmented`.
- A primary square as a toggle: never; it is the arrow of a split button in UiButtonGroup.

props.name: count
props.doc: The number on the corner; `0` hides the mark unless `dot` is set.

props.name: max
props.doc: The largest count shown as is; above it the mark reads `99+`.

props.name: dot
props.doc: A dot instead of a number: online, unsaved, something new.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Meaning of the mark: `danger` for unread by default, `success` for online.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Which corner of the element holds the mark.

props.name: size
props.doc: `sm` on an `xs` icon button or a small avatar, `md` on an `sm` or `md` icon button.

props.name: pulse
props.doc: A ring that keeps expanding: the state is live. Stops under reduced motion.

props.name: round
props.doc: The element is a circle (an avatar, as wide as it is tall): the mark sits on its edge, not on the corner of its box.

slots.name: default
slots.scope: { count: number; text: string; visible: boolean; }
slots.doc: The element that carries the mark: an icon button, an avatar. Gets the count to name the state from.

UiIndicator.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A count or a dot on the corner of what it marks. Take it on an icon button, an avatar (`round`) or a place's icon in UiAppShell's collapsed rail when something waits there; a number beside a label is UiCount.

decisions.label: Mark
decisions.text: The mark is a UiCount and follows its rules: a fraction is rounded down, an infinite count shows `{max}+`, and a bad one shows nothing. A ring in the surface color, or in `--ui-indicator-ring`, cuts it out from what it sits on.

decisions.label: Overflow
decisions.text: Half of the mark stands outside the element, so a clipping ancestor crops it, and a UiButtonGroup does not join it. The root is a `<span>`.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: the mark takes no focus and no pointer; the element in the slot keeps its own tab stop.
doc.reader:
- Mark: hidden (`aria-hidden`).
- Name: the host names the state on the element it marks, using the slot's `{ count, text, visible }`: "Inbox, 99+", or "new" while a dot is visible.
- Change: not announced.
doc.states: Hidden at `0` unless `dot`; a count, `{max}+` above `max`; a dot; `pulse`, a ring in the tone that keeps expanding and stops under reduced motion; `round`, on the edge of a circle; the four corners, mirrored in RTL; `sm` and `md`; the ring of the surface or of `--ui-indicator-ring`. A bad count hides the mark and warns in dev.
doc.notFor:
- A number beside a label: UiCount.
- A label: UiBadge.
- A status in a row of a table: UiBadge `inline`.

props.name: type
props.doc: Native type, `text` by default. A number stays `text` with `numeric`: `type="number"` has its own spinner and rejects a comma.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name for forms.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id when standalone. Inside UiField the field's id takes precedence, so the label always points at the control.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Hint shown while empty. Not a replacement for a label.

props.name: autocomplete
props.doc: Browser autofill hint: `email`, `current-password`.

props.name: inputmode
props.doc: Keyboard to show on a phone.

props.name: maxlength
props.doc: Maximum number of characters.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: Prevents editing while keeping the control focusable: something else sets the value.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents input and interaction.

props.name: loading
props.doc: A request for this value is on its way, as a search: a spinner at the end in the cross's place, and clearing waits.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control invalid: red border and halo. Inside UiField the error sets this.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: a value is needed, said to a reader and to a form (native `required`). Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible label. A prop, not `aria-label`: the root is the capsule, the name belongs to the control.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

props.name: passwordVisible
props.doc: Whether a `password` shows its characters (`v-model:passwordVisible`). Uncontrolled when omitted: the eye keeps the state.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The value as text (`v-model`): empty is `''`, or `null` with `numeric`. A number is plain text (`1234.5`) parsed by its owner on use.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `capsule` (the default) is the text field. `bare` has no capsule: the field is a window's header, edge to edge, larger type (a search over its results); the window draws the line under it. Text or search only, never `numeric`: no ring, no halo, `size` has no say.

props.name: numeric
props.doc: A number as text: tabular monospaced digits, decimal keyboard, a comma becomes a point, and with an `#end` unit the value sizes to its content so the unit sits right after it.

props.name: step
props.doc: With `numeric`: arrows in the capsule and ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the value by this much (`0.1` for money, `1` for pieces). A value written more precisely moves by its own last digit.

props.name: min
props.doc: With `numeric`: the lowest value the arrows reach. Typing is not clamped: the form validates.

props.name: max
props.doc: With `numeric`: the highest value the arrows reach.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The value changed: text, `''` when emptied, or with `numeric` the number as text and `null` when emptied.

events.name: update:passwordVisible
events.doc: The eye was toggled.

events.name: unsure
events.doc: With `numeric`: `true` while the field holds text the locale cannot read for sure, which the model carries as written; `false` when it does not. Said on mount, then on every change, right after the model it concerns.

slots.name: start
slots.doc: Addons before the value: a unit, an icon, a text.

slots.name: end
slots.doc: Addons after the value: a unit, a counter, a button.

UiInput.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A one-line text field in a capsule. Take it for text, a number or a password, with addons at either end.

decisions.label: Capsule
decisions.text: The capsule carries the border, background, height and focus ring. `#start` and `#end` hold addons: a unit, an icon, a button, a counter. Addons share the capsule but are not part of the value. A unit is its short form, two or three letters (`kg`, `pcs`), not a word. A button last in `#end` sits as close to the edge as the password eye does.

decisions.label: Password
decisions.text: A `password` gets an eye that shows the characters; `v-model:passwordVisible` drives it from outside. The eye keeps the focus in the value. It never offers the browser's own spellcheck, autocapitalize or autocorrect, shown or hidden, so a password never reaches a server's suggestions. To generate and copy a password, take UiPasswordField.

decisions.label: Numbers
decisions.text: A number is `numeric`, never `type="number"`: that type rejects the comma of a Russian keyboard and empties the field. With `step` the field draws its own arrows and moves by the step on ArrowUp and ArrowDown, the caret kept where it was and the digits the value was written with (`10.99` goes to `11.00`). `min` and `max` bound the arrows, not the typing; an arrow stops at its bound, one off the step's grid too. A number with a unit in `#end` is as wide as its digits, the unit after them; give it a `placeholder` (`0.00`), or an empty field shows the unit alone at the start.

TypeScript checks against `numeric` written as it is: `bare` with it does not compile, and a field that turns numeric at run time is two tags, one under `v-if` and one under `v-else`: `:numeric="flag"` does not compile.

decisions.label: Bare
decisions.text: `variant="bare"` drops the capsule: for a field in a window's header, such as a search over its results in UiModal's `#header`.

decisions.label: Search
decisions.text: A `search` with text shows a cross that clears it; Escape clears it too. With `loading` (its results on their way) the cross turns into its spinner, the same button, so a focus on it stays, and clearing waits: a press and an Escape clear nothing then.

decisions.label: Value
decisions.text: The value is text, numbers included: the owner parses it when it uses it, and a number passed in is read as its text. Empty follows the library's one rule: a text field is empty at `''`; a `numeric` one holds a number, so empty is `null`, and it sends `null` when emptied. The field shows the model: when the owner refuses a change, or a form resets, it goes back to it. A native form gets a number as the field shows it, `12,5` in a locale with a decimal comma.

decisions.label: Locale
decisions.text: A number is read in the app's locale: "1 234,50" pasted in a Russian app is 1234.50, "1,234" is a thousand in English, and so is "1.234" in German. Text the locale cannot read for sure ("1,23" in English), or with no digit at all, is kept as written, reaches the model as it is and is marked invalid on blur. The model cannot tell such text from a number ("2,500" and an unsure "2.500" are both `2.500` in Russian), so the field says it: `unsure` is `true` while it holds such text, and the app refuses to save then.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Standalone it takes `invalid` and `ariaLabel`; inside UiField it reads id, error and required from the field.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes and listeners land on the input (`pattern`, `autocapitalize`, `@blur`); `class` and `style` on the capsule. A change the field makes itself (an arrow, the cross, Escape) comes through `update:modelValue` alone, not a DOM `input` event.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In UiField; joined with a button in UiButtonGroup (a search); inside UiPasswordField; as the search of UiTableToolbar; as the count of UiStepper, between its minus and plus; and in a form column beside UiTextarea, UiSelect and UiDatePicker.

doc.keyboard:
A native text field.
- `Tab`: reaches it; a button in `#end`, or the cross of a search with text, comes next, one step later, since the number arrows are out of the tab order.
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown`: with `numeric` and `step`, move the value by the step without moving the caret, and stop at `min` and `max`; with Shift, Alt, Ctrl or Cmd held they are the browser's.
- `Escape`: in a `search` with text, clears it and goes no further; while its results are on their way it clears nothing and still goes no further; in an empty one it passes on.
Keys do nothing while an IME composes. The eye and the arrows keep the focus and the caret in the value.
doc.reader:
- Field: a text box named by `ariaLabel` or the field's label, never by the placeholder. A field with no name warns in dev.
- Errors: `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`; inside UiField the description and the error are read with it, and `aria-required` says it is required.
- Eye: a toggle button with its own name and `aria-pressed`.
- Arrows: named by the field, "Increase Price" and "Decrease Price".
- Search cross: has a name.
- Loading: the field and the cross say busy (`aria-busy`); in a search a status region in the capsule, there from the start, says "Searching".
doc.states: Rest, hover, focus (the capsule draws the ring), disabled (its own plate), readonly (looks ordinary, cannot be edited), invalid (red border and halo; disabled wins over it), with addons, `numeric` with its arrows, `password` shown or hidden, a `search` with its cross, a `search` with `loading` (the spinner in the cross's place), and `bare` with no capsule.
doc.notFor:
- Several lines: UiTextarea.
- A pick from a list: UiSelect.
- A day: UiDatePicker.
- A count of things, with minus and plus: UiStepper.
- A mark from 1 to N: UiScaleInput.
- A new password with generate and copy: UiPasswordField.
- A one-time code: UiCodeInput.

props.name: to
props.doc: A route or a URL; an absolute address is external, `mailto:` and `tel:` are not. `javascript:` and `data:` are refused: the text shows with no link.

props.name: tone
props.doc: `brand` is the link color; `info` the signal blue, a link to look at; `neutral` a quiet link in a caption.

props.name: target
props.doc: `_blank` or `_self` overrides the default: a new tab for an external address only.

props.name: rel
props.doc: Replaces the default `noreferrer`, e.g. `nofollow`, `sponsored`, `ugc`; `noopener` stays on a new tab.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The link text.

UiLink.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A link inside text, underlined at rest. Take it for a link in prose, a caption or a note.

decisions.label: Underline
decisions.text: The underline tells the link apart from the words around it, since its color alone may not.

decisions.label: New tab
decisions.text: Another site (or `target="_blank"`) opens in a new tab and says so: an arrow for the eye, a phrase for a screen reader.

decisions.label: Scripts
decisions.text: An address that runs script (`javascript:`, `data:`) is not linked: the text stays, in the ink of the words around it, with no line and no href, and dev warns. So is no address at all, an empty `to` or one the app's data left out (`null`) or holds as no string (a number): a menu built from data renders, on a server too, with that item as text. A link focused when its address goes away drops the focus with it, as any element that leaves.

decisions.label: Router
decisions.text: A path of the app (`/records/7`, `/people/john.doe`) goes through the link component given to `createGrani({ link })`, else the app's `RouterLink`, else a plain anchor; another site, `mailto:`, `tel:` and a file the server hands out (`/llms.txt`, `/report.pdf`) are plain anchors. An address padded with spaces is read trimmed.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits in prose, a caption, a card's footer note, or a header beside the title. Its neighbors are UiButton `to` (an action) and UiListItem `to` (a whole row as the link), and it never goes inside either: a link in a link warns in dev.

decisions.label: Wrapping
decisions.text: It never wraps, so a name or a command reads as one piece. A link is a few words: a long one is written shorter, not broken across lines.

doc.keyboard:
An anchor.
- `Tab`: reaches it; a refused address (`javascript:`, `data:`) or none is plain text and takes no focus.
- `Enter`: follows it; `Space` does not, as in the browser.
doc.reader:
- Name: the text.
- New tab: another site, or `target="_blank"`, adds "opens in a new tab" after the text, where the eye sees an arrow, which is hidden. The notice follows the real target, so a `mailto:` or `tel:` link says nothing.
- Attributes: native ones (`aria-current`, `hreflang`, `lang`, `title`) reach the anchor. An `aria-label` replaces the name and the notice with it: write "opens in a new tab" into it.
doc.states: Rest, underlined in the tone's ink (`brand`, `info`, `neutral`); hover, in the hover ink; focus. External with the arrow; internal, mail and phone without it. Always on one line. No disabled state: a refused or missing address shows as text.
doc.notFor:
- An action: UiButton, with `to` when it looks like a button.
- A whole row as the link: UiListItem `to`.
- A link inside either: never; a link in a link (UiListItem or UiButton with `to`) warns in dev.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The rows: UiListItem, a UiReveal around one, a notice. Each child is one item of the list.

UiList.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: Rows one under another, divided by lines. Take it around UiListItem rows wherever they stand in a column; a card of rows is UiCard `:padded="false"` around a UiList.

decisions.label: Lines
decisions.text: The list divides its rows: a line stands above every row that follows a row, or the block a row opened (UiReveal), drawn over the row's own air, so a row is one height wherever it stands. A notice is a row too, with the lines of any row; a framed row (`outline`, `muted`) stands alone, with no line above it or after it.

decisions.label: Edges
decisions.text: In a surface with a gutter (a padded card, a window, a drawer's section) the list runs its rows edge to edge, through the gutter, and their text stays on it. Standing first or last in a drawer's section, its own child and not inside a block of the section's, it reaches the section's line: the section says which of its children is first and last, so a section of rows alone is a list between two lines, and a list wrapped in a block after a paragraph keeps its place. Last in a padded card's body, the card drops its bottom gutter under it. In a card without padding the rows keep the card's inset.

decisions.label: Items
decisions.text: Every child is an item of the list: a row, a UiReveal with its row and its block, a notice. A notice stands among the rows as a row of the list, not as the card it is alone: the rows' edges, height and lines, its tone a 3px edge at the start along the whole row, clipped by the card's corners when it comes first or last; `variant="soft"` on it fills the row with its tone's pale plate as well. A child that is not a row (a separator, a plain block) stands as an item too, with no line above or after it.

doc.keyboard: Nothing of its own: a link or a command row is a tab stop, a label row reaches its control, a plain row takes no focus.
doc.reader: - List: `role="list"`, kept where a style drops a list's semantics, each child a list item, so a screen reader says how many rows there are and which one it is on.
doc.states: Rows of plain text, links, fields and commands; a notice among them, plain or `soft`; a long list in a card; a list at the top or the bottom of a drawer's section, line to line; on a narrow screen the rows wrap their text and keep their actions beside it.
doc.notFor:
- A list in a panel: the panel draws it itself, as a UiSelect or a UiMenu does.
- A table of columns: UiTable.
- A list that grows from its last row: UiListField over a UiList.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: The hint in the empty field: "Find or add a subcategory". Defaults to "Find or add…".

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: The field's name for a screen reader; defaults to the placeholder.

props.name: empty
props.doc: The line of an empty list; defaults to "Nothing here yet: type a name and press Enter".

props.name: search
props.doc: Typing filters the list and Enter opens the first match. Off, the field only adds: a short list inside a form, where every row is in view.

props.name: existing
props.doc: The names in the list: an exact one, in any case, is found, not offered again.

props.name: split
props.doc: `lines`: a pasted list splits by line. `lists`: also by commas and semicolons, typed or pasted.

props.name: fix
props.doc: Tidies an item on its way in: `(s) => s.toLowerCase()`. A change is named under the field.

props.name: check
props.doc: Why an item cannot be, in the product's words, or nothing when it can.

props.name: limit
props.doc: The most the list holds, counted from `existing`: full, the field is gone.

props.name: onAdd
props.doc: “Add …”, Enter or a pasted list (`@add`): the items, tidied, checked, without repeats. Return the request's promise to hold the field; a rejection gives the text back. Nothing returned, the field is not held. Put the new names into `existing` before the promise settles: repeats and `limit` are counted from it.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Nothing can be typed, added or cleared: the field, Add and the cross are held, on the disabled plate.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id of the input when standalone. Inside UiField the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the field's row, as a list row's: 44 px at `xs` and `sm`, 56 at `md`. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

props.name: query
props.doc: The text in the field (`v-model:query`): what the list is filtered by, and what “Add …” adds.

events.name: update:query
events.doc: The new value of `query`, for `v-model:query`.

events.name: taken
events.doc: A repeat was refused: the name as the list has it, to point at its row.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The rows that match `query`, UiListItem with `highlight`; `added` are the names added here, newest first, to put on top.

UiListField.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: One field that searches a UiList of UiListItem rows and adds to it. Take it when a list level holds only a list, such as a step of UiCrudDrawer.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.text: It is a behavior laid over a UiList of UiListItem rows. The field is the first row of a framed card, and the rows run under it, in a UiList the field draws round the slot.

decisions.label: Search
decisions.text: Typing filters. The default slot gets the `query` (and the names `added` here, to put on top) and draws the matching rows, each with UiListItem `highlight`, so the typed letters show why a row was found. The row named exactly as typed, else the first match, is ready for Enter and marked with a band. Enter opens a row that is a button or a link; under plain rows it adds the text, so a name added by mistake is offered back with Undo in a toast, by the app.

decisions.label: Adding
decisions.text: When no name in `existing` matches the text exactly, an "Add ↵" button stands at the field's end beside the cross (a screen reader hears "Add …" with the name), and Enter adds the text. A pasted column adds every line.

decisions.label: Full list
decisions.text: A full list hides the field and shows a line that says so; the focus moves to that line.

decisions.label: Items
decisions.text: Every item goes through `useAddItems` (`split`, `fix`, `check`, `limit`, and a request that gives the text back when it fails), and a line under the field says what happened. The items leave by `@add`, as UiLog's older events come by `@more`: the handler sends them, and until the promise it returns settles a second Enter or Add sends nothing; the person can keep typing. A promise that never settles holds the field until it unmounts: give the request a timeout.

decisions.label: Glyph
decisions.text: The icon at the start of the field shows its state: a search icon at rest, a spinner while an item is being added, and an alert after a failure or a bad item, until the text changes. A repeat only gets the line.

decisions.label: Add only
decisions.text: With `search` off the field only adds: a plus replaces the search icon, Enter adds, and the list is not filtered. Take it for a short list inside a form, with every row in view.

decisions.label: Value
decisions.text: The list's rows are the value, and they belong to the caller: it draws them in the slot, names them in `existing` and adds to them in `@add`, after its request. Repeats and `limit` are counted from `existing`, so it holds the new names by the time the request's promise settles; a name put there later can be added twice. The component holds no list of its own, so it takes no `v-model` of one. The field's text is a draft, `v-model:query`, not a form value; it follows its model after the owner refuses a change and after a form reset. A draft refused by `check` reads as invalid to a screen reader, yet a Save around it goes: it is not the form's to fix.

decisions.label: Draft
decisions.text: The text goes with its level: in UiCrudDrawer, ‹ and the backdrop step up and drop it. To keep it, hold the level `persistent` while `query` is not empty: ‹ and the backdrop shake instead until the text is added or cleared. The footer's Back and the cross are the explicit ways out, and they still leave.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Inside `UiField group` the legend names it once and says "required" once (the draft itself is never required); the field's description and error describe it. A plain UiField label points at its input, and a required one marks it `aria-required`.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: `disabled` blocks the field, Add and the cross. Caller attributes land on the input, and ours only where we have one. `required` and `name` would be the draft's: the browser would refuse an empty draft and post it. Leave them off; a required list is UiField's.

doc.keyboard:
Typing filters.
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`: move the band over the matches, past the last one to "Add ↵", and round again, while the cursor stays in the field; with Shift, Alt, Ctrl or Cmd held they are the browser's.
- `Enter`: opens the row under the band, or adds the typed text when no row is there; never submits the form around it.
- `Cmd+Enter` `Ctrl+Enter`: the form's, as in any field: a record's form around the field saves, without the draft.
- `Escape`: empties the field, or clears the line under it, and stops there; on an empty field it passes to the host.
The cross and Add keep the focus in the field, from the keyboard too. When a row with the focus in it is removed, the focus moves to its neighbor; when the list fills up under the focus, the focus moves to the line that says so.
doc.reader:
- Field: named by `ariaLabel`, else by the placeholder, by a plain UiField's label or by a group's legend.
- Line under it: what happened to an item, or a full list; an alert that describes the field.
- Enter hint: a live region says what `Enter` would do: open the named row, add the typed name, or that an item is on its way.
- Buttons: "Add" is named with the typed name, and the cross has a name.
- Errors: inside UiField the description and the error describe it, and a refused item sets `aria-invalid`.
doc.states: At rest with a search icon (a plus with `search` off), typing with the band on the first match and "Add ↵" at the end, adding (a spinner; Enter waits, typing goes on), refused (an alert icon and the line, until the text changes), a repeat (the line only), empty (a line saying how to start), nothing matching ("Add ↵" alone), full (no field, the line says so), and disabled (the field and the cross blocked, on the plate, no Add).
doc.notFor:
- A list with a toolbar and pages: UiDataTable.
- Picks from a fixed set: UiSelect `multiple`.
- One text value: UiInput.
- Rows that nobody adds here: UiListItem rows in a UiList.

props.name: title
props.doc: The primary line of text.

props.name: description
props.doc: Supporting text below the title.

props.name: variant
props.doc:
`plain` for a row among rows, `outline` for a standalone row, `muted` for a filled surface.
On a notice in a UiList, `soft` fills the row with its tone's pale plate as well; `plain` keeps the surface. Alone the notice is its card either way.

props.name: size
props.doc: `md` for pages, `sm` for drawers and dense lists. Unset: the host's (a sidebar says `sm`), else `md`. Rows keep their own scale, 44 at `sm` and 56 at `md`; the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`) does not move them.

props.name: highlight
props.doc: Letters of the title to mark, in any case: the query of a search over the rows. The first match is marked.

props.name: lit
props.doc: A moment of brand color: the row just came, or a refused repeat points at it. Set it, clear it after a second.

props.name: as
props.doc: The root element: `label` for a field, `button` for a command; a plain row is a `div`.

props.name: to
props.doc: A route or URL. Makes the whole row a link; `actions` then hold no controls. A disabled one is a disabled button, not a link; `javascript:` and `data:` are refused, as on UiLink.

props.name: target
props.doc: With `to`: `_blank` or `_self` decides the tab; unset, a new tab for an absolute address only.

props.name: rel
props.doc: With `to`: replaces the default `noreferrer` (`nofollow`, `sponsored`); `noopener` stays on a new tab.

props.name: step
props.doc: With `as="button"`: the row goes one level in, a step of a drawer; a chevron at the end.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: A command or link row that cannot be taken now: no rights, nothing to do.

props.name: loading
props.doc: A command or link row is running: a spinner in place of the glyph, clicks refused, focus kept.

props.name: error
props.doc: With `as="label"`: an error in place of the description, read with the control and marking it invalid.

props.name: required
props.doc: With `as="label"`: an asterisk after the title and `aria-required` on the control.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Meaning. On a plain row a notice: alone a white card whose start edge is in the tone, in a UiList a row with the tone's edge, read as a status. On a command or link row the ink alone: `danger` for an irreversible action, `brand` for the one that makes something new (“Add …”).

events.name: click
events.doc: The row was clicked; a command row is silent while `loading` or `disabled`.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: Own text in place of `title` and `description`, when two lines are not enough. On a label row it names nothing: give the control its own name.

slots.name: media
slots.doc: Content on the left: a glyph, an avatar or an image. The caller sizes avatars and images; glyphs are 20px.

slots.name: actions
slots.doc: Controls on the right: a button, a badge, a switch. Passive content only on a link or a command row (`to`, `as="button"`): a control there is a control inside a control, and warns.

UiListItem.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: One row, a title and its text on the left and a thing on the right. Take it for every row: a plain one, a link, a setting, a command, a notice; rows one under another stand in a UiList.

decisions.label: Anatomy
decisions.text: It is the library's one row: media, text and actions, centered on the row. A component with text on the left and a thing on the right stands on a UiListItem and does not draw its own row.

decisions.label: Modes
decisions.text: A row is one of four, told apart by its props and checked by TypeScript: a plain row; a link (`to`); a field (`as="label"`); a command (`as="button"`, with `step`, `loading` and `tone="danger"`). A prop of another mode is a type error, such as `step` on a link or `error` on a command.

decisions.label: Link
decisions.text: With `to`, the whole row is a link ending in a chevron that slides on hover; a page on another site opens in a new tab and ends in an arrow instead, as with UiLink. A link holds no interactive actions, a badge or a text at most, because a button inside a link makes two controls in one.

decisions.label: Lines
decisions.text: A row draws no line of its own: the UiList it stands in divides its rows, so a card of rows is UiCard `:padded="false"` around a UiList.

decisions.label: Notice
decisions.text: With `tone` a plain row is a notice, read as a status, with the glyph of its tone first (`#media` gives another) and its tone said to a screen reader; `xs` outline buttons go in `#actions`. It replaces a callout: a title, text, an action. Alone (over a form, in a toast) it is drawn like a toast: a white card whose start edge is in the tone. In a UiList it is a row of the list: the rows' edges, height and lines, no card of its own, and the tone's 3px edge at the start along the whole row; `variant="soft"` fills that row with the tone's pale plate as well, as on a soft badge.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: `as="label"` makes the row a field: the title names the one control in `#actions` (a UiSwitch, a UiCheckbox, a UiSelect), the description or `error` describes it, `required` marks it, and a click anywhere on the row reaches it. A setting row is this, with a UiSwitch in `#actions`.

decisions.label: Command
decisions.text: `as="button"` makes the row a command: the whole row is a button, with a status glyph in `#actions` (a check, a trash can). `loading` puts a spinner in the glyph's place and refuses clicks while the focus stays. `tone="danger"` is the red ink of a command that cannot be undone. `step` ends the row in a chevron, as on a link: the row goes one level in, to a step of UiCrudDrawer (Rules, Move to), with a count or a word in `#actions`. Such rows one after another form the action block of a record. In UiMenu a command row is an item of the menu, drawn by the menu as a row of its panel list.

decisions.label: Lit
decisions.text: `lit` lights a row for a moment: the one UiListField just added, or the one a refused repeat points at.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It stands in a UiList in a card, in a drawer section, in a dropzone's file list; alone in a toast and in a table's error row and bulk bar. Its neighbors are UiField (a label above its control) and UiButton. A link or a command row holds no control in `#actions`, and warns if it does. The chevron and the text follow the reading direction.

decisions.label: Highlight
decisions.text: `highlight` marks the letters a search found.

doc.keyboard:
A plain row takes no focus; the controls in `#actions` do.
With `to`, the whole row is a link:
- `Enter`: follows it.
With `as="button"`, a native button:
- `Enter` `Space`: press it; `loading` or `disabled` refuses the press in the capture phase, before the router sees it, keeping the focus while loading. A held Enter is one press: its repeats press nothing.
`as="label"` reaches its one control with a click anywhere on the row; the control keeps its own keys.
doc.reader:
- Row: the title, then the description; `highlight` marks letters for the eye only.
- Label row: names its control by the title (`aria-labelledby`), describes it by the description or the error (`aria-describedby`), and marks it `aria-invalid` and `aria-required`; the error is an alert.
- Notice: a `status` that says its tone in words before the title. It appears with its words, which is often not read out; what must be heard goes through a toast (UiToaster).
- Link: to another site, says it opens a new tab.
- Command: says busy while loading (`aria-busy`, `aria-disabled`).
- Glyphs: the chevron and the tone glyph are hidden.
- In a list: in a UiList it is a list item.
doc.states: Rest; hover and focus as a band on a link or a command; `disabled`, in the disabled ink and cursor, not faded; `loading`, a spinner in place of the glyph, with the ink kept; `tone` as the ink of a command (`danger` red, `brand` for the one that creates something new), or as a notice on a plain row (a card alone, a row with the tone's edge in a list, `soft` filled there); `lit`, a moment of brand color; a label row whose control is disabled, with the title muted; `step`, a chevron at the end. A row of a list is 44px tall at `sm` and 56px at `md`: a second line of text grows it, a control in `#actions` does not (up to the row's own height, 44 and 56).
doc.notFor:
- A field with its label above its control: UiField.
- An action on its own: UiButton.
- A list of names that grows from its last row: UiListField.
- A message about a request: a toast through UiToaster.
- Why a list is empty: UiNoData.

props.name: items
props.doc: The events, newest first.

props.name: node
props.doc: `dot`: a dot in the event's tone. `actor`: the face of who did it, the system a plate with a glyph.

props.name: filters
props.doc: Kinds to choose from over the list, matched against each event's `kind`; "All" comes first. Up to three stand as segments, more go into a select.

props.name: hasMore
props.doc: Older events exist: the list ends in "Load older events", which calls `@more`.

props.name: onMore
props.doc: "Load older events" (`@more`): load the events before the last one. Return a promise to hold the button while it runs and to say a failure; nothing returned, it is not held.

props.name: empty
props.doc: The line when there are none; defaults to "No activity yet".

props.name: loading
props.doc: The first load is on its way: rows in the shape of events, nothing else.

props.name: failed
props.doc: The first load failed: says so, with Retry.

props.name: onRetry
props.doc: Retry (`@retry`): load the history again. Return a promise to hold the button while it runs.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: The list's name for a screen reader, when no heading names it.

props.name: filter
props.doc: The kind that is on: an event `kind`, or '' for all.

events.name: update:filter
events.doc: The new value of `filter`, for `v-model:filter`.

UiLog.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: The history of a record on a timeline, newest first. Take it as the last section of a record's drawer or page.

decisions.text: The app's part. It sorts `items` newest first (an unsorted log repeats its day headings), keys the log per record (`:key="record.id"`), so a filter or a failed "older" of one record does not stay on the next, and returns the promise from `@more` and `@retry`, which is what holds their buttons.

decisions.label: Event
decisions.text: Each event is a node with who did what to what ("Anna changed Status"), when, and the value before and after. One field reads on its own line ("Status Waiting → Approved", a status in badges); several fields stand in a small table (field, was, became). Words that came with the event, such as a reason to decline, stand under it. An event with no one behind it (`actor: null`, a release in a changelog) opens with what was done; an unset actor is the system. `anchor` gives the event's row an id, so a link can point at it.

decisions.label: Node
decisions.text: The node is a dot in the event's tone, or, with `node="actor"`, the face of who did it, for a log where the person matters most.

decisions.label: Timeline
decisions.text: A line joins the nodes, so it is a timeline, not a list of rows, and does not stand on UiListItem.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: The last section of a record's drawer or page, after its form and its card of facts (UiListItem rows). It only tells, so a drawer level that ends in it has no footer.

decisions.label: Filters
decisions.text: `filters` offers a choice over the list by the events' `kind`, "All" first: one kind at a time, so it is a choice, not toggles. Up to three kinds stand as a segmented choice; four or more go into a select, so the filter never runs past the card. A filter that leaves nothing loaded says so and offers "Show all".

decisions.label: Load
decisions.text: While the first page comes (`loading` with no events) the log draws rows in the shape of events, a node and a line of text, so nothing moves when they arrive. A failed first load (`failed`) says so with Retry, which calls `@retry` and is held while its promise runs. No events is said, not left blank. With events in view, `loading` is a refresh: they stay, dimmed and busy, and "Load older events" waits; `failed` leaves them and says so under them, with Retry. The states stand on UiNoData and UiSkeleton, as every data state of the library does.

decisions.label: Older events
decisions.text: `hasMore` with `@more` ends the list in "Load older events", held while the promise runs. A failed load says so under the list and leaves the button to retry. When older events arrive, what was on screen stays in place and the count that came is said.

decisions.label: Days
decisions.text: When every event's `at` is a Date, the events stand under their days: "Today", "Yesterday", then the weekday and the date, with the year when it is not this one. Each event then reads its hour alone, and the timeline runs on through the headings: one history. It is decided over all of `items`, so a filter never turns the headings on or off. A time given as a string cannot be told apart by day, so such a log keeps every date on its line: the hour for today, the date otherwise. A Date that is no moment reads "—" under the day before it.

decisions.label: Time
decisions.text: The exact moment is in the time's title, in the app's time zone (`createGrani({ timeZone })`). Set the zone, or the server and the browser may show different hours and days.

decisions.label: Rhythm
decisions.text: 24 between events, 8 inside one, so where an event ends reads at a glance.

decisions.label: Values
decisions.text: A value is never cut: a long one wraps. A `from` or `to` that is `null` or an empty text is no value: no `from` reads as set, no `to` as cleared; a 0 is a value. In a table of changes an arrow stands between what it was and what it became, as on one line; in a card too narrow for three columns each row stands as a stack, the field over the pair, so a long value keeps the card's width. Among faces (`node="actor"`) the system has a plate of a face's size with a glyph.

doc.keyboard:
The filter is a segmented UiRadioGroup, or a UiSelect past three kinds; "Show all", "Load older events" and Retry are buttons; the events take no tab stop.
- `Tab`: reaches the filter, then goes on to "Show all", Retry or "Load older events".
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: move the segmented filter from kind to kind; the select opens on its own keys.
- `Enter` `Space`: press the button.
When "Load older events" disappears under the focus, the focus goes to the first new event, else the last event shown, else the filter, never to the page; so does a Retry that brought the history, whether the app draws it before or after its promise ends, and a Retry that failed again hands it to the new Retry. A refresh leaves the focus on "Load older events", which waits.
doc.reader:
- List: named by `ariaLabel` when no heading names it.
- Event: read as its words: who did what to what, and when; with no one named, what to what.
- Days: each day is an item of the log, its events a list named by its heading.
- One change: reads "Status Waiting became Approved" (the arrow is hidden and "became" is said in its place).
- Several changes: stand in a table named "Changes" with the columns Field, Previous value and New value; the arrows between them are hidden.
- Filter: a radiogroup, or a combobox past three kinds, named "Show events", the kind that is on chosen.
- Older events: a status region says how many came ("3 older events loaded"), once: a refresh or another kind shown lets it go.
- Failed load: an alert under the list; a failed first load is an alert with Retry.
- First load: a status says the history is loading; the rows in its shape are hidden.
doc.states: Events under their days or with their dates, as dots in their tone or as faces, the system's plate among faces, an event with no one named, one change on a line, several in a table, a note; filters with the kind that is on; `hasMore` with "Load older events", held while the promise runs, failed with its line and the button left to retry, and the loaded count said; nothing yet (`empty`), and a filter that leaves nothing loaded, with "Show all"; the first load (`loading`), and a first load that failed (`failed`), with Retry held while it runs.
doc.notFor:
- The facts of a record: UiListItem rows in a UiList.
- A list of records: UiTable.
- A request answered: a toast of UiToaster.
- A timeline the person edits: never; it only tells.

props.name: align
props.doc: Which edge of the button the menu lines up with; start and end follow the reading direction.

slots.name: trigger
slots.doc: The button that opens the menu: one element or component, it keeps its own look and name.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The items: `UiListItem as="button"` rows placed directly (not inside a component of your own), groups split by a `UiSeparator`. An item's `@click` that stops the click keeps the menu open with the focus on its button: let it through.

UiMenu.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A list of commands that opens under a button. Take it for actions that have no room beside their subject, such as the actions of a table row.

decisions.label: Trigger
decisions.text: The trigger is your own button in `#trigger` (a UiButton, or a UiIconButton with three dots); the menu gives it `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` and the toggle.

decisions.label: Items
decisions.text: Items are UiListItem command rows (`as="button"`) in the default slot, with groups split by a UiSeparator. The menu draws every one as a `menuitem`, a row of its panel list (`utils/panelList`, shared with UiSelect, UiFilterList and UiDateRange): edge to edge, lit as the same band by the arrows and by the pointer, with the row's title, description, glyphs, tone, `loading`, `disabled` and `step`. A click on an item runs it and closes the menu, unless the item is `loading` or `disabled`. A menu runs commands only: a link row (`to`) or a label row in it warns in development, since it would be a button going nowhere; a place to go is a link row outside the menu, or a command whose `@click` navigates. A text or a row inside a component of your own warns too: it is not an item.

decisions.label: Popover
decisions.text: It stands on the panel core UiPopover stands on, which gives the panel, its place beside the button and its place on the overlay stack; the menu adds the items and the keys. It holds commands only. A panel of controls (filters, a period, columns) is a plain popover, because it needs the focus moved into it and kept there, which a menu does not do.

decisions.label: Kept pages
decisions.text: In a page that a `KeepAlive` keeps, a menu left open stays in the body when the page is deactivated, as a popover does. Close it when the route changes.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits under a button of its own, in the trailing slot of a UiButtonGroup, and in a table row's `#row-actions`. Opened from a drawer or a window, it paints above it.

doc.keyboard:
As in the WAI-ARIA menu button.
On the button:
- `Enter` `Space` `ArrowDown`: open it on the first item.
- `ArrowUp`: opens it on the last item. With `Alt` the arrows open it too; `Ctrl` or `Meta` with one stays the browser's.
In the open menu:
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp` `Home` `End`: move; the arrows wrap and skip a disabled item.
- `A–Z`: goes to the next item that starts with the letter.
- `Escape` `Tab`: close it and return the focus to the button, and so does running an item, before its command runs: a command that removes the button's row leaves the focus to the list.
A held Enter is one press: it opens the menu once and runs one item.
A click outside closes it, and the focus stays where the click went. Opened with the mouse, it puts the focus on the panel, not on an item.
doc.reader:
- Button: says it opens a menu (`aria-haspopup="menu"`) and whether it is open (`aria-expanded`).
- Panel: a `menu` named by the button (`aria-labelledby`; your own id on the button wins).
- Items: each a `menuitem` outside the tab order; a `loading` item says busy (`aria-busy`), and a `disabled` one is a disabled button.
doc.states: Closed, or open beside the button on its start or end edge (`align`); while the button is scrolled out of the window, it waits hidden, still open, and the focus it held comes back with it. A `loading` item spins and refuses the click, and the menu stays open; a `disabled` item is skipped by the arrows. Past five commands, the panel takes a measured height that shows half of the sixth row, and scrolls. With every item switched off by `v-if` it opens empty, the focus on the panel: give the button `disabled` instead.
doc.notFor:
- A panel of controls (filters, a period, columns): UiPopover.
- A value to pick: UiSelect.
- A few actions side by side: UiButtonGroup.

props.name: title
props.doc: The window's name, read first by a screen reader; required, a dialog without one is mute.

props.name: description
props.doc: One line under the title, read right after it.

props.name: size
props.doc: Width: `sm` for a question or a short form, `md` for a form with a few rows.

props.name: persistent
props.doc: Unsaved input: the backdrop and Escape are refused with a shake; the cross still closes.

props.name: submitting
props.doc: A request is out (a save, a delete): every close is refused with a shake, and no second submit goes.

props.name: role
props.doc: `alertdialog` for a question that needs an answer: the backdrop does not close it, focus starts on the footer's first button.

props.name: padded
props.doc: `false` for rows edge to edge (a detail of key and value): the body keeps no padding of its own.

props.name: align
props.doc: `center` for a result after an action: a glyph over a centered title, no lines between the parts.

props.name: form
props.doc: The body and the footer are a form: its `type="submit"` button, Enter in a field and Cmd+Enter from a text box send `submit`. Off, a question or a detail keeps its buttons plain.

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the window is open (`v-model:open`); every way out sets it false and emits `close`.

events.name: submit
events.doc: The form was sent, with `form`: its `type="submit"` button, Enter in a field, Cmd+Enter from a text box.

events.name: update:open
events.doc: The new value of `open`, for `v-model:open`.

events.name: close
events.doc: The window closed: the cross, the backdrop, Escape, or another window that took its place. A window whose input must not go that way is `persistent`.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The body. It scrolls when long; the header and the footer stay.

slots.name: media
slots.doc: A glyph over the title with `align="center"`: a check in a halo after a sent invoice. The window sizes it.

slots.name: header
slots.doc: The window's own header in place of the title, the description and the cross: a search field, as a palette's. The title is still read by a screen reader; Escape and the backdrop close. It stands alone: no `#media`, no `align="center"`.

slots.name: footer
slots.doc: Actions, sharing the footer's width in equal parts: the cancel is `secondary` and first, the main action last.

UiModal.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A window over the page for one task: a short form, a question, a detail. Take it when the task needs the person's whole attention.

decisions.label: Closing
decisions.text: `title` names the window and `description` describes it. The backdrop, Escape and the cross close it. Escape works only while the window is the top layer, so a confirm over a drawer closes first. `persistent` guards unsaved input: the backdrop and Escape are refused with a shake, but the cross still closes, since pressing it is an explicit intent. `submitting` refuses every close while a request is out. These guard only the window's own exits; `open` set to false from outside is for the host to guard.

Over a window. One window is seen at a time. A window opened from a window takes its place: the first closes, and when the new one closes the focus returns to what opened the first. A question (`role="alertdialog"`, UiConfirm) is about the window under it: it hides that window, out of sight and out of reach, and when it is answered the window comes back as it was, the focus on what asked. A window holding unsaved input (`persistent`) or a request (`submitting`) is not replaced: it waits hidden in the same way. The tint on the page stays as it was. A drawer is not hidden: a window over it leaves it in view.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.text: Attributes land on the dialog. The page under it does not scroll; a long body scrolls between the header and the footer. The footer's buttons share its width, so two buttons take half each.

decisions.label: Kept pages
decisions.text: In a page that a `KeepAlive` keeps, a window left open stays open when the page is deactivated: its layer, its Escape and its scroll lock go on over the next page. Close it (`open` false) when the route changes.

decisions.label: Question
decisions.text: `role="alertdialog"` is a question that needs an answer (UiConfirm): the backdrop does not close it, and the focus starts on the first button of the footer, the safe one.

decisions.label: Result
decisions.text: `align="center"` shows a result after an action: `#media` (a glyph) over a centered title, with no lines between the parts.

decisions.label: Header
decisions.text: `#header` puts a header of the window's own in place of the title and the cross (a search field over its results); the title stays for a screen reader.

decisions.label: Form
decisions.text: With `form` the body and the footer become a form that sends `submit`. The main action is `type="submit"`; Enter in a field, and Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter from a text box, send it. The shortcut presses that button, so while the button is held or spinning, the shortcut does nothing either. One request gets one submit. A submit that leaves a field `aria-invalid` puts the focus on the first such field and scrolls it into view; the form is ready again as soon as the person moves to fix it. An answer that comes later and marks a field does the same when `submitting` falls, unless the person went on typing in another field meanwhile. Do not put a form of your own in the slot. `submit` carries nothing: a window has one way to send, its main action. UiCrudDrawer's `submit` carries `{ another }`, since its Save can also mean "save and start the next record".

doc.keyboard:
The focus starts on the first field (a drawn select, date, switch, scale, drop zone or date range too), not on the cross. With no field it starts on a body longer than the window, so the arrows scroll it at once, else on the window itself; `role="alertdialog"` starts it on the first button of the footer. On close the focus returns to where it was.
- `Tab`: goes round inside the window; a body longer than the window is one of its stops.
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown` `PageUp` `PageDown` `Home` `End`: scroll that body once it holds the focus.
- `Escape`: closes the window, only while it is the top layer; `persistent` answers it with a shake, and `submitting` refuses it.
With `form`:
- `Enter`: in a field, sends the form.
- `Meta+Enter` `Ctrl+Enter`: send it from a text box too (`Meta` is Cmd).
A submit that leaves a field `aria-invalid` puts the focus on the first one.
doc.reader:
- Window: a modal dialog (`aria-modal`) named by `title` (`aria-labelledby`) and described by `description`. With `#header` the title is still read, and a question (`alertdialog`) with no description is described by its body.
- Cross: named "Close".
- Long body: a region named by the title, so the reader says what the keys scroll through.
- Errors: a refused submit marks the field in error `aria-invalid`.
- Refused close: a shake for the eye; the reader keeps the focus where it was and hears why, from a status region inside the window: input not saved, or a request still on its way. A question refuses a press beside it with the shake alone: its answers are in reach.
- Refused submit: the reader hears the field in error the focus moved to.
- A window under another: out of the reader's reach until it comes back; then the reader hears it and the control the focus returned to.
doc.states: A form; a long body that scrolls between the header and the footer; a detail of rows running edge to edge (`padded` off); a question (`role="alertdialog"`); a result (`align="center"`); a search (`#header`); a window opened from a window, in its place; a question over a window, the one under hidden. `persistent` shakes at the backdrop and Escape; a submit the host refuses by marking a field as it gets it shakes too; `submitting` refuses every close and a second submit. Sizes `sm` and `md`, in both themes.
doc.notFor:
- A record to edit: UiCrudDrawer.
- A side panel beside a list: UiDrawer, to read or set at the side of the screen.
- A small panel of controls under a button: UiPopover, with the page live.
- A yes-or-no question: UiConfirm, built on this window.
- The outcome of an action: a toast from `useToast` in UiToaster.

props.name: value
props.doc: The amount in major units: a number or the decimal string an API sends. Empty or unreadable prints a dash.

props.name: currency
props.doc: ISO 4217 code for this cell; unset, the app's currency (`createGrani({ currency })`).

props.name: unit
props.doc: What the amount is per, `kg` or `pc`; shown after the currency as "EUR / kg".

props.name: tone
props.doc: Meaning of the amount: `success`, `danger`, `info`. Unset is the normal ink.

UiMoneyCell.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: An amount in a table column: the number on top, the currency and unit under it ("EUR / kg"). Take it for any column of money.

decisions.label: Two lines
decisions.text: The number is in monospace and the unit is under it in small capitals, so amounts line up and the unit is read once per row, not once per digit.

decisions.label: Value
decisions.text: The value is in major units, as a number or the decimal string an API sends. The cell formats it in the library's locale with as many decimals as its currency has: two for EUR, three for KWD, none for JPY, two with no currency. Zero is a number and prints, also an amount that rounds to zero, with no minus; an empty value prints the dash a table prints.

decisions.label: Currency
decisions.text: The app sets it once with `createGrani({ currency })`, or `currency` sets it for one cell. With neither, the lower line holds the unit alone, or is left out.

decisions.label: Tone
decisions.text: `tone` is what the amount means: `success`, `danger` or `info`; there is no warning amount. The tone is color only, so the row says the meaning in words elsewhere (a status, a label), as the demo does. Without a tone the amount takes the host's text color, so a class on the cell colors it. Outside a table cell, an ancestor must set that color (`text-fg`); the cell sets no default.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: no tab stop, no keys.
doc.reader:
- Value: the number, then the unit line, read as text in that order ("1,250.00 EUR / kg").
- Tone: color only, so the row says the meaning in words elsewhere.
- Empty value: read as the dash.
doc.states: None of its own: the row and the table carry hover, selection, loading and failure. The cell has a value with and without a unit line, zero, an empty or unreadable value as a dash, and the three tones.
doc.notFor:
- A date: UiDateCell.
- An amount to type: UiInput with the unit in `#end`.
- A change against the value before: UiDelta.
- A share of a whole: UiProgress.

props.name: title
props.doc: One short line of what happened: "No invoices yet", "The record did not load".

props.name: description
props.doc: Why it is empty and what to do next.

props.name: tone
props.doc: `danger` for a load that failed: a red plate and an alert; its Retry is a `secondary` UiButton in `#actions`.

props.name: size
props.doc: `md` for a page, `sm` for a section inside a drawer or a card.

slots.name: media
slots.doc: The glyph on the plate, as a row's `#media`; `danger` draws a warning sign when it is empty.

slots.name: actions
slots.doc: The next step, a UiButton of your own or two: `primary` to create the first one, `secondary` to reset the filters or retry, with `loading` when it sends.

UiNoData.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: An empty place that says why and offers the next step. Take it where a list, a table or a section has nothing to show. Nothing yet: create; nothing matches: change the filters; the load failed: retry (`tone="danger"`, read out as an alert).

decisions.label: Anatomy
decisions.text: A glyph in `#media` on a round plate in the tone, a short `title`, the `description`, and the next step in `#actions` (UiButton of your own: you choose the weight and `loading`).

decisions.label: Frame
decisions.text: On a page it has a dashed frame; in a card (UiCard `#empty`), a drawer or a window, the surface frames it. The root is a `<div role="status">`.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: the block takes no focus; the buttons in `#actions` are the tab stops.
doc.reader:
- Role: a `status`; `tone="danger"` is an `alert`, read at once. The block appears with its words, and a status that appears with its words is often not read out: that a list is empty is said by a region that was on the page before (UiTable has one), and a page of your own keeps one.
- Order: the title, then the description.
- Glyph: the glyph on its plate is hidden.
doc.states: Nothing yet, with a `primary` button to create the first one; nothing matches, with a `secondary` button to reset the filters; the load failed, `danger`, a red plate with a warning glyph and Retry. `sm` in a drawer or a card, `md` on a page. A dashed frame on a page, none inside a card, a drawer or a window. A neutral one without a glyph draws no plate.
doc.notFor:
- Content on its way: UiSkeleton.
- An action in flight: UiSpinner.
- A notice over content that is there: UiListItem in a `tone`.
- A failed request: a toast through UiToaster.

props.name: page
props.doc: Current page, from 1 (`v-model:page`).

props.name: pageSize
props.doc: Records per page; the page count is derived from it and `total`. Changing it is not this component's job.

props.name: total
props.doc: Total records.

props.name: compact
props.doc: "N / M" instead of page numbers, for a narrow row.

props.name: siblings
props.doc: Pages shown on each side of the current one.

props.name: boundary
props.doc: Pages always shown at each end.

props.name: loading
props.doc: A page is on its way: the pressed arrow shows a spinner and keeps the focus, the numbers are held, and a press asks nothing. Pass the list's loading flag.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The row cannot page at all: the arrows are off, the numbers are held. A load is `loading`.

props.name: size
props.doc: Control size shared by every button in the row. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

events.name: update:page
events.doc: Asks the parent for this page, clamped to the range; the parent applies it.

UiPagination.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: Page numbers with previous and next arrows. Take it under a list that pages, beside the count.

decisions.text: What it owns. It knows the total and the page size and asks for a page, nothing else; the list owns the data and the page size.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In the footer of a UiDataTable, in the corner beside the count ("1–25 of 57").

decisions.label: Count
decisions.text: The page count is max(1, ceil(total / pageSize)); one page renders nothing.

Out of range. A page that is out of range or unreadable is drawn as the nearest one, and a click is clamped to the range. The pager draws; it does not ask: on a list that shrank (a delete, a filter), the app sets the page to the last one, as UiDataTable does.

decisions.label: Loading
decisions.text: While a page is on its way the app passes `loading`: the arrow that asked shows a spinner and keeps the focus, the other arrow is off, the numbers are held but keep the focus, and a press asks nothing. A number that asked shows the spinner in place of its digits, in a slot of the same width. A click on the current page asks nothing either. `disabled` is a row that cannot page at all, not a load.

decisions.label: Steady row
decisions.text: The row holds still. Once the pages do not fit, it always shows the same number of slots (a gap never hides a single page), and every number is as wide as the widest, so the arrows stay under the pointer.

decisions.label: Narrow box
decisions.text: It fills the box it is given, as wide as its parent or the rest of a row, and draws its row at the start of it: `text-center` or `text-end` on it moves the row. Where that box is too narrow for the numbers (20rem at `xs`, 24rem at `sm`, 28rem at `md`, a container query, not the screen; wider as the last page gains digits past two), they give way to "3 / 20" between the arrows. A number that had the focus hands it to "3 / 20".

doc.keyboard:
- `Tab`: walks the previous arrow, each page number and the next arrow; an arrow at its end is disabled and skipped.
- `Enter` `Space`: press the arrow or the number, which are buttons.
While `loading` the pressed arrow keeps the focus with its spinner, and the numbers stay in the Tab order (`aria-disabled`), so a press that starts a load keeps the focus in the row. An arrow that turns off at its end once the page has come hands the focus to the current page, or to "3 / 20" in the compact row; so does an arrow under the focus when the row turns `disabled`.
doc.reader:
- Landmark: a navigation landmark named "Pagination", or by the caller's `aria-label`; a second pager on the page takes one of its own, so the two landmarks are told apart.
- Arrows: "Previous page" and "Next page".
- Numbers: every number is "Page N", the current one is `aria-current="page"`, and held numbers are `aria-disabled`.
- Page change: a status region, always there, says "Page N of M" when the page changes, in the wide row and the compact one alike; the numbers are grouped as the app's language does.
- Compact label: "3 / 20" is read as "Page 3 of 20" when it takes the focus.
- Loading: the pressed arrow or number says busy (`aria-busy`).
doc.states: Every page while they fit, the ends with a window and gaps, the first and the last page with an arrow inert, `loading` with a spinner on the pressed arrow, `disabled`, `compact` and the narrow row with "N / M", a stale page past the range drawn as the last; three steps of the ladder. One page draws nothing.
doc.notFor:
- A list that loads and owns its page: UiDataTable around the table.
- Older events at the end of a timeline: UiLog with `hasMore`.
- Views of one page: UiTabs.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The password (`v-model`); empty is `''`.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name for forms.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Hint shown while empty.

props.name: autocomplete
props.doc: Password manager hint: `new-password` when setting one, `current-password` when signing in.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Nothing can be typed, generated or copied.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: The password is shown and copied but not changed: typing and generate are held.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the input invalid standalone. Inside UiField the error sets this.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id of the input when standalone. Inside UiField the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder for the field and both buttons. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

props.name: length
props.doc: Length of a generated password; never under 10.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the input when no UiField label names it.

props.name: copy
props.doc: The copy button beside the field; `false` leaves it out, where a password must not reach the clipboard.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The value changed, typed or generated.

events.name: generate
events.doc: A generated password the owner took: it holds no typo, a form may copy it into its repeat field. Not fired when the owner refused it.

UiPasswordField.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A field for setting a new password, with buttons to show, copy and generate it. Signing in and signing up take UiInput `type="password"` instead.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.text: The eye that shows the password sits inside the field (UiInput). Beside the field, 8px apart, stand a copy button (UiCopyButton, once there is a value) and, at the end, a generate button (`generatePassword`). Generate is last, so it never moves under the pointer when copy appears. `:copy="false"` leaves copy out, where a password must not reach the clipboard.

decisions.label: Generate
decisions.text: A generated password has a lower-case letter, an upper-case letter, a digit and a symbol. Once the owner accepts it, it is shown at once, announced to a screen reader without its value, and emitted through `generate`, so a form can fill its "repeat" field itself. When the owner refuses it, nothing is said or shown.

decisions.label: Hiding
decisions.text: Emptying the field hides the password again.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: The password is text, and empty is `''`, never `null`.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: `class` and `style` land on the row, everything else on the input.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In UiField, which gives the label, description and error, beside UiInput `type="password"` for the repeat.

decisions.label: Signing in
decisions.text: It is not for signing in or signing up: there, a generated password the person never saw is one they cannot type again.

doc.keyboard:
A row.
- `Tab`: reaches the input, its eye, then copy, then generate.
- `Enter` `Space`: on generate, fill the field and show the password; on copy, copy it. Neither submits the form around them.
When the copy button disappears under the focus (the value emptied, the field disabled), the focus moves to generate. `disabled` blocks typing and generate and takes the copy button away; `readonly` blocks generate and keeps copy.
doc.reader:
- Input: named by the field's label or by `ariaLabel`; `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` on it, and the field's words are read with it.
- Buttons: copy and generate are icon buttons with their own names; copy says it copies the password.
- Generate: a generated password is announced without its value, again on a second generate.
- Copy: UiCopyButton says the outcome from the page's live region, or from the open window's.
- Eye: says whether the password is shown (`aria-pressed`).
doc.states: Empty (no copy button), with a value (copy appears before generate, which never moves), shown or hidden by the eye, generated (shown at once), disabled (all three blocked), readonly (copy kept, generate blocked), and invalid.
doc.notFor:
- Signing in or signing up: UiInput `type="password"`.
- The repeat field beside it: UiInput `type="password"` too.
- A secret given to copy and never typed: UiCopyButton with an `ariaLabel` and neither `label` nor `truncate`, which would put it on the screen and in its name.

props.name: align
props.doc: Which edge of the button the panel lines up with; start and end follow the reading direction.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: The element the panel lines up with, when the button sits inside a wider one (a field's capsule).

props.name: labelledby
props.doc: The id of what names the panel, when the button's text is not its name (a field's label).

props.name: open
props.doc: Whether the panel is open (`v-model:open`): the host learns of every close and can open it from outside.

events.name: update:open
events.doc: The new value of `open`, for `v-model:open`.

slots.name: trigger
slots.doc: The button that opens the panel: one element or component, it keeps its own look and name.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The controls. `close` closes the panel and returns focus to the button.

slots.name: footer
slots.doc: The actions under a line at the end of the panel, `xs` buttons 8px in (a gray Reset first with `me-auto`, Apply last); it stays in view while the controls scroll. Gets `close`. One that draws nothing draws no line.

UiPopover.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A small panel under a button, with the page still live. Take it for a few controls about the page (a note, a currency, a date); a filter is UiFilter and the columns of a table UiTableColumns, both on this panel, as UiMenu is for its list of commands.

decisions.label: Trigger
decisions.text: The trigger is your own button in `#trigger`; the popover gives it `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` and the toggle. The panel has no heading: the button names it, or `labelledby` does (a field's label).

decisions.label: Dialog
decisions.text: The panel is a non-modal dialog, and the page stays live: no backdrop, no scroll lock.

decisions.label: Open state
decisions.text: `v-model:open` lets the host open it, at mount too, and hear every close. When it is closed from outside, a focus that was inside goes back to the button.

decisions.label: Kept pages
decisions.text: In a page that a `KeepAlive` keeps, a panel left open stays in the body when the page is deactivated, and Escape closes it there. Close it (`open` false) when the route changes.

decisions.label: Footer
decisions.text: Actions (Apply, Reset) go in `#footer`, under a line at the end, never among the controls; both slots get `close`. Sections are flat UiCard components with a separator between neighbors, as in every overlay.

decisions.label: Nesting
decisions.text: A select, a menu or a date picker inside works: a press in its list does not count as outside, and anything opened from the panel paints above it. A list at the top or the bottom of the panel (a UiFilterList) reaches that edge, as a select's list does. The panel is never taller than the room beside its button, so it never covers the button; a longer panel scrolls inside itself.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: `class` and other attributes land on the panel. Its `id` stays its own, because the button points at it.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits in a table toolbar (UiFilter, UiDateRange, UiTableColumns), under a date field (UiDatePicker); a menu's panel (UiMenu) is the same panel, holding commands.

doc.keyboard:
- `Enter` `Space`: on the button, open it, as a click does. The focus goes to the first field (a drawn select, date, switch, scale, drop zone or date range too, or what is marked `data-autofocus`), else to the first control; a panel of buttons opens on its first button.
- `Tab`: goes round inside.
- `Escape`: closes it and returns the focus to the button, only while the panel is the top layer.
`close` from a slot does the same, unless the focus has already moved into a layer opened from the panel (a drawer an item opened), which keeps it. A click outside closes it and leaves the focus where the click went.
doc.reader:
- Button: says it opens a dialog (`aria-haspopup`), whether it is open (`aria-expanded`) and what it controls (`aria-controls`).
- Panel: a non-modal `dialog` named by the button (`aria-labelledby`), or by `labelledby` (a field's label), with no heading of its own.
doc.states: Closed, or open under the button on its start, center or end edge (`align`), above it when there is no room below. It is never taller than the room beside the button; a longer panel scrolls inside itself with the `#footer` in view. While its button is scrolled out of the window, the panel waits hidden, still open, and the focus it held comes back with it. Opened from outside with `v-model:open`, at mount too. A select, a menu or a date picker open inside it. Opened from a drawer, where Escape closes only the panel.
doc.notFor:
- Commands: UiMenu.
- A task that needs the whole attention: UiModal.
- A record to edit: UiCrudDrawer.
- A hint of text alone: UiTooltip.

props.name: value
props.doc: The current value, in the units of `max`. Not read while `indeterminate`.

props.name: max
props.doc: The value at which the bar is full.

props.name: indeterminate
props.doc: Work of unknown length: a band runs along the track, no value is said.

props.name: step
props.doc: Size of one segment; turns the bar into segments, an empty one reads as one step still to go.

props.name: maxSegments
props.doc: Above this many segments the bar is continuous again: a finger cannot tell them apart.

props.name: tone
props.doc: Color of the fill; `brand` by default.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `plain` fills with `tone`; `thermometer` colors the fill by how full it is, danger through warning to success (`utils/scaleRamp`).

props.name: invert
props.doc: Reverses the thermometer: less is better (load, pain, cost).

props.name: valueText
props.doc: Words for the value instead of a number: "3 of 10 payments". Past `max` they carry the overage, the number stops at `max`.

UiProgress.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: How far work or a target has come, `value` of `max`. Take it when the share is known: an upload, a quota, a goal; for work of unknown length set `indeterminate`.

decisions.label: Steps
decisions.text: With `step` it shows one segment per step, filled by whole steps reached; an empty segment is a step still to go.

decisions.label: Color
decisions.text: `tone` colors the fill. `variant="thermometer"` colors it by how full it is, from danger to success, and `invert` flips that for "less is better".

decisions.label: Unknown length
decisions.text: `indeterminate` is work of unknown length: a band runs along the track, with no number.

decisions.label: Size
decisions.text: The host's classes set the size; without them the bar is 8px tall.

decisions.label: Value
decisions.text: It is a progressbar with `aria-valuenow`, absent while the value is unknown. `valueText` gives words, and it is what says a value past `max` ("14 of 10, over"), since the number stops at `max`. Name each bar (`aria-label`); unnamed, it is "Progress".

decisions.label: Marks
