decisions.text: A mark already given is this bar with `:step="1"`; a mark to give is UiScaleInput.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It sits in a table's progress column, as UiDropzone's upload bar, and in a card, under its figure or as its `#divider`.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: it takes no focus. A mark to give is UiScaleInput.
doc.reader:
- Name: a `progressbar` named by the `aria-label` the host gives it, else "Progress"; a host that names it with `aria-labelledby` gets no second name.
- Value: `aria-valuenow` runs from `0` to `max`, and is absent while `indeterminate` or while the value is not a number.
- Value text: `valueText` is read in place of the number and carries a value past `max`.
- Hidden: the fill and the segments.
doc.states: Empty, part, full and past `max`, where the number stops at `max`. `step` segments, filled by whole steps reached, and a continuous bar again above `maxSegments` or with no step filled. `tone` on the fill. `thermometer` from danger through warning to success, `invert` reversed. `indeterminate`, a band running along the track, which keeps running, slower, under reduced motion. 8px tall without a height class, else the host's height. In forced colors the track is outlined and the fill takes the highlight.
doc.notFor:
- A wait in place: UiSpinner.
- Content on its way: UiSkeleton.
- A number: UiCount.
- A change: UiDelta.
- A mark to give: UiScaleInput.

props.name: value
props.doc: The value this radio stands for; the group's model takes it when selected.

props.name: description
props.doc: A second line under the label. Read with the radio as its description. Not drawn in a segment.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents selecting this radio; the group's `disabled` covers all of them.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id, for a label elsewhere.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when the slot has no text: a glyph segment, a label outside the row.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: Label text displayed next to the mark. Clicking it selects the radio.

slots.name: media
slots.doc: A glyph or a small image before the text. Cards only.

slots.name: meta
slots.doc: A value at the end, before the mark: a price, a count. Cards only.

UiRadio.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: One option of a UiRadioGroup, with its label in the slot and an optional `description` under it. It works only inside UiRadioGroup; its spec lives in the group's.

decisions.label: Row
decisions.text: It is a native radio drawn as the library's round mark. The whole row is the label, so a click anywhere on it selects. The mark stands at the first line (18px, 1px down in its 22px line), 8px from the text as a checkbox's, so a long label wraps beside it.

decisions.label: Card
decisions.text: In a `card` group the row is a card: `#media` first, then the text, `#meta` (a price, a count), and the mark at the end, all centered on the card. A selected card gets a brand border and halo; a disabled one keeps the neutral border, and its muted mark says the choice. In a `card-check` group a check and a tint replace the round mark.

decisions.label: Segment
decisions.text: In a `segmented` group the row is one segment of the bar, pressed when selected, with no mark. It takes a press out to the bar's edge, the first and the last also to its ends. A disabled selected segment keeps a plate, so the choice still shows.

decisions.label: Group
decisions.text: The group says invalid and required, not the radio. A form reset puts the radios back on the model.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes and listeners land on the input, `class` and `style` on the row.

decisions.label: Naming
decisions.text: A radio with no slot text (a glyph segment, a row whose label sits elsewhere) is named by `ariaLabel` or by a `<label for>` that points at its `id`.

doc.keyboard:
The keys belong to the group: a native radio sits under the mark, the card and the segment, so they work through UiRadioGroup, with one tab stop once one is checked.
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown` `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: move the selection.
- `Space`: selects.
A click anywhere on the row selects, a card's media and meta included. `disabled` blocks it whatever the group says.
doc.reader:
- Name: a radio named by the slot text alone, or by `ariaLabel` or a `<label for>` when the slot holds no text.
- Description: the `description` and a card's `#meta` are read once after it, as its description, never as part of the name.
- Errors: the group says invalid and required, not the radio.
- Segment: the radio lies invisible over the pressed plate, so a screen reader hears a radio where the eye sees a segment.
doc.states: Unchecked, checked (a brand fill with a dot; a check and a tint in `card-check`; a pressed segment in `segmented`), hover (an empty mark darkens), focus, disabled (muted; a disabled selected segment keeps a plate), and invalid, which reddens the empty marks when the group says so.
doc.notFor:
- Several answers: UiCheckbox.
- A radio outside a group: never, it belongs to UiRadioGroup.
- A card that opens something rather than picks: UiListItem `as="button"`.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The selected value (`v-model`). `null` when nothing is selected.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name shared by every radio, for forms. Generated when omitted, stable across server and client; two apps on one page need their own `app.config.idPrefix`.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents selecting in every radio.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the group as invalid: red marks. Inside UiField, the error state sets this automatically.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `plain` rows with the mark first; `card` a card per radio with the mark at the end; `card-check` cards that show a check and a tint on the selected one only; `segmented` a bar with one segment pressed.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder. A `segmented` bar is 36 or 44 px (`xs` is read as `sm`: a 24px segment is too small to hit); a `plain` mark is 16, 18 or 20 px. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`).

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id of the group, for a reference from elsewhere (`aria-controls`, a link); a field names it by its legend.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the group when there is no visible legend. Inside a UiField group the legend names it.

props.name: required
props.doc: One answer is needed: said to a reader on the group, and `required` on the radios for a form. Inside UiField group the legend says it instead.

props.name: block
props.doc: A segmented bar as wide as its row, segments sharing the width.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The selected value changed.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The radios.

UiRadioGroup.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: One answer out of a few, shown as rows, cards or a segmented bar. The group owns the value, the name and the states; its `UiRadio` children are thin options drawn from it.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: No answer is `null`; a pick sends the option's value. A person cannot take an answer back: where none is an answer too, give it a radio of its own. A value no radio stands for shows nothing chosen and sends nothing; in development the console names it once, an empty string excepted: it is read as no answer yet, as in UiSelect.

decisions.label: Required
decisions.text: It does not force a selection. `required` says one is needed, to a screen reader and to a form.

decisions.label: Variants
decisions.text: `variant` changes only the look: rows, cards, or a `segmented` bar with one segment pressed. The bar stands on the control ladder (the app's step, `sm` at least), `block` makes it fill the row, and it reddens its frame when invalid. A press on the bar's frame picks the segment beside it. A bar wider than its row scrolls sideways inside its frame, its edges fading where more segments wait: keep its words short, two to four of them. The segmented bar is also the library's state switcher.

decisions.label: Model
decisions.text: The radios follow the model after a refused pick and after a form reset.

decisions.label: Names
decisions.text: Two groups in one form need two names: the browser joins radios that share a name. Two Vue apps on one page each need their own `app.config.idPrefix`, or their generated names meet.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Inside UiField, use `group`.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes land on the root (`data-*`); ours apply where we set one, and the caller's description is joined to ours.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a form column beside UiCheckbox and UiSwitch. A segmented bar switches what a card or a list shows (a period, a view, the kind of event in UiLog), over it or in its toolbar.

doc.keyboard:
Native radios: the keys are the browser's, and the radios are native inputs under the marks, the cards and the segments, so a bar is walked the same way as rows.
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown` `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: move the selection.
- `Space`: selects.
There is one tab stop, on the checked radio, or on the first while none is. A click anywhere on a row, a card or a segment selects it. Safari passes over a group whose checked radio is disabled:
turn the whole group off, not its chosen radio.
doc.reader:
- Group: a radiogroup named by the field's legend (`aria-labelledby`) or by the caller's `ariaLabel`.
- Description: the field's description and error, and the caller's own, are read with it.
- Invalid: `invalid` is `aria-invalid` on the group once, never on a radio.
- Required: `required` is `aria-required` on the group and native `required` on the radios for a form; inside a UiField `group` it is silent, since the legend says it once.
- Disabled: `disabled` is `aria-disabled`.
- Radio: each radio is named by its own text, as UiRadio says.
doc.states: Nothing chosen, one chosen, hover, focus, disabled (the whole group, or one radio that stays disabled whatever the group says), invalid (red empty marks; a `segmented` bar reddens its frame), required, and the variants `plain`, `card`, `card-check` and `segmented`, with or without `block`.
doc.notFor:
- Several answers: UiCheckbox in a UiField `group`.
- A mark from 1 to N: UiScaleInput.
- A pick from a long list: UiSelect.
- On or off: UiSwitch.
- Sections of a page, each with its own content: UiTabs.
- Actions side by side: UiButtonGroup.

props.name: open
props.doc: The block is shown (`v-model:open`); the parent owns it, the trigger only asks. Unset, the block starts closed and keeps its own state, which a `#trigger` toggles.

props.name: autofocus
props.doc: When the block opens, the focus goes to its first field: a block opened to be typed in, such as a note. A block shown at mount takes no focus.

events.name: update:open
events.doc: The trigger asked for the other state.

slots.name: trigger
slots.scope: { open: boolean; toggle: () => void; controls: string | undefined; }
slots.doc: The control that opens the block: `controls` is its `aria-controls` while the block is shown; a button also takes `open` as `aria-expanded`, a switch does not (its `aria-checked` says it).

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The block shown under the trigger; it stands on the gutter the host gives (16 under what is above, or the row's inset in a card of rows).

UiReveal.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A block that opens and closes in place, under the control that names it. Take it for settings behind a switch or more options behind a button.

decisions.label: Content
decisions.text: The block goes in the default slot. With `v-model:open`, a `#trigger` (`{ open, toggle, controls }`), such as a UiSwitch in a UiListItem, stands above it; or `:open` alone follows a control elsewhere, which points at the block by its `id`.

decisions.label: Spacing
decisions.text: In a card of rows, the block continues the row: it sits on the row's inset, 16 below it. On a padded surface, or on no surface, it stands 16 under what is above it. A nested block keeps that gutter.

doc.keyboard:
Nothing of its own: the control in `#trigger` keeps its keys (a UiSwitch, a button).
- `Tab`: reaches the fields of an open block in their order.
When the block closes with the focus inside, the focus goes to the control that names the block in `aria-controls`, else to the element above. Opening leaves the focus on the trigger, as a disclosure does; with `autofocus` it goes to the block's first field, for a block opened to be typed in.
doc.reader:
- Trigger: says the block's state: a button takes `open` as `aria-expanded`, and a switch says it through `aria-checked`. `controls` points the trigger at the block only while the block is shown.
- Closed block: its fields leave the page and are not submitted.
- Height: the change of height is not announced.
doc.states: Open and closed, with the height following the content: `ui-reveal` animates a grid row from `0fr` to `1fr`, with the opacity, over `--ui-dur-fast`; under reduced motion the change is instant. With a `#trigger` and `open` unset, it starts closed and keeps its own state.
doc.notFor:
- A panel floating beside its trigger: UiPopover.
- A record inside a record: a step of UiCrudDrawer.
- Panes switched among others: UiTabs.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The mark (`v-model`); `null` while there is no answer.

props.name: min
props.doc: First step of the scale.

props.name: max
props.doc: Last step. Twelve steps at most.

props.name: clearable
props.doc: A click on the mark, Delete or Backspace clears the answer; off, an answer once given stays.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Nothing can be picked.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control invalid: the empty segments and the frame take the danger tone. Inside UiField the error sets this.

props.name: required
props.doc: An answer is needed: said to a reader on the group. Not enforced by a form: the hidden input takes no validation. Inside UiField group the legend says it instead.

props.name: unit
props.doc: Shown after the readout: "7 / 10 km".

props.name: readout
props.doc: The line "mark / max" above the bar.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id of the group, for a reference from elsewhere (`aria-controls`, a link); a field names it by its legend.

props.name: name
props.doc: Form field name: a hidden input sends the mark; nothing is sent while there is no answer or the scale is disabled.

props.name: showNumbers
props.doc: Numbers in the segments; off for a dense row.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `brand` fills with the brand; `thermometer` colors the fill by the mark, danger through warning to success.

props.name: invert
props.doc: Reverses the thermometer: more is worse (difficulty, pain, load).

props.name: lowLabel
props.doc: What the low end means: "easy".

props.name: highLabel
props.doc: What the high end means: "hard".

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the scale when there is no UiField around.

props.name: size
props.doc: Height of the bar on the control ladder: `xs` 28, `sm` 36. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`); `md` is read as `sm`: the scale has no `md`.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The mark changed; `null` after a clear.

UiScaleInput.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: One mark on a scale of a few steps, 1 to 10 by default. Take it for how hard, how good or how much.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.text: A bar of segments is filled up to the mark, with the number in each segment. A readout shows "mark / max" with a unit at its end; the name is the field's, a UiField `group` label over it, or `ariaLabel` alone. Words at the two ends say what low and high mean, and a screen reader hears them with the first and last step.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: No mark is `null`, as a choice is: a clear sends `null`.

decisions.label: Thermometer
decisions.text: `variant="thermometer"` colors the fill by the mark in five stops, from danger through warning to success, each with an ink that reads on it. `invert` is for scales where more is worse.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Standalone it takes `ariaLabel`, `invalid` and `required`. Required is only announced, not enforced, because a hidden input takes no validation. Inside UiField `group` the legend names it, and the description or the error describes it. Invalid tints the empty segments and the frame with the danger tone.

decisions.label: Form
decisions.text: `name` sends the mark with a form through a hidden input; nothing is sent while there is no answer or the scale is disabled.

decisions.label: Stray values
decisions.text: A value off the scale shows as no answer. It is dropped only when the scale itself shrinks below it.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes land on the radiogroup, ours where we set one; `class` and `style` on the root.

decisions.label: Steps
decisions.text: Twelve steps at most, because a narrower segment cannot be hit with a finger. For a free number take UiInput with `numeric`.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: Beside UiRadioGroup `segmented` and UiInput in a form column.

decisions.label: Loading
decisions.text: The scale has no loading of its own: while its mark is on its way, its owner draws a UiSkeleton in its shape, a short line where the readout stands over a bar of the control's height for its size (`h-7`, `h-9`, `h-11`), and the field's words at the ends stay, with a `role="status"` of its own that says the load. The demo's Loading tab has it.

doc.keyboard:
A radiogroup underneath. There is one tab stop: on the mark, or on the first step while there is no answer.
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight` `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown`: move the mark from the step in focus; `ArrowUp` at `max` and `ArrowDown` at `min` send nothing.
- `Home` `End`: jump to the ends.
- `Delete` `Backspace`: clear it; a click on the mark clears it too, and `clearable` off stops both.
- `Space` `Enter`: pick the step in focus and never clear.
- `Alt` `Ctrl` `Meta`: keys with them go to the browser.
After a clear or a refused move, the focus returns to the tab stop.
doc.reader:
- Group: a radiogroup named by the field's legend, or by `ariaLabel`; the field's description or error is read with it.
- Step: a radio named by its number out of `max`, the first and the last with their end words; the chosen one is `aria-checked`.
- States: `invalid` is `aria-invalid`; `required` is `aria-required` standalone and silent inside a UiField `group`; `disabled` is `aria-disabled`.
doc.states: No answer (a dash in the readout), a mark with the bar filled to it, hover, focus, disabled (the disabled tokens; it wins over invalid), invalid (the empty segments and the frame in the danger tone, the frame alone on a full bar), required, `thermometer` colored by the mark, inverted, with or without numbers, and a unit in the readout.
doc.notFor:
- A free number: UiInput `numeric`.
- A count of things: UiStepper.
- One answer in words: UiRadioGroup `segmented`.
- A mark shown without editing: UiProgress with `:step="1"`, in a table or on a card.

props.name: items
props.doc: Options or groups of options with labels. With `fetcher` they are the known labels: a prefilled value shows its label before the server answers.

props.name: fetcher
props.doc: Asks a server for the options: called with the filter text on open and as it is typed (250 ms after the last key); a late answer to an older query is dropped. Implies `searchable`.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The options the app passes in `items` are on their way: with none yet, rows in their shape; with options in view, they stay, dimmed. A `fetcher` says this by itself.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown when nothing is selected.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name for forms. The value is submitted through a hidden input.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id when standalone. Inside UiField, the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents opening and clearing.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control as invalid. Shows the invalid border and focus ring. Inside UiField, the error state sets this automatically.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

props.name: searchable
props.doc: Adds a filter to the option list. Typing narrows options by label.

props.name: clearable
props.doc: Adds a button that resets the value to `null`, or to `[]` with `multiple`; never shown on a required field.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: empty is an error, said to a reader, and no cross. Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

props.name: tags
props.doc: With `multiple`: every pick as a tag with a cross below the field, the trigger counting them. Without it the picks are listed in the trigger, which fits a narrow place such as a toolbar.

props.name: tagSize
props.doc: Size of the tags, as a UiBadge's.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The selected value (`v-model`): `null` when nothing is selected; with `multiple`, the picked values in the order they were picked, `[]` when none is.

props.name: multiple
props.doc: Several values: check marks in the rows, an array in the model, the list stays open after a pick.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The selected value changed; `null` (or `[]` with `multiple`) after clearing.

slots.name: start
slots.doc: Before the value, inside the trigger: a glyph that says what is chosen (a clock, a flag). Decoration.

slots.name: picks
slots.scope: { options: SelectOption<SelectValue>[]; remove: (option: SelectOption<SelectValue>, event?: MouseEvent | undefined) => void; disabled: boolean; }
slots.doc: With `multiple`: the picks drawn by the app under the field, in place of tags, the field a search that adds to them. `options` are the picked options as given in `items` or by the `fetcher`; `remove` takes one back and puts the focus on the field (pass the click, `remove(option, $event)`, and a double click's second click on the row sliding under the pointer is held back); `disabled` is the field's, and while it holds `remove` does nothing.

UiSelect.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A form control for picking one value from a list of options, or several with `multiple`. It sits in the input capsule on the control ladder.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a form, under a UiField label beside UiInput and UiDatePicker on the same step, or joined with a UiInput in a UiButtonGroup (an amount and its currency); as the kind filter of UiLog past three kinds.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.text: The trigger is a button with the combobox role. The list is a listbox in a panel anchored under it; the panel flips above when there is no room below and follows scrolling.

decisions.label: Options
decisions.text: Items are options or groups of options. A disabled option is shown but cannot be picked. While the app's options are on their way it passes `loading`: with none yet the list draws rows in their shape, never "No matches"; with options in view they stay, dimmed, still to be picked, and the highlight keeps to its option as they change. A picked value whose option has not come yet reads as a load in the field and is sent as it is; once the load is over, a value no option knows shows as its own text and is sent, so the field never looks empty while the form holds a value, and in development the console names it once per app. An empty string no option has is nothing picked, as `null` is. With `fetcher` the select says its own load and `loading` does nothing. A list that loads holds the height it reached while open, until a filter narrows options already in.

decisions.label: Types
decisions.text: The model's shape follows `multiple`: one value or `null` without it, an array with it, and the props reject the other. A `multiple` decided at run time is two branches (`v-if` with the array model, `v-else` with the single one). `update:modelValue` carries either shape: an explicit handler casts what it receives, `v-model` needs nothing.

decisions.label: Search
decisions.text: `searchable` puts a filter at the top of the list; an option's `keywords` are matched too. The filter leaves the accents of Latin and Cyrillic letters out, so a name typed without them is found ("munchen" finds München) and the Cyrillic yo reads as ie; the Cyrillic short i stays a letter of its own. `fetcher` asks a server for the options as the filter is typed. The picked options are remembered, so their labels survive a new search. While the first answer is on its way the list draws rows of the options' shape, and while it is open it never shrinks, so nothing under the pointer moves as answers come. A failed search offers Try again, which asks once more; a search that matches nothing offers Clear search.

decisions.label: Clear
decisions.text: `clearable` adds a button that resets the value to `null`, or `[]` with `multiple`: a choice is a value or `null`. A required field never gets it, since there empty is an error, not a state. Its place is kept while there is nothing to clear.

decisions.label: Width
decisions.text: A single pick from a local list keeps the field's width: the text is sized to the longest labels, counted in letters, so a label of wide letters outside the three longest can still widen it. A chosen label longer than the field is cut, and shows whole in a tooltip on hover while the list is closed.

decisions.label: Multiple
decisions.text: `multiple` turns the rows into check marks and the model into an array, and a pick keeps the list open. The trigger shows the count of picks, and each pick stands below the field as a tag with a cross.

decisions.label: Picks
decisions.text: With `multiple`, the `#picks` slot draws the picks under the field the app's way, in place of tags: a row with what the app keeps for each, a quantity, a price. The field becomes a search that adds; it keeps its placeholder, since the picks are in view below. The value stays the list of picked values in the order they were picked; what a row holds besides is the app's. A disabled select takes no pick back, and hands `disabled` to the rows, so the app can hold its own controls too.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Standalone it takes `invalid` and `ariaLabel`; inside UiField it reads id, error and required from the field.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: `class` and `style` land on the select's outer box: the capsule, or with tags or the app's picks the box that holds the capsule and them; every other attribute and listener lands on the trigger, the combobox.

doc.keyboard:
On the closed field:
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp` `Enter` `Space` `Home`: open the list, and so do `Alt+ArrowDown` `Alt+ArrowUp`; `Ctrl` or `Meta` with a key stays the browser's.
- `End`: opens the list on the last option.
- `A–Z`: opens it on the first label that starts with the letter, or starts the filter when there is one.
- `Backspace`: with `multiple`, removes the last pick.
In the open list:
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`: move over the enabled options.
- `Home` `End`: jump to the first and the last option; in the filter they move the caret.
- `Enter`: picks; never submits the form around it. While the answer to the typed text is on its way it picks nothing. After a failed search it asks again. A pick closes a single list and returns the focus to the field; a `multiple` list stays open.
- `Space`: picks, outside the filter; after letters typed over the list it belongs to the word.
- `A–Z`: jumps to the first match; letters typed together find a word.
- `Escape`: closes the list and returns the focus to the field; inside a window it closes only the list, and in a filter with text it clears the text first.
- `Tab`: closes the list and moves on to the next field. A pointer press outside closes it too.
On a tag:
- `Enter` `Space`: on its cross, removes that pick and moves the focus to the next tag, or to the field.
doc.reader:
- Field: a combobox named by `ariaLabel` or the field's label. It says the chosen label, the count of picks or the placeholder, whether it is expanded, and that it opens a listbox.
- List: a listbox with the same name, `aria-multiselectable` with `multiple`. A group's heading is shown but is not an option.
- Options: each says selected and disabled. The highlighted one is tracked through `aria-activedescendant` on the field, or on the filter, a named text box with `aria-autocomplete`.
- Status: a region that stays in the DOM says what the list is doing: "Searching…" for a `fetcher`, "Loading options…" and "Updating…" for the app's load, then "No matches" to a search, "No options" to none, or the failure, once nothing is on its way.
- Errors: `invalid` is `aria-invalid`, `required` is `aria-required`, and the field's description and error are read with the field.
- Tags: they stand in a named list, each cross is named with its label, and the clear button has a name.
doc.states: Empty with the placeholder, a pick, open with the chosen option highlighted, a disabled option, groups, the app's options on their way (`loading`: rows of their shape, then dimmed), `searchable` with its filter, a server search (rows of the options' shape while the first answer is on its way, the previous options dimmed while a new query waits, no matches with Clear search, failed with Try again, the list holding the height it reached while open; a late answer is dropped), `multiple` with check marks and a count, with tags below the field, or with the app's rows below it, `clearable` with the cross and its place kept, disabled (the plate, an inert trigger, nothing sent), invalid (a red border; disabled wins over it), and required, with no cross.
doc.notFor:
- A few answers in view: UiRadioGroup.
- Several answers in view: UiCheckbox in a UiField `group`.
- A time of day: UiTimePicker.
- A day: UiDatePicker.
- Commands: UiMenu.
- A list that adds what is typed: UiListField.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: `horizontal` spans the width between stacked blocks; `vertical` stands between items of a row. Default: across the enclosing UiButtonGroup, else horizontal.

UiSeparator.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A line between groups of content. Take it between menu items, parts of a toolbar or groups of a UiButtonGroup.

decisions.label: Spacing
decisions.text: It has no margin of its own: the parent's gap spaces it. On a padded surface, a horizontal line runs through the gutter to the edges by itself; your own `-mx-*` is only for a place with no gutter. A vertical line stretches to the height of its flex row; in a UiButtonGroup it stands across the group.

decisions.label: Border
decisions.text: It is a border, not a fill, because forced colors keep borders.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: it takes no focus and no tab stop.
doc.reader: - Line: a `separator` with its `aria-orientation`: a break between groups and nothing more.
doc.states: None: one line, horizontal or vertical, through a surface's gutter or across a row; a border, so forced colors keep it.
doc.notFor:
- The line under a section title: UiHeader `legend`; where a legend opens a section, the legend is the line.
- The line between rows of a list: UiList draws it.
- Lines under a card's header and above its footer: UiCard draws them.
- The lines between the flat sections of an overlay: the overlay places them, as UiDrawer does.

UiSkeleton.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: The shape of content on its way. Take it in a block of your own while its first load runs; a card, a table, a drawer and a chart card draw their own under `loading`.

decisions.label: Size
decisions.text: Size and shape come from the classes the host passes (`h-4 w-32`, `h-64 w-full`, `rounded-pill` for an avatar); without them it has no size. A line of text is an `inline-block h-3 align-middle` inside a block of the text's size, which keeps the line's height. A page skeleton is several of these, mirroring the real layout.

decisions.label: Decoration
decisions.text: It is decoration, and its shimmer is the sign that the first load runs: under reduced motion it keeps shimmering, slower, since a still gray block reads as a broken page. The host's live region announces the loading state.

decisions.label: By hand
decisions.text: UiCard, UiTable, UiDataTable, UiCrudDrawer and UiChartCard (with its charts) draw it themselves under `loading`. Place it by hand only in blocks of your own, which bring their own `role="status"` and drop it when the data comes.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: it takes no focus and holds no control.
doc.reader: - Hidden: `aria-hidden`; the loading state is announced by the host's live region, a `role="status"` the host brings and drops when the data comes.
doc.states: One: a shimmering block, slower under reduced motion, in the size and shape the host's classes give it; without them it has no size.
doc.notFor:
- An action in flight: UiSpinner.
- Work measured or of unknown length: UiProgress.
- Nothing there or a failed load: UiNoData.
- Loading a card, a table, a drawer or a chart card: UiCard, UiTable, UiCrudDrawer and UiChartCard draw it themselves under `loading`.

UiSkeleton.about: The shape of content on its way. Take it in a block of your own while its first load runs; a card, a table, a drawer and a chart card draw their own under `loading`.

props.name: values
props.doc: The values in order, the newest last; `null` is no data, a gap.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `line` a trend, `area` the same filled below, `bar` one box per value from zero.

props.name: tone
props.doc: What the trend means: `brand` for a figure of the product, `success` or `danger` for a verdict, `neutral` for a quiet one.

props.name: endpoint
props.doc: A dot on the newest value of a line or an area.

props.name: height
props.doc: The height in pixels; the host sets the width.

props.name: highlight
props.doc: The index of the value in light: the full bar, or the dot on a line; the newest value when unset.

props.name: mark
props.doc: A line of reference across the trend, named at its end: `{ at: 43.06, label: '12-month average 43.06' }`.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: What the trend shows, for a screen reader: "Average receipt, the last 12 months". Unset, it is decoration.

UiSparkline.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: A small trend with no axes, beside the number it belongs to. Take it in a table cell, in a strip's actions beside a UiDelta, or under a headline in a UiChartCard.

decisions.label: Shapes
decisions.text: `line` and `area` stretch in one viewBox, with a dot on the newest value kept inside the box; a flat run stands at mid-height. `bar` draws HTML boxes from zero: the newest one (or `highlight`) is full, and the rest are pale with a line at their height, so each still reads. Bars stand 4px apart while there is room; a long run in a narrow host closes the gaps.

decisions.label: Gaps
decisions.text: A `null` is no data: the line breaks (a single value between two gaps is a dot), and a bar's place stays empty. A zero is a stub on the zero line.
Size and tone. The host sets the width, and `height` sets the height. Set `tone` to agree with the verdict beside it. `mark` draws one reference line, an average or a plan, named at its end.
In a card. In a UiChartCard it draws its shape pale on the first load and holds it still when there is nothing to draw.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: no tab stop, no keys; the number beside it carries the value.
doc.reader:
- Name: without `ariaLabel` it is hidden (`aria-hidden`), and the number beside it says the value; with one it is an image with that name, followed by the mark's label ("Average receipt, the last 12 months, 12-month average 43.06").
- Values: not read; a chart a reader can walk is UiAreaChart or UiBarChart.
- Hidden: on a card's first load, when the card has nothing to draw, and when no value is a number, whatever its name.
doc.states: `line`, `area` and `bar`, a dot on the newest value or on `highlight`, a gap (`null`) that breaks the line or leaves a bar's place empty, a loss below the zero line, a flat run at mid-height, a `mark` with its name, six tones. In a UiChartCard: its first load as a pale shape, nothing to draw held still, a refresh dimmed by the card. No hover or focus state of its own.
doc.notFor:
- A chart with axes, a legend and a tooltip: UiAreaChart or UiBarChart.
- A share of a whole: UiProgress.
- The verdict beside it: UiDelta.
- A single figure with a trend as a card: UiChartCard with `bleed="full"`.

UiSpinner.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: The sign that work is under way. Take it where a request runs and nothing draws one for you; a button, a badge, a switch and a row draw their own under `loading`.

decisions.label: Size
decisions.text: It is 16px unless the host sets `h-*` or `size-*`. It has no props.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: It is the loading state of buttons, badges, switches, rows, selects, list fields, uploads, toasts and chart cards.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: it takes no focus. A button that spins is UiButton `loading`, which handles the keys.
doc.reader:
- Name: with an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` it is a `status` with that name; without a name it is decoration, hidden. A `role` or `aria-hidden` you set never overrides this.
- Status: one that mounts with its name already in place is often not read out. Say the wait in a live region that was on the page before the request starts (UiCard `loading` has one), and let the spinner be its picture.
doc.states: One: turning, slower under reduced motion, never still; 16px unless the host sets `h-*` or `size-*`.
doc.notFor:
- Content on its way: UiSkeleton.
- Work of unknown length on a track: UiProgress `indeterminate`.
- A button, a badge, a switch or a row at work: UiButton, UiBadge, UiSwitch and UiListItem draw it themselves under `loading`.

UiSpinner.about: The sign that work is under way. Take it where a request runs and nothing draws one for you; a button, a badge, a switch and a row draw their own under `loading`.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The relation between the children, a step of the scale: `tight` 8, `group` 16, `title` 24, `block` 48, `section` 96 px.

props.name: direction
props.doc: `column` stacks the children; `row` lines them up on one line.

props.name: align
props.doc: Where the children stand across the stack. Unset, a column stretches them to its width and a row centers them on the line.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element: `div` by default; `section`, `ul`, `form` or `li` when the stack is one.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The things stacked, in order, each without a margin of its own.

UiStack.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: Things one under another or side by side, spaced by what they are to each other. Take it for the blocks of a page or a form; text on the left and a thing on the right is UiListItem.

decisions.label: Gaps
decisions.text: You name the relation, never a number. `tight` is 8, for the lines of one thing (a label and its control, a name and its count). `group` is 16, the default, for the things of one group (the fields of a form, a search over its list). `title` is 24, for a title and the text or the fields it names. `block` is 48, for the blocks of one page, and `section` is 96, for its sections. Importance is shown by size and color, not distance: a wider gap says "another thing", never "a bigger thing".

decisions.label: Margins
decisions.text: It is a gap, not a margin, so the children carry no space of their own. A UiSeparator among them keeps the rhythm, and a UiHeader legend after other content adds its own 32 to the gap: in the default stack that lands at `block` (48), in another it is that gap plus 32. The stack pads nothing: in a UiCard it is the body, and the card's gutter goes round it.

decisions.label: Rows
decisions.text: `row` is for things that share one line and nothing else (a badge beside a name, two buttons); they align on its vertical center. Text on the left and a thing on the right is UiListItem, not a `row`.

doc.keyboard: Not interactive: the children keep their own tab stops, in the order they are stacked.
doc.reader: - Element: nothing of its own; a `div`, or the element `as` names (`section`, `ul`, `form`, `li`), with the children read in order.
doc.states: None: the gap is one step of the scale and does not change with the content.
doc.notFor:
- Text on the left and a thing on the right: UiListItem.
- A table: UiTable.
- The toolbar row: UiTableToolbar owns it.
- Buttons joined into one capsule: UiButtonGroup.
- A grid of columns: the page lays it out itself.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The count as text (`v-model`): `null` when emptied. A number is plain text (`12`) parsed by its owner on use.

props.name: step
props.doc: How much a button or an arrow key moves the count.

props.name: min
props.doc: The lowest count the buttons and the arrows reach. Typing is not clamped: the form validates.

props.name: max
props.doc: The highest count the buttons and the arrows reach.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name for forms.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id when standalone. Inside UiField the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Hint shown while empty. Not a replacement for a label.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: Prevents editing while keeping the count focusable: something else sets it.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents input and interaction.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control invalid: red border and halo. Inside UiField the error sets this.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: a count is needed, said to a reader and to a form. Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible label.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The count changed: the number as text, `null` when emptied.

events.name: unsure
events.doc: `true` while the count holds text the locale cannot read for sure (`1.200` in Russian), which the model carries as written; `false` when it does not. Said on mount, then on every change.

slots.name: start
slots.doc: An addon before the count: a currency sign, an icon.

slots.name: end
slots.doc: A unit after the count, its short form: `pcs`, `kg`.

UiStepper.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A count of things with minus and plus at its edges, the count between them. Take it for pieces, people, nights: a whole number a person changes by one more often than types.

decisions.label: Count
decisions.text: It is a number field, the one UiInput draws with `numeric`: the value is text, empty is `null`, a number pasted or typed is read in the app's locale, and one it cannot read for sure is marked and told through `unsure`, as in UiInput; a press on it moves nothing and marks it at once. The step is `1` unless set; the buttons and ArrowUp and ArrowDown move by it and stop at `min` and `max`, which bound the buttons, not the typing. A count of things takes `min` (`0` or `1`): without it minus goes below zero. A fraction typed into it is carried as written, as a count past `max` is: the form checks it (`Number.isInteger`). The app takes or refuses a count in the same tick it is sent; a count confirmed later is a draft of the app's own. A unit stands after the count in `#end`, its short form (`pcs`, `kg`); an addon before it in `#start`.

decisions.label: Width
decisions.text: The count is 3em wide, room for four digits, and the stepper keeps that width in a field rather than stretching across it; given a width, the count takes the room between the buttons, so they stand at the edges and never move. A longer count is cut at its end.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Standalone it takes `invalid` and `ariaLabel`; inside UiField it reads id, error and required from the field.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes and listeners land on the input (`@blur`, `data-testid`); `class` and `style` on the capsule.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a form column under a UiField label; in a row of a list or a cart, beside the name of what is counted; joined with other controls in a UiButtonGroup.

doc.keyboard:
- `Tab`: reaches the count; the buttons are out of the tab order.
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown`: move the count by the step without moving the caret, and stop at `min` and `max`.
The buttons keep the focus and the caret in the count; `disabled` or `readonly` turns them off.
doc.reader:
- Count: a spinbutton named by `ariaLabel` or the field's label; it says its value and its bounds, and no value while the count is unsure. The unit in `#end` is not part of it.
- Buttons: named by what they change, "Decrease Guests" and "Increase Guests", disabled at a bound; out of the tab order.
- Errors: `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`; inside UiField the description and the error are read with it.
doc.states: Rest, focus, a button resting at a bound, disabled, readonly, invalid, with a unit, at `xs`, `sm` and `md`.
doc.notFor:
- A number with decimals or money: UiInput `numeric`.
- A mark from 1 to N: UiScaleInput.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: On or off (`v-model`).

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents toggling.

props.name: size
props.doc: Track size: `sm` 20px, `md` 24px.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name for forms: an on switch sends `value` under it, an off one nothing.

props.name: value
props.doc: Sent under `name` while on.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when the slot is empty and there is no field label; slot text wins over it.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The change is being saved: a spinner in the thumb, `aria-busy`, no toggling; focus stays.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id when standalone. Inside UiField the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the switch invalid: the track takes the danger tone while off. Inside UiField the error sets this.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: the switch must be on, said to a reader, with a star after its text. Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The state changed.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The visible label, to the right of the track; clicking it toggles.

UiSwitch.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: An on or off setting that applies at once. Take it where a change takes effect without saving a form.

decisions.label: Element
decisions.text: It is a `button` with `role="switch"`, so a screen reader says "switch, on".

decisions.label: Form
decisions.text: With a `name`, an on switch sends `value` (`on` by default) under that name with the form, and an off switch sends nothing, as a checkbox does.

decisions.label: Label
decisions.text: Label text goes in the default slot, toggles the switch on click, and is then its only name; without it, `ariaLabel` names the switch. Inside UiField it takes the field's label and description. The label starts at the middle of the track (2px down beside the 24px `md` track), so a long label wraps below.

decisions.label: Model
decisions.text: When the parent does not apply a change, the switch stays as the model says.

decisions.label: Loading
decisions.text: `loading` keeps the focus on the switch while the change is saved.

decisions.label: Invalid
decisions.text: An invalid switch that is off tints its track with the danger tone.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes land on the button, `class` and `style` on the root.

decisions.label: Size
decisions.text: Its `size` is a track, not a box, so it stays `sm` by default and does not follow the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`).

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: Beside UiCheckbox and UiRadio in a form column. A setting row is UiListItem `as="label"` with the switch in `#actions`. It also works as a `UiReveal` trigger.

doc.keyboard:
A native button.
- `Tab`: reaches it.
- `Enter` `Space`: toggle it.
`disabled` blocks it. `loading` blocks it too while the focus stays, the caller's own click included. A label in the slot toggles it on click, except while disabled.
doc.reader:
- Switch: `role="switch"`; it says on or off (`aria-checked`).
- Name: the slot text, else `ariaLabel`, else the field's label: one name only. A switch with no name warns in dev.
- Loading: `loading` says busy (`aria-busy`, `aria-disabled`).
- Errors: `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`, and the field's words are read with it.
- Required: `aria-required` says it is required, except in a group, whose legend says it once.
doc.states: Off, on, hover, focus, disabled (the plate, and the thumb in the disabled ink so on and off still look different), loading (a spinner in the thumb), invalid (the track in the danger tone while off; disabled wins over it), and the two tracks, `sm` and `md`.
doc.notFor:
- Saved with the form, not applied at once: UiCheckbox.
- One answer out of a few: UiRadioGroup.
- A toggle that is a button: UiButton `pressed`.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The columns in order; each names its `#cell.<key>` slot. A column is `{ key, label }` and may add `accessor(row)` (the value when it is not `row[key]`), `format(value, row)` (the text), `sortable` with `defaultSortDir` (`asc` or `desc`, the first press), `align: 'end'` (numbers, digit under digit), `width` (one CSS value, `120px` or `calc(…)`), `truncate` (one line, cut with a tooltip; cut columns with no width share the room left evenly).

props.name: items
props.doc: Rows of the current page. The table does not load, filter or sort them.

props.name: rowKey
props.doc: What tells rows apart: a field name or a function; `id` when unset, so rows without an `id` need it. A row without a key cannot be selected, and is known by its object: a parent that rebuilds its rows on every render remounts them all.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Rows are on their way: skeleton rows on the first load, the rows in view dimmed on a refresh.

props.name: skeletonRows
props.doc: Skeleton rows on the first load: the page size, so nothing moves when the rows arrive.

props.name: rowLabel
props.doc: Names a row for its checkbox: "Select Anna" instead of "Select row".

props.name: error
props.doc: Why the rows could not be loaded, in words for the reader, shown with a retry. A failed refresh shows the same plate in place of the rows.

props.name: selectable
props.doc: A checkbox on every row and one for the page in the header.

props.name: selection
props.doc: Keys of the selected rows (`v-model:selection`); the page checkbox adds or removes the page, Shift with a row's checkbox the rows from the last one marked. The parent drops the keys of rows it deletes.

props.name: isRowSelectable
props.doc: Which rows can be selected; the others show a disabled checkbox and stay out of the page checkbox.

props.name: sort
props.doc: The current sort (`v-model:sort`); a header click cycles the column's first direction, the other one, then none.

props.name: clickable
props.doc: Rows answer a click with `row-click` and show a pointer cursor. A pointer shortcut: the keyboard path to a row is a control in it (`#row-actions`), the row itself takes no tab stop.

props.name: filtered
props.doc: The page is empty because of a filter or a search: the empty text says so.

events.name: retry
events.doc: The retry of a failed load was pressed.

events.name: update:sort
events.doc: A header was clicked: the column and direction to sort by, `null` to drop the sort.

events.name: update:selection
events.doc: The selection changed; a new set, the one passed in is not mutated.

events.name: row-click
events.doc: A row was clicked with `clickable` on. Not for a click on a control inside the row, with a modifier key, or over selected text.

slots.name: row-actions
slots.doc: Controls of a row, in a column kept at the end when the table scrolls: ghost icon buttons.

slots.name: empty
slots.doc: Instead of the empty-page text; `filtered` says which wording it replaces.

UiTable.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: Records as rows under column headers, with sorting, selection and loading states. Take it inside UiDataTable, or alone for a list with no toolbar and no pages.

decisions.label: Data
decisions.text: It draws the page it is given and owns none of the data. A header click asks for a sort (`v-model:sort`). A checkbox marks a row (`v-model:selection`, a set of row keys); with Shift, by pointer or Shift+Space, it marks the range from the last row marked. The parent loads, filters and orders the rows, and keeps the selection to rows that still exist.

decisions.label: Look
decisions.text: One presentation: a hairline between rows, space between columns, a tint on the row under the pointer. The table draws no shell; the card around it does (`UiCard :padded="false"`). Its focus rings are drawn inside, since the card clips what sticks out.

decisions.label: Wide tables
decisions.text: A wide table scrolls sideways in its own box, with `#row-actions` kept at the end. Once it overflows, the box takes focus and the arrow keys scroll it, a side with more columns past it is shaded, and on a desktop pointer an arrow in the header's band pages the table toward it, so a narrow screen shows the table goes on and how to reach the rest. The arrow stands over the edge of the header cell under it, which is pressed beside it. An empty or a failed table shows its plate with neither. Once it scrolls, a column of short values (24 characters or fewer) keeps them on one line: the table has the room to the side.

decisions.label: Loading
decisions.text: The first load shows skeleton rows, as many as the page will hold; a refresh keeps the rows in view, dimmed and busy, and says it updates. In UiDataTable, a list that searches, the table stands on a floor: its empty and failed states fill it, and a skeleton holds as many rows as were in view, never fewer than fill it. A skeleton cell draws the lines its column holds (`lines`, 2 for a UiMoneyCell or UiDateCell), so the rows arrive at their height. With `#row-actions`, it holds the square of one icon button at the app's size, so the actions column keeps its width and the row its height. The other columns take their width from their content, which a skeleton does not have: those without a `width` settle when the rows arrive.

Empty and failed. An empty page is UiNoData: "no records yet", or, with `filtered`, "nothing matches"; `#empty` puts one with its own action in its place. A failed load is UiNoData `danger` with the message and Retry. A failed refresh shows the same plate in place of the rows, and Retry brings the skeleton back.

decisions.label: Rows
decisions.text: A row without a key keeps its DOM node for the life of the page, so a sort moves the row with its record. The totals row shows only when there are rows. A cell of an object needs `format`, `accessor` or its slot; without one it draws a dash.

decisions.label: Focus
decisions.text: It stays where the person is when the rows change under it: a sort leaves it on the same control of the same row, a row deleted hands it to the same control of the row now in its place (the row above when it was the last), and a page left without rows gives it to the table's box. A focus that went elsewhere, into a window opened from a row, is not pulled back; that window gives it back to its own trigger. A row's own control turned off for a moment keeps it. A row deleted from its UiMenu is handed on the same way: the menu gives the focus back to its button first. A row removed while a window opened from it holds the focus (a question's `action`) is handed on too: the window gives the focus to the same control of the row now in its place.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: They reach the `<table>`, so `aria-label` names it and its page checkbox; `class` and `style` stay on the root.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In UiDataTable, under UiTableToolbar and over UiPagination, with UiMoneyCell and UiDateCell as its cells. Alone in a `UiCard :padded="false"` when a list needs no toolbar and no pages.

doc.keyboard:
- `Tab`: once the table overflows, reaches its scroll box first; then the page checkbox, a sortable header, each row's checkbox and the controls in `#row-actions`, and the Retry of a failed load.
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight` `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown`: on the scroll box, scroll it.
- `Enter` `Space`: on a sortable header, a button, turn it.
- `Space`: on a checkbox, marks the row.
- `Shift+Space`: on a checkbox, marks the range from the last row marked.
A row is reached through a control in `#row-actions`, never by a click on the row alone. A header pressed while rows load asks for nothing and keeps the focus; Retry is held the same way and leaves the focus in the table.
doc.reader:
- Table: named by the `aria-label` the page gives it, and so are its page checkbox ("Select all on this page of Orders") and its scroll box.
- Sortable header: says its direction (`aria-sort`); a sort a press asked for is said once the app sends it back ("Sorted by Name, ascending").
- Row checkbox: "Select row", or "Select Anna" with `rowLabel`, and says its shortcut.
- Columns: the selection column and the actions column have hidden names.
- Row: says whether it is selected (`aria-selected`).
- Status: one region, present from the start and drawn empty, says "Loading…", the empty words, from a moment after the table mounts. The plate of an empty page is no second live region; a UiNoData of your own in `#empty` takes `role="none"` for the same.
- Failed load: announced by its plate.
- Refresh: `aria-busy` on the rows.
doc.states: A first load (skeleton rows, as many as the page holds), rows, a refresh (the rows kept, dimmed to 60% and busy), empty with nothing yet, empty because of a filter (`filtered`), a failed load (UiNoData `danger` with Retry), a failed refresh (the same plate in place of the rows), a sort, a selection with the page checkbox mixed, a totals row shown only with rows, and a wide table that scrolls in its box.
doc.notFor:
- A list screen: UiDataTable, with its toolbar, pages and selection strip.
- Rows of settings or facts: UiListItem rows in a UiList.
- A list of names that grows from its last row: UiListField.
- The changes of one event: UiLog's own table.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The columns state from `useTableColumns`: every column, the hidden ones, which may be hidden. The table draws its `visible`.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder for the button: the toolbar row's, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`) when unset.

UiTableColumns.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A button with a panel where a person picks which columns a table shows. The table toolbar draws it from its `columns` prop; it is not placed by hand.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.text: The panel is a UiPopover with a checkbox per column, applied at once. A required column is ticked, held and marked "Required". The last column shown cannot be hidden and is marked "Last one". The marks are one word, so the one that comes with the last tick does not widen the panel under the pointer, and the column's own name keeps its room. Reset in the footer returns to the default; it is held while nothing differs, so the list never moves under the pointer. From six columns the shown stand first under "Shown" and the hidden under "Hidden", a line between, so the list says why its order is not the table's.

A view, not a filter. The choice is a personal view, so the button shows no count. `useTableColumns` keeps the choice per kind of table; this component is the view of that state, and the page draws the table from the state's `visible`. A stored choice arrives once the page runs in the browser, so a page rendered on the server shows the default columns for a moment.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: The toolbar draws it first in the right cluster, across the row from UiFilter and UiDateRange. UiDataTable takes the same state as its `columns`.

decisions.label: Button
decisions.text: The button names itself in a tooltip. Attributes land on the button, not on the panel.

doc.keyboard:
On the button:
- `Tab`: reaches it.
- `Enter` `Space`: open the panel; the focus goes to the list, or to its search when there are six columns or more.
In the panel, where the list is one tab stop and Reset the next; from six columns up the search takes the list's tab stop, and its cross is one more once it holds text:
- `ArrowDown` `ArrowUp`: in the list, move the highlight.
- `Home` `End`: jump.
- `Enter` `Space`: tick.
- `A–Z`: jumps to the column that starts with the letter.
- `Escape`: closes the panel and returns the focus to the button.
- `Tab`: cycles inside the panel.
doc.reader:
- Button: named "Columns" (`aria-label`, and the tooltip), with `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`.
- Panel: a dialog with the same name.
- List: a multi-select listbox named "Columns", each column an option that says whether it is ticked.
- Held column: says "Required" or "Last one" after its name.
- Count: under the list, a status region, read as it changes: "2 hidden" or "All columns shown".
doc.states: Rest, open, a column ticked, a required column held with "Required", the last column shown held with "Last one", Reset held while nothing differs; the choice kept across a remount, and the default columns for a moment on a page rendered on the server. No count on the button: the choice is a view, not a filter.
doc.notFor:
- Narrowing the rows: UiFilter.
- A period: UiDateRange.
- One choice among a few: UiSelect.
- A second menu beside a toolbar: never; the toolbar draws it from `columns`.

props.name: search
props.doc: The search text (`v-model:search`); the field is always there. Sent as typed, spaces included, after a 250 ms pause or at Enter.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.doc: What the search looks in; the field's placeholder and its name.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The columns menu: the state from `useTableColumns`. The button stands first in the right cluster; without it the columns are fixed.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder for the row: `xs` for a dense row, `sm` (36 px), `md` for a comfortable one; unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`). The slots get it as `{ size }`.

events.name: update:search
events.doc: The search text, after the pause or at Enter.

slots.name: start
slots.doc: What narrows the list, after the search: a period, filters; bind `size` on them.

slots.name: end
slots.doc: What acts on the list, after the columns menu: catalog buttons, then the main action last; bind `size`. Not another columns menu.

UiTableToolbar.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: The row above a list, with a built-in search, what narrows the list on the left and what acts on it on the right. UiDataTable builds it from its own props and slots.

decisions.label: Clusters
decisions.text: `#start` holds what narrows the list (a period in UiDateRange, filters). `#end` holds what acts on it: catalog buttons, then the main action last. The columns menu is built in too; when the toolbar is given its state, it stands first on the right.

decisions.label: Search
decisions.text: The search is built in and always present (`v-model:search`). The field takes every key; the value goes out after a 250 ms pause, and Enter sends it at once. A value set from outside (a reset, the URL) replaces what was being typed. When a host applies the model late, the toolbar's own sent values coming back are not taken for an outside value, so what was typed since stays, and a clear or a step back made while a value is on its way is sent too. A host that drops a value it was sent without a word keeps it counted as on its way, and takes one outside value equal to it for its answer.

decisions.label: Size
decisions.text: Controls in the row share one step, `size`: the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), or `sm` (36 px) if unset; `xs` for a dense row, `md` for a comfortable one. The slots get it as `{ size }` to bind on their controls.

decisions.label: Layout
decisions.text: On a narrow screen the search takes a line of its own and the rest share the line under it. The row is padded 16 px, so it lines up with the table's cells under it and with its footer; the card around them is the shell.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In UiDataTable's card, above the table; UiDataTable builds it from its search, `#filters`, `#actions` and `columns`. UiFilter and UiDateRange stand in `#start`, UiTableColumns first in the right cluster. A host may make it `inert` while a selection strip covers it.

doc.keyboard:
- `Tab`: reaches the search first (its cross next, while it holds text), then the controls in `#start`, the columns button and the controls in `#end`, in the order they stand.
- `/`: from anywhere outside a field, goes to the search of the first list in view, in the window open over the page when there is one. An app that takes the key itself calls `preventDefault` on it first.
In the search, where every key narrows the list after a 250 ms pause:
- `Enter`: sends at once and does not submit a form around it.
- `Escape`: empties it and keeps the focus, as the cross does.
Leaving the field sends what was typed. The Enter that confirms an IME candidate sends nothing.
doc.reader:
- Search: a landmark (`role="search"`) named like its field, by `searchPlaceholder`, "Search" by default; UiDataTable adds its own name ("Search Invoices"), so two lists on one page keep their searches apart. The field says its shortcut, `/` (`aria-keyshortcuts`).
- Row: has no name and no role.
- Slots: what they hold is read as the controls they are.
doc.states: Rest, text in the search (the cross shows), a pending send, a value set from outside that replaces the typing, `inert` under a selection strip; the row at `xs`, `sm` and `md`, and on a narrow screen the search on a line of its own.
doc.notFor:
- One block of table, toolbar, pages and states: UiDataTable.
- A search outside a list: UiInput `type="search"`.
- A second columns menu: never in `#end`; the toolbar draws it from `columns`.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: Value of the active tab (`v-model`).

props.name: tabs
props.doc: Tabs in order: `value`, `label`, `disabled`, and a `badge` with its `badgeTone` and `badgeLabel` (what it means, in words).

props.name: variant
props.doc: `panel` (the default) is the header of a block inside the card shell; `underline` is a strip on its own.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the tab set.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of a tab on the control ladder: `sm` 36px, `md` 44px. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`); `xs` is read as `sm`.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The new value, for `v-model`.

slots.name: header
slots.doc: Above the strip, inside the shell; `panel` only. What the tabs do not switch.

UiTabs.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: Panes of one screen, one at a time. Take it when a page or a record splits into parts a person moves between; a choice with no panes is UiRadioGroup `segmented`.

decisions.label: Panes
decisions.text: The root is a `<div>`. The active tab's pane is the slot named after its value (`#overview`); a tab without a slot renders no pane. A pane that is not shown is unmounted, so a form in it must keep its values in the parent, not in the DOM. The pane follows `modelValue`, not the tabs: a value whose tab is gone (taken away with a permission) still shows its slot, named by no tab, so set `modelValue` to a tab that stays when the tabs change.

decisions.label: Variants
decisions.text: `underline` is a strip on its own. `panel` puts the strip inside the card shell as the header of a block, with `#header` above it; inside a UiCard's `#header`, the card is the shell and the panel draws none of its own. A tab stands on the control ladder (`size`, else the app's step).

decisions.label: Focus
decisions.text: A focused tab rings inward with its underline kept, so no scroll edge or card clips the ring. In forced colors the selected tab is highlighted.

decisions.label: Direction
decisions.text: The strip follows the reading direction: on a right-to-left page it starts at the right, and its paging arrow and faded edge stand on the side where tabs wait.

decisions.label: Routing
decisions.text: The active tab is not synced to the URL; the consumer does that around `v-model`.

doc.keyboard:
The WAI-ARIA tab pattern: the strip has one tab stop, the active tab, and a move activates the tab and focuses it.
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: the tab to the left and the tab to the right, round the ends; a disabled tab is passed over. On a right-to-left page the strip starts at the right, so `ArrowRight` is the tab before and `ArrowLeft` the tab after.
- `Home` `End`: the first and the last tab.
- `Tab`: on to the pane's first control, or to the pane when it holds none.
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown`: stay the page's: the strip is horizontal.
- `Alt` `Ctrl` `Meta`: a chord with them stays the browser's.
The paging arrows of a wide set are for the pointer, outside the tab order.
doc.reader:
- Strip: a `tablist` named by `ariaLabel`.
- Tab: says whether it is selected (`aria-selected`) and controls its pane (`aria-controls`) only while the pane is there; a disabled tab says so (`aria-disabled`).
- Pane: a `tabpanel` named by its tab.
- Badge: read in the words of `badgeLabel`, with the number hidden; a bare number warns in dev, since the reader would hear the label and the number as one.
doc.states: Active, with the brand ink and underline; rest; hover, only when enabled; disabled, in the disabled ink, not chosen by a click or a key; focus, ringing inward with the underline kept. `panel` in the card shell, with `#header` and a rule above the strip, and inside a UiCard's `#header` with no shell of its own; `underline` on its own. A set wider than the strip scrolls, with faded edges and arrows on desktop. In forced colors the selected tab is highlighted. `sm` is 36px, `md` 44px.
doc.notFor:
- A choice with no panes: UiRadioGroup `segmented`.
- Pages of one set: UiPagination.
- The places of the app: UiAppShell.
- A block shown or hidden in place: UiReveal.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The text (`v-model`); empty is `''`.

props.name: rows
props.doc: Visible lines before the user resizes the control.

props.name: name
props.doc: Native name for forms.

props.name: id
props.doc: Own id when standalone. Inside UiField the field's id takes precedence.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Hint shown while empty. Not a replacement for a label.

props.name: maxlength
props.doc: Maximum number of characters.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: Prevents editing while keeping the control focusable.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Prevents input and interaction.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Marks the control invalid: red border and halo. Inside UiField the error sets this.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: a value is needed, said to a reader and to a form (native `required`). Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when there is no visible label. A prop, not `aria-label`: the root is the capsule, the name belongs to the control.

props.name: size
props.doc: Height of one row on the control ladder; defaults to the app's step.

props.name: resize
props.doc: `vertical` gives the user a handle; `none` fixes the height at `rows`; `auto` grows with the text.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: The value changed.

UiTextarea.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A multi-line text field in the input capsule. Take it for a note, an address or a bio.

decisions.label: Height
decisions.text: The height comes from `rows`, from the resize handle, or from `resize="auto"`, which grows from `rows` up to 24rem and then scrolls. One row stands on the control ladder (`size`, else the app's step), so it lines up with UiInput.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: It reads the field context; standalone, the name goes through `ariaLabel`.

decisions.label: Attributes
decisions.text: Attributes and listeners land on the textarea, `class` and `style` on the capsule.

decisions.label: Model
decisions.text: The field shows the model: when the owner refuses a change, or a form resets, it goes back to the model and the caret stays where it was.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: The value is text, and empty is `''`, never `null`.

decisions.label: Length
decisions.text: `maxlength` cuts off text past the limit and shows no counter; the caller writes one into UiField's `#meta`.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: In a form column beside UiInput, inside UiField, or in a UiModal or a UiCrudDrawer that sends on Cmd+Enter from it.

doc.keyboard:
A native textarea.
- `Tab`: reaches it.
- `Enter`: adds a line.
- `Meta+Enter` `Ctrl+Enter`: send from it in a UiModal or a UiCrudDrawer; that key belongs to the surface, not to the textarea.
Nothing is sent while an IME composes. `readonly` keeps it focusable and blocks typing; `disabled` blocks the focus too. The handle resizes with the pointer.
doc.reader:
- Field: a text box named by `ariaLabel` or the field's label, never by the placeholder. A textarea with no name warns in dev.
- Errors: `invalid` sets `aria-invalid`. Inside UiField the description and the error are read with it once, and `aria-required` says it is required.
- Caller attributes: a caller's `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` reach it when the field sets none.
doc.states: Rest, hover, focus (the capsule draws the ring), disabled (its plate, nothing sent), readonly, invalid (red border and halo; disabled wins over it), with a handle, a fixed height, `auto` growing to 24rem and then scrolling, and one row on each step of the ladder.
doc.notFor:
- One line: UiInput.
- Names added one by one: UiListField.
- A counter under it: the caller's text in UiField `#meta`.

props.name: modelValue
props.doc: The time, `HH:mm` (`v-model`); `null` for none.

props.name: step
props.doc: Minutes between two rows of the Minute column.

props.name: min
props.doc: The first time the window allows, `HH:mm`.

props.name: max
props.doc: The last time the window allows, `HH:mm`; a `min` after it wraps the window past midnight.

props.name: clearable
props.doc: A cross that empties the field.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: Shown while empty; defaults to "Pick a time".

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The field cannot be changed.

props.name: required
props.doc: Standalone only: empty is an error, said to a reader, and no cross. Inside UiField the field's `required` says so.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Standalone only: the value is wrong. Inside UiField the field's error says so.

props.name: name
props.doc: Sends the time with a form, under this name.

props.name: id
props.doc: Id of the trigger, standalone; inside UiField the field's id wins.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Standalone only: the accessible name. Inside UiField the label names it.

props.name: hourCycle
props.doc: 12 hours with an AM/PM column, or 24; unset, the app's language decides (`2:30 PM` in American English, `14:30` in Russian). The field writes the time the same way.

props.name: size
props.doc: Step of the control ladder. Unset, the app's size (`createGrani({ size })`), `sm` by default.

events.name: update:modelValue
events.doc: A time was picked (`HH:mm`), or `null` when cleared.

UiTimePicker.attrs: Attributes: `class` and `style` stay on the outer element; the rest (native attributes, aria-*, data-testid) reach the control inside it.

doc.lead: A form field for a time of day, in the input capsule on the control ladder. Take it beside a UiDatePicker or a UiCalendar for a day and its hours.

decisions.label: Value
decisions.text: The value is `HH:mm` (`10:30`); one with seconds (`14:30:00`) is read to the minute, and a change sends `HH:mm`. It is shown as the app's language writes a time: `14:30` in Russian, `2:30 PM` in American English.

decisions.label: Panel
decisions.text: The button opens a UiPopover with two listboxes side by side, Hour and Minute (a third, Period, in a 12-hour locale); each shows five rows and a half and scrolls the rest (`useVisibleRows`), scrolled on open to the chosen row. A press on an hour sets the value at once, the current minute clamped to the nearest one the window still allows (the first allowed minute with no value yet), keeps the panel open and moves the focus to Minute; a press on a minute sets it and closes the panel, the focus back on the field. A press on a period keeps the hour's number and flips its half of the day, and stays open.

decisions.label: Typing
decisions.text: Digits build a time without the search row UiSelect has: one or two are the hour (`9` lights 9, `14` lights 14), three are `H:mm` (`930`, `230`) while the minute fits (`183` stays 18:3_), four `HH:mm` (`0930`, `1437`). A mark after the hour (`9:30`, `9.30`, `9 30`) ends the hour where it is, and a lone digit after it is the minute's tens. Digits of other scripts count as theirs. The hour reads on the 24-hour clock unless `a` or `p` sets its half of the day, and a 12-hour field says the half it reads as it is typed (`2:30 AM`); `a` or `p` with nothing typed moves the time held to that half. A time that does not exist (`9:75`, `2400`) is no time, never one nearby. The field shows what was typed until Enter takes it to the minute, off the step too, and closes; a time that is not one, or one outside the window, is not taken: the field is marked invalid until the text changes, and a reader hears why. A press away takes it too when it is written in full: the hour and two digits of the minute, and in a 12-hour language its half of the day or an hour past 12 (where the half cannot be typed as `a` or `p`, Korean or Arabic, the minute is enough); anything else is dropped there, and a reader hears why. While it is typed the columns show it chosen, the minute once both of its digits are in, off the step too. Backspace takes back the last key, the half of the day too; Escape, the cross, a press on a row and an arrow drop it and give the time held back.
