Typing opens the panel from the closed field too, and the keys typed while it opens go on with the time, so the pointer picks on the step and the keys reach any minute.

decisions.label: Hours
decisions.text: The app's language decides: a 24-hour one draws 00…23 in two columns and writes `14:30`; a 12-hour one draws 12, 1…11 and a Period column of the language's AM/PM words and writes `2:30 PM`. `hourCycle` sets it for every language.

decisions.label: Window
decisions.text: `min` and `max` are `HH:mm`. `min` after `max` is read as a window that wraps past midnight (a night shift, 22:00–06:00), not an empty one. An hour with no allowed minute in the window, and a minute outside it, are shown but disabled; a value outside the window is kept and reads invalid.

decisions.label: Step
decisions.text: Minutes in a column are multiples of `step` (1..60, a bad step falls back to 1); the default is 5. A value off the step is kept and listed in its own place.

decisions.label: Empty
decisions.text: No time is `null`: the cross sends `null`, and `null` or an empty string reads as none. With `name` a form gets the field's name with an empty value, as a native time input sends it.

decisions.label: Odd values
decisions.text: `9:30` is read as `09:30`. A value that is not a time (`25:99`) counts as none.

decisions.label: Width
decisions.text: The field keeps its width when a time is picked or cleared; cut in a narrow column, the whole time shows in a tooltip on hover. A required field shows no cross.

decisions.label: Field
decisions.text: Inside UiField it reads id, error and required. `focus()` puts the focus on it.

doc.keyboard:
- `Tab`: reaches the combobox.
- `ArrowDown` `Alt+ArrowDown` `Enter` `Space`: open the panel, on the closed field.
- `0–9`: a digit opens the panel and starts the typed time; a mark after the hour (`:` `.` `-` `,` or a space) ends it; in a 12-hour language `a`/`p` set its half of the day.
- `Alt` `Ctrl` `Meta`: a chord with them stays the browser's, on the field and in the panel; only `Alt+ArrowDown` on the closed field is its own.
In the open panel:
- `ArrowUp` `ArrowDown`: move within a column, over the enabled rows; `Home`/`End` to its ends.
- `ArrowLeft` `ArrowRight`: move to the next or the previous column.
- `Enter` `Space`: picks the row, as a press does; on Minute (or Period with no Minute column left to fill) it closes the panel too. With a time typed, Enter takes it and Space is a mark.
- `Backspace`: takes back the last typed key.
- `Escape`: closes the panel; inside a window it closes only the panel.
- `Tab`: moves to the next column and goes round inside, as in UiDatePicker's calendar; `Escape` leaves.
The cross clears the value and keeps the focus on the field.
doc.reader:
- Field: a combobox named by `ariaLabel` or the field's label and says the time as the locale prints it, or the placeholder.
- Panel: Hour, Minute and, in a 12-hour locale, Period are listboxes named in words, the chosen row marked, the focus moving with the rows (roving, not `aria-activedescendant`: three listboxes side by side read better as one tab stop each).
- Icon: the clock icon is hidden from a screen reader.
- Errors: a time outside `min` and `max`, a typed time refused, or a field error, sets `aria-invalid`; `required` sets `aria-required`; the field's description and error are read with it once.
- Typed time: a time not taken is said in words, "Not a time", "Time outside the allowed range" or "Time not kept: type it in full".
doc.states: Empty, a time picked, open with the chosen hour and minute (and period) highlighted, a time off the step (listed in its place), a time outside the window (kept, reads invalid), a value that is not a time (shown as empty, nothing sent), disabled (nothing sent, the panel closes), invalid, required (no cross), `clearable` with the cross, and joined in a UiButtonGroup. The width holds in all of them.
doc.notFor:
- A day: UiDatePicker.
- A duration in minutes: UiInput `numeric`.
- Any other pick from a list: UiSelect itself.

props.name: placement
props.doc: Where the stack stands on the bottom edge; `start` and `end` follow the reading direction.

UiToaster.attrs: Anything else lands on the root element: native attributes, aria-*, data-testid.

doc.lead: The place where toasts appear. Put it once at the app root (its root component or a layout), beside UiConfirm.

decisions.label: Root
decisions.text: Never put it in a page or a component: every `useToast()` call anywhere lands in this one stack, and a second toaster in the same app warns in dev. Without a toaster, a toast is queued and never seen, and dev says so once. It stands at the end of the `body`, or where `createGrani({ teleport })` says.

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: By default it stands at the bottom start of the screen (`placement`: `bottom-start`, `bottom`, `bottom-end`; start and end follow the reading direction), clear of the safe area. On a phone it stands at the top, where it covers no pinned footer and no Save button. The newest toast is in front, and up to three are shown; older ones peek behind it, smaller and as tall as it, so a short one never hides behind a long one nor a long one stands over a short one as an empty frame, and wait with their timers paused until there is room. Under the pointer or the focus, the pile opens into a column and every timer stops until both have left.

Over a drawer. The stack stands above every layer and leaves no room for the one under it. On a phone, at the top, it covers the drawer's header (its cross and title) while it stays; on a screen under 850px wide, at the bottom start, it covers the end of a drawer's footer, its Cancel. It goes by itself, by a swipe or with its close button. In a UiAppShell the stack at the bottom start stands over the sidebar's `#footer` while it shows: with a control there that is used often (a theme switch), set `placement="bottom-end"`.

decisions.label: Toast
decisions.text: A toast is a row on a card: the glyph of its tone (or its own `icon`; `neutral` has none), a title, a detail line, one action and a close button. It closes when its `duration` runs out (5 s, 7 s for an error, 13 s with an action, time to reach it by `F8`), on the close button, on Escape while focused, or on a swipe away from the screen edge it stands at (down, or up on a phone) or toward its side. Its action runs once. A long line wraps; a long detail is cut at three lines. A toast never holds what the page needs to go on: that is a dialog or inline text.

decisions.label: Again
decisions.text: The same toast shown again while one stands, shown or waiting (the same title, detail, tone, glyph and `announce`, no action), is that one card: it comes to the front with its whole time again, and its id is returned. Five presses of Copy are one "Copied", not a pile of five. A toast with an action is always new: two Undo buttons undo two things.

decisions.label: The key
decisions.text: F8 is a function key no browser uses for itself, and the key a toast region is commonly reached by. F6 is the browser's own walk between its panes, and a letter with Alt or Ctrl+Alt types text on some keyboards. The region's name includes the key, so a screen reader user hears how to get in. The toaster stands above every layer, and an open window's focus trap lets the focus into it.

doc.keyboard:
- `F8`: from anywhere on the page, with a window open or not, moves the focus to the newest toast's action (its close button when it has none); `F8` again goes back.
- `Tab`: reaches a toast's action and its close button.
- `Escape`: on a focused toast, closes it.
When a toast closes with the focus in it (Escape, its close button, its action), the focus goes back to where it came from. Focus in the stack opens the pile and pauses every timer until it leaves; a toast beyond the three shown is `inert` until it moves up. The swipe is for a pointer; the keyboard closes a toast with the button or Escape.
doc.reader:
- Live regions: two stand on the page before any toast arrives.
- Error: with `priority: 'high'`, an alert, read at once.
- Other toasts: a status, read at a pause.
- Content: each is read with its title and detail.
- Several: toasts that come together are read one after another in the order they came.
- Again: the same toast shown again while it stands is read once more.
- Silent: `announce: false` is not read (for a control that has already said it).
- Stack: a region named "Notifications (F8)".
- Close button: each is named "Close" and the toast's title.
- Action: its label, described by the toast's title, so F8 landing on it says what it acts on.
- Glyph: hidden.
doc.states: One toast per tone (`neutral` without a glyph, `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info`); a glyph of its own; loading from `promise`, then a new toast with its outcome; with an action; open until closed (`persistent`); the same toast again, one card; long text wrapping and a detail cut at three lines; a pile of three with older ones peeking behind, opened under the pointer or the focus; placed at the start, the center or the end of the bottom edge, and at the top on a phone.
doc.notFor:
- What the page needs to go on: UiModal or inline text.
- A question: UiConfirm.
- A field's validation: stays by the field in UiField.
- A load that failed: UiNoData `tone="danger"` with Retry, inline.

props.name: content
props.doc: The hint. Empty or absent means no tooltip.

props.name: side
props.doc: Preferred side; it flips when that side has no room, and a side hint with room on neither side goes below or above.

slots.name: default
slots.doc: The trigger: one element or a single-root component the hint describes. It should be focusable.

UiTooltip.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: A short text hint beside its trigger. Take it for detail a dense row has no room for.

decisions.label: Showing
decisions.text: It shows on hover and on keyboard focus, but not when a script gives the focus back after a click. When the pointer moves from one trigger to the next, the next hint opens at once. A tap shows it on a trigger that only shows something (a cut text, a date); a tap on a button that opens something only opens it. A press outside hides the hint and still reaches the window under it. A long word wraps inside it.

decisions.label: Content
decisions.text: Text only. It is never the only place for what must be read by a person who cannot reach it: a natively disabled button takes no focus, so its reason is visible text beside it; UiButton and UiIconButton with `disabledReason` keep the focus and say their reason in one.

decisions.label: Trigger
decisions.text: Attributes and listeners set on the tooltip reach the trigger along with the trigger's own, so it can stand inside a popover's or a menu's `#trigger`. The trigger is one element or a single-root component (not a fragment, not another tooltip) and should be focusable (a static badge takes `tabindex="0"`). When the panel is pushed aside, its tail stays on the trigger; a trigger that goes away takes the hint with it. The pointer may cross onto the tooltip (WCAG 1.4.13).

decisions.label: Placement
decisions.text: UiTruncate and UiDateCell stand on it; UiButton and UiIconButton draw the same hint for the reason they are off. It names an icon button where a sighted user needs the name (the sidebar's toggle, a table's columns).

doc.keyboard:
Keyboard focus on the trigger shows it at once, and blur hides it; a focus a script gives back after a click does not show it.
- `Escape`: hides it first and goes no further, so a window under it stays until the next `Escape`.
The hint itself takes no focus and holds nothing focusable.
doc.reader:
- Role: a `tooltip`.
- Description: while shown, it describes the trigger (`aria-describedby`), next to any description you set; with no `content` there is none.
- Repeated words: a hint that repeats the trigger's own name (an icon button's `ariaLabel`) or a description it already has (a disabled button's reason) is not wired, so the words are read once.
- Tail: hidden.
doc.states: Hidden; shown after a short delay on hover, at once on keyboard focus, on a tap on a touch screen, and at once when the pointer moves from one trigger to the next. On one of four sides (`side`), flipped when that side has no room, and pushed aside at the screen edge with the tail kept on the trigger; a `left` or `right` hint with room on neither side goes below or above, never over its trigger. Long text and a long word wrap. One hint on the page at a time.
doc.notFor:
- A hint with a link or a control: UiPopover.
- The reason a button is off: UiButton or UiIconButton `disabledReason`, which keeps the focus and says it; for a button natively `disabled`, visible text beside it.
- A cut value in a cell: UiTruncate, built on it.
- A date: UiDateCell, built on it.

props.name: text
props.doc: The text; the whole of it goes to the tooltip while it is cut.

UiTruncate.attrs: Attributes are placed by the component itself: its description says where.

doc.lead: One line of text cut with an ellipsis, its whole text in a UiTooltip while it is cut. Take it for a name or a title in a narrow place: a table cell, a list row, a file name.

decisions.label: Tooltip
decisions.text: While the text is really cut, the whole text shows in the tooltip on hover and tap, as UiDateCell shows the full date; text that fits has no tooltip. The cut is measured, not assumed: when a column widens or the text changes, it is measured again, and the tooltip follows.

decisions.label: Props
decisions.text: `text` is the only prop; markup in a slot handles its own cut. The root is a block `<span>` with no tab stop, and attributes land on it.

doc.keyboard: No tab stop: the span is not focusable, so the tooltip opens on hover and on tap, not from the keyboard; for the keyboard, put a control beside it that leads to the whole text.
doc.reader:
- Text: the whole text, always: the cut is CSS, and the span holds every character.
- Tooltip: while shown, it describes the span (`aria-describedby`) with the same words again.
doc.states: Fits, with no tooltip and no native `title`; cut, with the whole text in the tooltip on hover and tap. The cut is measured on mount, on resize, when a web font arrives and when `text` changes, with one pixel of slack; an empty text is a cut of nothing.
doc.notFor:
- Markup in a slot: it handles its own cut (`truncate` on the element).
- A date: UiDateCell.
- The label of a badge: UiBadge cuts it itself.
- Text that may wrap: plain text.

types.name: AnchorTrigger
types.doc: Where a floating panel stands relative to its trigger: below or above with a flip when the preferred side has no room, left or right for a tooltip, clamped to the viewport. Pure arithmetic on numbers, no DOM: the edge cases (a panel taller than the screen, a trigger at the right edge, an unmeasured panel on the first frame) are tested, not hoped for.

fields.name: panel
fields.doc: Panel size; `0` means not measured yet (first frame): no flip, no clamp by height.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: Gap between trigger and panel.

fields.name: margin
fields.doc: Safe distance from the viewport edge.

fields.name: prefer
fields.doc: Preferred side. The panel flips only when its side has no room and the other has more; `auto` flips as soon as it does not fit.

fields.name: align
fields.doc: Alignment on the cross axis: `start` with the trigger's start edge, `end` with its end edge, `center` on its middle. Under a panel that stands above or below, the edges follow the reading direction (`rtl`).

fields.name: rtl
fields.doc: The trigger reads right to left: its start edge is the right one. Without it, the left.

fields.name: matchTriggerWidth
fields.doc: Panel as wide as the trigger (selects): the clamp uses the trigger width.

fields.name: capToRoom
fields.doc: The panel is capped to the room on its side (`room`), so it stands beside the trigger and never covers it.

fields.name: placement
fields.doc: Where it ended up; a tooltip's tail and the tests need it.

fields.name: room
fields.doc: The height there is on that side, between the trigger and the viewport's margin.

members.name: announce
members.doc: Says `text` to a screen reader through one polite live region at the end of the page, outside any button: a button's content is presentational, and some readers never say a region inside one. The region outlives the control that spoke, so an outcome that arrives after a menu row has closed is still heard. While a modal window is open (`aria-modal`), the words are said in a region inside it instead, the one that holds the focus or else the last opened: a reader keeps to it and may not hear the page's. A window that closes before the words are written is passed for the page. Emptied first and filled a moment later, so the same words said twice are read twice. Client only; on the server it does nothing.

members.name: createAnnouncer
members.type: () => { say(write: Write, words: string): void; stop(): void; }
members.doc: One reader's voice: lines said one after another in the order they came, each emptied first, written a beat later and held a beat before the next empties its region. The page's live region speaks through one; UiToaster speaks its toasts through its own.

members.name: hush
members.doc: Drops the page's line that waits or is under way, and says nothing: between tests, since a line is written on the real clock a beat after it was said, when the next test's page may have no document.

members.name: useSplitAttrs
members.type: () => { attrs: Attrs; rootClass: ComputedRef<never>; rootStyle: ComputedRef<never>; control: ComputedRef<{ [k: string]: unknown; }>; }
members.doc: The caller's attributes for a component whose root is not its control: `class` and `style` stay on the root, the rest (`data-*`, `aria-*`, `required`, `@blur`) reaches the control. Pair with `defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })`.

members.name: ownWhereSet
members.type: (caller: Record<string, unknown>, own: Record<string, unknown>) => Record<string, unknown>
members.doc: The caller's attributes with the component's own over them, but only where the component has a value: an `aria-invalid` it does not set must not wipe the one the caller gave.

members.name: joinIds
members.doc: Ids for one `aria-describedby`: the caller's and the component's, neither wiping the other.

members.name: parseDay
members.doc: The day as a UTC midnight, or null for an empty or malformed string.

members.name: addMonths
members.type: (iso: IsoDay, n: number, day?: number) => IsoDay
members.doc: Moves by months and keeps the day where it can: 31 January plus a month is 28 or 29 February. `day` is the day of the month to aim for, so a run of hops from the 31st lands on the 31st again in March instead of creeping down to the 28th.

members.name: splitTypedTime
members.doc: A typed time taken apart, as a time field reads its keys: digits, and `:` where a mark ended the hour. One digit is the hour, open to a second while it is 0–2; two are the hour while they make one (`14`), else an hour and the minute's tens (`93`); three are `H:mm` (`930`, `230`) while the minute fits, else an hour and the minute's tens (`183` is 18:3_, as `18` was); four `HH:mm` (`1437`). After a mark the hour is what came before it and the minute what follows. Nothing is checked here: `typedTimeOf` says whether the parts make a time.

members.name: typedTimeOf
members.type: (parts: TypedTimeParts | null, period?: "am" | "pm" | null) => { hour24: number; minute: number; } | null
members.doc: The time typed parts make, on the 24-hour clock: the hour as typed, or on the half of the day typed (`am`, `pm`); a lone digit of the minute is its tens (`9:5` is 9:50), none is 0. An hour past 23, a minute past 59, or an hour past 12 with a half of the day is no time: `null`, never a time nearby.

members.name: twelveHours
members.doc: Whether the language writes a time of day in 12 hours with AM and PM (American English, Korean) rather than 24 (Russian, British English). An unknown language reads as 24.

members.name: today
members.doc: Today in the zone, or in the device zone when none is given.

members.name: weekStart
members.doc: The first day of the week for a locale: 0 Sunday, 1 Monday, 6 Saturday.

members.name: weekend
members.doc: The days of a locale's weekend, as `getUTCDay` counts them: 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday.

members.name: latinDigits
members.doc: Digits as other scripts and full-width keys write them (`٢٤`, `۲۴`, `２４`), as the Latin ones.

members.name: typedInFull
members.doc: Whether a typed day is written in full: day, month and a four-digit year as three parts, or eight digits alone. `12.03`, `03/12/19` and a lone `1` are not.

members.name: readTypedDay
members.type: (text: string, locale: string, today: IsoDay) => IsoDay | ""
members.doc: A day typed as people write it in `locale`: its parts in the locale's order (`12.03.1987` in `ru`, `03/12/1987` in `en-US`) with any marks between them, or as digits alone (`12031987`, `120387`). A part left out is today's: `12.03` is this year's, `12` this month's. A two-digit year is the nearest one at most ten years ahead. Digits of other scripts read as theirs, and a year in the locale's calendar (`2530` in Thai) as that calendar's; a calendar whose months differ (Persian, Hijri) reads nothing. Anything else, a day that does not exist included (`31.02`), is no day: `''`, never a guess.

members.name: monthGrid
members.doc: Six weeks around the month of `iso`, starting on `firstDay`: the grid never changes height.

members.name: dayWindow
members.type: (min?: string, max?: string) => { lo: IsoDay; hi: IsoDay; }
members.doc: The window of days `min` and `max` allow, read once for every user of it: a malformed bound is no bound, and bounds given backwards are the same window. Empty is open.

members.name: inRange
members.type: (iso: IsoDay, min?: string, max?: string) => boolean
members.doc: Whether the day lies inside `[min, max]`; an empty bound is open. ISO days compare as strings.

types.name: TypedTimeParts
types.doc: A typed time taken apart: the hour, the minute's digits so far, and whether the hour may take a second digit.

members.name: cardShellClass
members.doc: The one definition of the flat card chrome: a border on a surface, no shadow.

members.name: formatChartValue
members.type: (tr: Numbers, value: number | null | undefined, format?: ChartFormat, { compact }?: { compact?: boolean; }) => string
members.doc: A value as text. `compact` is for an axis, where the digits have no room: "42.4K" in the language's own words, no currency, since the axis names its unit once. Missing data is a dash, never "0".

members.name: formatChartTicks
members.type: (tr: Numbers, ticks: readonly number[], format?: ChartFormat) => string[]
members.doc: The labels of a value axis: compact numbers ("1.3M", "42K"), or percents, as few digits as keep every label apart (0, 0.05, 0.1 reads so, not 0, 0.1, 0.1). A function format and the currency stay off the axis: its figures are short, and the chart names its unit once.

members.name: parseChartDate
members.doc: A point of a time axis as a calendar day: `2026-09` is September, `2026-09-01` its first day, a timestamp the day it falls on in `timeZone` (the app's, as a date cell reads it), in the device's without one. `null` when it is not a date.

members.name: chartDateLabels
members.type: (tr: Dates, points: readonly DateValue[], grain: ChartGrain, shown?: (index: number) => boolean) => string[]
members.doc: The labels of a time axis, one per point. The year stands only where it changes and on the first label, and only when the points span more than one year; a point that is not a date keeps its text, as a category. `shown` says which labels a thinned axis prints: the year then stands on the first one shown and where the year changes between two shown, so a hidden first point never takes the year away with it.

members.name: chartDateLong
members.type: (tr: Dates, point: DateValue, grain: ChartGrain) => string
members.doc: One point in full, for a tooltip and a screen reader: "September 2026", "5 September 2026", "Saturday, 5 September 2026", "Week of 5 September 2026".

members.name: linePath
members.type: (xs: readonly number[], ys: readonly (number | null)[], curve?: ChartCurve) => string
members.doc: The `d` of a line through the points, in the caller's coordinates. A `null` is a gap: the line breaks there and goes on after it; no data is never drawn as zero.

members.name: areaPath
members.type: (xs: readonly number[], ys: readonly (number | null)[], base: number | readonly number[], curve?: ChartCurve) => string
members.doc: The `d` of the band between the line and a base: a number (the zero line's coordinate) or a lower edge per point, for a stack. Gaps break the band as they break the line.

members.name: ringArcs
members.type: (values: readonly (number | null)[], { inner, outer, pad, grow, }: { inner: number; outer: number; pad?: number; grow?: { index: number; by: number; }; }) => RingArc[]
members.doc: The arcs of a ring around 0,0, clockwise from twelve o'clock, in the order given: the caller sorts. A value that is not a positive number takes no room, and its share is 0; when nothing is left the ring has no arcs. `outer` is the radius, `inner` the hole; `pad` parts the arcs by that length along the middle of the ring, the same gap whatever the share; a part thinner than the gap is drawn twice as wide as it, its share unchanged. `grow` widens one arc outward.

types.name: RingArc
types.doc: One part of a ring: the `d` of its arc, and its share of the whole, 0 to 1.

members.name: linearScale
members.type: (values: Iterable<number | null | undefined>, { count, min, max, zero }?: LinearScaleOptions) => LinearScale
members.doc: A value axis over the numbers given; `null`, NaN and infinity are gaps and do not stretch it.

members.name: tickCount
members.doc: How many ticks a value axis of this height holds: one per 48px, never fewer than 2.

members.name: pointPosition
members.doc: Where the point `index` of `count` stands along the axis, 0 to 1; a lone point stands in the middle.

members.name: nearestPoint
members.doc: The point under a position 0..1 along the axis: the nearest one, clamped to the ends.

members.name: labelStep
members.type: (widthPx: number, labelWidthsPx: readonly number[], gapPx?: number, insetPx?: number, fromEnd?: boolean) => number
members.doc: Every how many points a label stands so that no two shown labels touch: 1 shows them all. `labelWidthsPx` are the labels as measured, one per point. The first label stands from the start of the axis and the last one ends at its end; the rest are centered on their points. An unmeasured axis (0 wide on the server) shows them all, so the first paint is the widest one and a narrow screen only takes labels away. `insetPx` moves the two ends inward, for an axis that runs to a card's edges and keeps its words on the gutter. `fromEnd` counts the shown labels back from the newest, as a chart that always labels its newest point prints them.

members.name: crowdedLabels
members.type: (spans: readonly { index: number; from: number; to: number; }[], widthPx: number, gapPx?: number) => Set<number>
members.doc: The shown labels to hide so that none runs into the next, starts before the plot or ends past it, walked from the newest, which always stays. `spans` are the labels as they stand, measured from the plot's left edge in pixels, in the order of their points; a chart laid out right to left, its newest label leftmost, is read from the other side. A step is chosen from widths measured before the year moved onto the labels it shows, so they may be wider than it counted; this is the last word.

members.name: placedLabels
members.type: (labels: readonly HTMLElement[], plot: HTMLElement | undefined, shows: (index: number) => boolean) => { index: number; from: number; to: number; }[]
members.doc: The shown time labels as they stand, in pixels from the plot's start and in order: what `crowdedLabels` weighs. Each label carries its point in `data-label`.

types.name: LinearScale
types.doc: A value axis: its round bounds, the ticks on them, and where a value stands between them.

fields.name: domain
fields.doc: The bounds after rounding: `[0, 5000]` for data up to 4380.

fields.name: ticks
fields.doc: Round values from the lower bound to the upper, both included.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: Where a value stands, 0 at the lower bound and 1 at the upper; out of range goes past them.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: About how many ticks; the scale picks a round step near it. 5 by default.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: A fixed lower bound, for an axis that does not start at zero.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: A fixed upper bound: a plan, or one ceiling shared by charts side by side.

fields.name: zero
fields.doc: The axis reaches zero even when every value is far from it; on by default, a bar or an area lies to the eye without it.

members.name: checkMarkClass
members.type: (checked: boolean, disabled?: boolean, invalid?: boolean) => string
members.doc: Hover belongs to the host: the checkbox gates it on `enabled:` and darkens to `control-border-hover`, a select row lights it with the row.

members.name: CHECK_MARK_BOX
members.doc: The size and corner of a check mark, 18px; its corner stops at a third of the side, or it reads as a radio. A skeleton of a checkbox takes it too.

members.name: CHECK_MARK_BASE
members.type: "flex h-[18px] w-[18px] rounded-[min(var(--radius-badge),33%)] shrink-0 items-center justify-center border transition-colors duration-fast"
members.doc: The box of a check mark (checkbox, multiple-select rows).

members.name: CHECK_MARK_SHELL
members.type: "flex shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-[min(var(--radius-badge),33%)] border transition-colors duration-fast"
members.doc: A check mark's box without its size: a checkbox sizes it by its step (`MARK_STEP`).

members.name: RADIO_MARK_SHELL
members.type: "flex shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-pill border transition-colors duration-fast"
members.doc: A radio mark without its size: a plain radio sizes it by the group's step.

members.name: MARK_STEP
members.type: Record<ControlSize, { box: string; glyph: string; dot: string; top: string; }>
members.doc: A mark beside text, per step of the control ladder: 16, 18 and 20 px. The text stays `text-sm`, and the mark stands at its first line (a 22px line), so a long label reads on beside it; `sm` is the mark as it always was.

members.name: RADIO_MARK_BASE_CARD
members.type: "flex h-5 w-5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-pill border transition-colors duration-fast"
members.doc: In a card the mark stands alone on a 60px row: 20px, or it reads as a dot.

members.name: useComposedValue
members.type: (emit: (value: string) => void, normalize?: (value: string) => string, model?: () => string) => { composing: Ref<boolean, boolean>; display: (model: string | null | undefined) => string; onInput: (e: Event) => void; onCompositionStart: () => void; onCompositionEnd: (e: Event) => void; }
members.doc: The value of a text control under an IME. Nothing is emitted mid-composition, and while composing the bound value follows the DOM: a host that re-renders for its own reasons would otherwise write the stale model back into the control and break the characters being typed. `normalize` rewrites the value before it is emitted (a comma to a point); the DOM follows, caret kept. With `model`, the control follows the owner after each change: a change the owner refused is put back.

members.name: useFormReset
members.type: <E extends TextControl>(el: Ref<E | null>, restore: (control: E) => void) => void
members.doc: A form reset puts a control on its default (the server's markup, empty or unchecked) and fires no input or change event: once the reset is done, `restore` puts the model back into it.

members.name: controlChromeClass
members.doc: Border and fill of a control's capsule, by state. One place for input, textarea, select and the code cells. Disabled is a state, not a fade: its own plate and ink, so it reads apart from a field at rest.

members.name: triggerCapsuleClass
members.type: (ladder: ControlSize, disabled: boolean, invalid: boolean) => string[]
members.doc: The capsule of a field that opens a panel (a select, a day): its value, then the glyphs at its end.

members.name: capsuleRoot
members.type: (stacked: () => boolean, column: () => { class: unknown; style: unknown; }) => (_: unknown, { slots }: SetupContext) => VNode<RendererNode, RendererElement, { [key: string]: any; }>
members.doc: The root of a field with something under its capsule (tags, shortcuts). Stacked, a column holds both and takes the caller's class and style; alone, the capsule is the root, so a UiButtonGroup joins it as one of its controls.

members.name: capsuleEndButtonClass
members.doc: A button at the end of a capsule (a clear cross, the eye), pulled to its edge. It is an `xs` icon button, 28px; in a 28px capsule it takes 24px, so it fits inside the capsule's border.

members.name: CONTROL_HEIGHT
members.doc: The control height ladder in px. Every interactive control stands on it.

members.name: controlHeightClass
members.doc: Tailwind classes for the ladder, one place to change the implementation.

members.name: controlMinHeightClass
members.doc: The ladder as a floor, for a control that grows with its content (a textarea's single row).

members.name: countValue
members.doc: A count as a mark reads it: a fraction floored, an endless count kept as the overflow, a negative, NaN or missing one `0`.

members.name: countMax
members.doc: The largest count a mark shows as is: a whole number from 1, else 99.

members.name: countText
members.doc: What a mark reads, and what its host says: the count, or `{max}+` above the cap.

members.name: rangeFor
members.type: (preset: RangePreset, today: IsoDay, firstDay?: number) => { from: string; to: string; }
members.doc: The days of a preset around `today`, both ends inclusive; `all` and `custom` are empty. Months and years are whole calendar ones, so a page that moves over a month keeps its periods; a week starts on `firstDay` (0 Sunday, 1 Monday, 6 Saturday), Monday when it is not given, and the last 7 or 30 days end today, today counted. UiDateRange counts a week from the app's language (Sunday in American English), so a model built here for This week may be brought to other days when it mounts.

members.name: cutToWindow
members.type: (r: { from: string; to: string; }, { lo, hi }: { lo: string; hi: string; }) => { from: string; to: string; } | null
members.doc: The days of a span inside the window `[lo, hi]`, cut at its edges; `null` when none of them is inside. No bounds stay no bounds.

members.name: presetDays
members.type: (preset: RangePreset, today: IsoDay, { firstDay, min, max }?: { firstDay?: number; min?: string; max?: string; }) => { from: string; to: string; }
members.doc: The days a range filter applies for a preset: its own around `today`, cut by the window when they reach past it. One wholly outside the window keeps its own days.

members.name: periodBounds
members.type: (period: { from?: string | null; to?: string | null; preset?: RangePreset | null; } | null | undefined, options?: { timeZone?: string; locale?: string; min?: string; max?: string; }) => { start: string | null; end: string | null; }
members.doc: The moments a period covers, for a query: from midnight of its first day to midnight after its last, by the clock of `timeZone` (the zone given to `createGrani({ timeZone })`), or of the device without one. `end` is exclusive: a query for `at >= start && at < end` counts the last day whole, a day the clock changes on too. A named preset is counted from today in that zone, as UiDateRange shows it, whatever days the period carries, so the first request, on the server too, asks for this Last month and not the one saved with a link: give it the app's `locale`, where a week starts, and the filter's `min` and `max`, or it asks for other days than the button shows. Without a `locale` a week starts on Sunday, as in English, the language an app has when it names none (said in development for a week); `rangeFor` alone starts it on Monday. A zone no clock knows is the device's. `custom` and a period with no preset keep their days; All time is no bounds. An open end, or one that is no day, is `null`, and ends given backwards are the same period.

members.name: RANGE_PRESETS
members.doc: The presets in the order a panel lists them; `custom` is not listed, a pick on the calendar makes it.

members.name: midnightIn
members.doc: The moment a day begins by the clock of `timeZone`, or of the device without one; an unknown zone is the device's, as `createGrani({ timeZone })` reads it. `null` for what is no day.

members.name: parseDateValue
members.type: (value: DateValue | null | undefined, timeZone?: string) => ParsedDate | null
members.doc: Reads a value as a cell does; `null` for empty or unreadable. A day alone is local midnight, not UTC: `new Date('2026-09-24')` is the evening before west of Greenwich. A day and a time with no zone (`2026-09-24T10:00`) is the reading of a clock: with `timeZone`, the moment that zone's clock reads it, so it shows as it came in that zone; without one, the device's clock.

members.name: dayIn
members.doc: The calendar day a moment falls on by a zone's clock, as a day count; the device's without one.

members.name: relativeDayKey
members.type: (date: Date | number, now?: Date | number, o?: { timeZone?: string; dateOnly?: boolean; }) => "today" | "yesterday" | null
members.doc: Today or yesterday, else `null`: by the calendar of `timeZone` when given, the device's without one. A day alone (`dateOnly`) is its own calendar day, wherever it is read. `now` is a parameter, so the answer can be tested.

fields.name: dateOnly
fields.doc: The value named a day and no time (`2026-09-24`); it is read as a local day and shows no time.

members.name: debounce
members.type: <A extends unknown[]>(fn: (...args: A) => void, wait: number) => Debounced<A>
members.doc: Holds a call until `wait` ms pass without another; the last arguments win.

fields.name: cancel
fields.doc: Drops the pending call.

fields.name: flush
fields.doc: Runs the pending call now instead of after the pause.

members.name: isDev
members.doc: Whether the app's bundler built for development. Written as Vue writes it, so Vite and webpack replace it in the app's build; the library's own build leaves it alone (`import.meta.env.DEV` would be fixed to `false` there, for every app). Where nothing replaces it and `process` does not exist, it is production. This is the function the sources and the specs call. The library's build (`scripts/lib.config.mjs`) writes its test into each call instead, since no bundler or minifier drops a branch behind a call and a production bundle would keep every warning text. So in the shipped files a check made with no `process` and nothing replacing it throws, as Vue's does; only the import is safe (`useShared`).

members.name: warnOnce
members.type: (app: object | undefined, key: string, message: string) => void
members.doc: Warns once per app and key: a table of a hundred rows that repeat one mistake says it once. With no app (a component mounted outside one) it warns every time.

members.name: useFieldWiring
members.type: (props: FieldWords, slots: Slots) => { id: ComputedRef<string>; ids: { label: ComputedRef<string | undefined>; description: ComputedRef<string>; error: ComputedRef<string>; meta: ComputedRef<string>; }; describedBy: ComputedRef<string | undefined>; }
members.doc: The wiring of a field, shared by UiField and a label UiListItem: the ids of the label, description, error and meta lines, provided to the control inside.

members.name: useFieldControl
members.type: (own: () => FieldControlOwn, lines?: FieldControlLines) => { field: FieldContext | null; id: ComputedRef<string | undefined>; invalid: ComputedRef<boolean>; required: ComputedRef<boolean>; disabled: ComputedRef<boolean>; describedBy: ComputedRef<string | undefined>; aria: ComputedRef<{ 'aria-invalid': true | "true" | "false" | undefined; 'aria-required': true | "true" | "false" | undefined; 'aria-describedby': string | undefined; }>; }
members.doc: A control's side of the field contract: its id and its invalid, required and disabled state, merged from its own props and the field around it, and the `aria-*` values for the element a person reaches. Ours win only where set: a caller's `aria-invalid` or `aria-required` stays when the control has none, and the caller's `aria-describedby` is read first, then the field's.

members.name: useField
members.doc: The context of the field around the caller, or `null` outside one.

members.name: hideField
members.doc: Hides the field from what the caller renders: its controls keep their own ids, names and states, as outside any field.

members.name: NoField
members.doc: Hides the field from what it wraps: controls in it keep their own ids, names and states, as outside any field.

types.name: FieldContext
types.doc: What a field tells the control inside it; it wins over the control's own props.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Id for the control, the one the label points at; `undefined` in a group, where each control keeps its own.

fields.name: labelId
fields.doc: Id of the label, for a control that is not labelable (`aria-labelledby`).

fields.name: describedBy
fields.doc: Ids of the lines that describe the control: error or description, then meta.

fields.name: invalid
fields.doc: The field shows an error: the control marks itself `aria-invalid` and draws the invalid border.

fields.name: required
fields.doc: The control marks itself `aria-required`: a required field around one control. In a group it is false, since the legend says it once and not each control.

fields.name: group
fields.doc: The field is a fieldset around a group of controls (`UiField group`).

types.name: FieldWords
types.doc: The props of a field that decide its wiring.

types.name: FieldControlOwn
types.doc: What a control brings of its own to the field's wiring: its props, read on every change.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The control's own id; the field's wins, so the label always points at the control.

fields.name: invalid
fields.doc: The control's own mark (its prop, or a value it cannot read); the field's error adds to it.

fields.name: required
fields.doc: The control's own prop; a field says it for a single control, never for one in a group.

fields.name: disabled
fields.doc: The control's own prop: a field never turns a control off.

types.name: FieldControlLines
types.doc: Ids of the control's own lines, read with the field's: `before` them (a note) or `after` (a hint).

members.name: focusInvalid
members.doc: Puts the focus on the first field in error under `root` and scrolls it into view, only as far as needed. A save that stopped on a field would otherwise be pressed again, and on a long form the reason is off the screen. A group in error (radios, a scale) takes no focus itself: the focus goes to its chosen control, else its first. A field in error that cannot take the focus (a disabled one, one in a hidden or inert container) is passed over for the next, and so is a refused draft (`data-draft`), which a Save does not wait on. Returns whether a control took it.

members.name: TYPED_FIELD
members.doc: A field where you type: Cmd+Enter sends from it, and a late error does not take the focus from it. A button is not one.

members.name: INVALID
members.doc: A field in error that the form must fix. A draft refused on its own (the text of a UiListField, marked `data-draft`) is not one: it is said to a screen reader, and a Save goes past it.

members.name: succeed
members.doc: `next` takes the focus meant for `gone`, a control that left the page.

members.name: standIn
members.type: <E extends Element>(el: E | null | undefined) => Element | null | undefined
members.doc: What stands in for `el` once it left the page, through every hand-on; `el` itself while it is there.

members.name: generatePassword
members.doc: A random password from `crypto.getRandomValues`, uniform over the alphabet (bytes above its largest multiple are discarded, not reduced), between 10 and 256 characters, 16 when the length is not a number. It holds a lower, an upper, a digit and a symbol: a draw without one is drawn again, so the passwords stay uniform over the ones a policy accepts.

members.name: giveFocus
members.type: (target: () => HTMLElement | null | undefined, wanted: () => boolean) => void
members.doc: Gives the focus to `target()` now, and frame by frame until it takes, a dozen frames at most, while `wanted()` holds: a panel just shown is `visibility: hidden` for its position, and the browser may count what it holds as hidden for a few frames more (measured: 4 or 5), refusing the focus meanwhile. Never over a focus the person moved: a press or a key from here on is theirs and ends it. A focus that moved with neither was moved by code, and is taken over: a menu that closes behind the item that opened this hands the focus to its button (Firefox does that first), and Safari focuses no pressed button but the nearest focusable box around it.

members.name: GROUP_AXIS
members.doc: The axis of the enclosing UiButtonGroup: a UiSeparator inside it stands across it by default. Injection reaches every descendant, so a panel opened from a button in the group (a menu, a popover) provides `vertical` again, or its separators would stand across its rows.

members.name: GROUP_NESTED
members.doc: Whether a UiButtonGroup stands inside another one. Only the outermost group of a `UiField group` takes the field's name; a panel opened from a button in a group provides `false` again, so a group inside the panel is wired to its own field.

members.name: holdEnter
members.doc: On a native button each repeat of a held Enter clicks (Space clicks as it comes up, once): its repeats press nothing. Bound to the button's keydown, or to a container's around its buttons.

members.name: isHeldPress
members.doc: A key held down sends its keydown again and again. A press read on keydown runs on each repeat: a toggle flips back and forth, a pick closes a list and the next repeat opens it again on its button, a button clicks at key-repeat speed. Enter and Space held down are one press; the arrows and the letters still repeat, since they walk and type.

members.name: isImeKey
members.doc: Whether a key belongs to an IME composition: during it (`isComposing`), and the key that confirms the candidate, which Safari sends after it has ended the composition, with `isComposing` already false but key code 229. Such a key picks a word, never an option, an item, a step or a submit.

members.name: versionLine
members.doc: Two copies of grani can meet on one page: the app and a library of its own depend on different versions, or a monorepo does not dedupe. Every injection key is registered per line of the version: copies of one line share the app's settings, a field's wiring and the link component, while copies of different lines stay apart instead of reading each other's shape. The line is the major and the minor (`0.1`, `1.2`), never the major alone: what the copies share is internal (the scope, the toasts, the question, the overlay layers), and a minor may change its shape without breaking anything public. So 0.1.0 and 0.1.7 share; 1.1 and 1.2 stay apart.

members.name: graniKey
members.doc: The key under `name` for this copy's line: `grani@0.1:scope`.

members.name: registerCopy
members.doc: Records a copy's version on the page; every copy does it once, as it loads.

members.name: copiesWarning
members.doc: The warning for the versions on the page, once per set of them; `null` for one version or a set already told. Two copies are twice the code; two lines are also two settings and two link components, and a field of one does not label a control of the other.

members.name: normalizeAddress
members.doc: An address the way the URL parser reads it: C0 controls and spaces trimmed from both ends, and every tab, LF and CR dropped wherever it stands. Every predicate here reads this, not the raw string, or `java\tscript:` and `http:\t//evil.example` slip past a check the parser does not make. Anything that is no string reads as no address.

members.name: unsafeHref
members.doc: An address that runs script or carries a document: never rendered as a link. Read the way the URL parser reads it (`normalizeAddress`), or `java\tscript:` slips past. Anything that is no string (the app's data may hold a number where the types say a string) is no script either: RouteLink draws no link for it, and nothing here throws on it.

members.name: linkTarget
members.type: (to: string | undefined, target?: "_blank" | "_self", rel?: string) => { newTab: boolean; target: "_blank" | "_self" | undefined; rel: string | undefined; }
members.doc: The anchor's `target` and `rel` for an address: a caller's `target` decides, unset a new tab for another site only. A new tab always has `noopener`; another site has `noreferrer` unless the caller's `rel` replaces it (`nofollow`, `sponsored`). An explicit `_self` is kept.

members.name: opensElsewhere
members.doc: Where a link goes, shared by UiLink, UiButton and UiListItem so the three never drift: one predicate for "another site", one for an address that must not be a link, one resolution of `target` and `rel`, and the flag a link sets for what it holds. An absolute web address opens in a new tab; `mailto:` and `tel:` hand off to an app and stay put: a new tab there is left empty and "opens in a new tab" is untrue. The app's own origin written in full counts as absolute: pass `target="_self"` for it.

members.name: hasAddress
members.doc: Whether `to` is an address at all. The app's data may hold none where the types say a string (`null`, a blank, a number from a tenant's menu): no address is as no `to`, never a link.

members.name: INSIDE_LINK
members.doc: Set by a whole-row link (UiListItem, UiButton with `to`): a link inside it is a link in a link.

members.name: markCorrection
members.doc: Marks the change the list is about to make as its own correction, until the current task ends.

members.name: isCorrection
members.doc: Whether the change being written is the list's own correction.

members.name: listFilters
members.doc: The filters of one list; `changed` hears what the person does to them.

members.name: LIST_FILTERS
members.doc: The table a filter stands in: it starts on page one when the person changes a choice.

types.name: ListFilter
types.doc: A filter of a list, as the table around it knows it.

fields.name: chosen
fields.doc: Something is chosen.

fields.name: clear
fields.doc: Undoes the choice, as the filter's own Reset does.

types.name: ListFilters
types.doc: The filters of one list, and what the person does to them.

fields.name: all
fields.doc: Every filter in the list, in the order they came.

fields.name: put
fields.doc: Takes a filter in and gives back how to take it out.

fields.name: changed
fields.doc: The person changed a choice (a tick, Only, Reset), never the app.

members.name: callListeners
members.type: <A extends unknown[]>(listener: unknown, ...args: A) => Promise<unknown[]> | undefined
members.doc: Calls the listener of an event a component waits for (`@more`, `@add`). The component declares it as a prop (`onMore`), so the handler reaches it and what the handler returns is seen: one promise holds the control until it settles. Two listeners merged from attributes arrive as an array; each is called, and every promise among their answers is awaited. Nothing returned a promise: `undefined`, and the control is not held. A listener that throws at once throws here.

members.name: useLiveText
members.doc: The words of a status region that is always in the DOM: empty when it is drawn, and its words a beat after it mounts, then whenever they change. A region that appears with its words is often not read, so a table that opens loading would never say it loads. The server renders it empty, so hydration matches.

members.name: minorDigits
members.doc: How many minor digits a currency has, as the browser knows them: two for EUR, three for KWD, none for JPY. A code it does not know, or no code, gives two. The money cell and a chart's money values print amounts with it, so the two never disagree.

members.name: decimalsOf
members.doc: Decimal places of a value written with a point: `10.44` gives 2, `10` gives 0.

members.name: effectiveStep
members.doc: The step an arrow applies. A value written more precisely than `step` moves by its own last digit (`10.44` with `0.1` moves by a cent), finer only and not below two orders under the step; an integer step is never refined (`5.5` + `1` = `6.5`).

members.name: stepValue
members.type: (raw: string | null, delta: number, bounds?: StepBounds) => string
members.doc: One arrow press: a comma is read, empty is `0`, rounded to the precision of the value or the step and written with it (`10.99` and a cent gives `11.00`), then held at the bounds, which keep their own digits: a bound off the step's grid (`min` 0.01 with a step of 1) is never passed.

members.name: numberMarks
members.doc: The marks of `locale`: `en` has `.` and `,`, `de-DE` `,` and `.`, `ru` `,` and a no-break space.

members.name: readLocaleNumber
members.doc: A number as a person of `locale` writes it, read without changing its magnitude. Spaces and the locale's grouping mark go; the decimal mark becomes a point; digits of another numbering system become ASCII. With both `.` and `,` the last one is the decimal and the other must group by thousands. A single mark of the locale's grouping must group by thousands, else it is unsure (`1,23` in English). In a locale that groups with a space, the point is a decimal too, unless it reads as a thousand (`1.234`). Two decimal marks, a digit among other signs, or text with no digit at all (`abc`, `-`) are unsure. Unsure text comes back as written with `ok` false.

members.name: showLocaleNumber
members.doc: The model as a person of `locale` reads it: a plain number shows the locale's decimal comma.

types.name: NumberMarks
types.doc: The decimal and grouping marks of a locale, as Intl writes them.

types.name: ReadNumber
types.doc: What a typed or pasted number reads as: `value` is the model text, `ok` false when unsure.

members.name: usePanelList
members.type: <T>(o: PanelListOptions<T>) => { active: Ref<number, number>; firstEnabled: (from: number, step: 1 | -1) => number; next: (step: 1 | -1) => number; move: (index: number) => void; keys: (e: KeyboardEvent, inField?: boolean) => boolean; scrollToActive: () => void; typeAhead: (char: string) => void; resetTypeAhead: () => void; typing: () => boolean; }
members.doc: The behavior of a list in a panel, written once: the highlight, the arrows, Home and End passing over a disabled row, the letters that jump, and the highlighted row brought into view in the list, never by scrolling the page. UiSelect, UiFilterList, UiDateRange, UiMenu and UiListField walk their rows with it; what Enter, Space and Escape do stays theirs.

members.name: PANEL_LIST_ROW
members.type: "relative flex select-none items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 first:pt-[max(0.375rem,calc(var(--radius-overlay)*0.3))] last:pb-[max(0.375rem,calc(var(--radius-overlay)*0.3))]"
members.doc: The one definition of a list in a panel: UiSelect's listbox, UiFilterList, UiDateRange's presets, UiMenu's items and UiAppShell's places read it (through `PanelRow` and `usePanelList`), so a change here reaches all of them. Rows run edge to edge, 12px in; the first and the last grow by 0.3 of the panel radius, since a corner arc of radius r reaches r(1 - 1/√2) in at 45°. A press takes neither the focus nor a text selection (the row also cancels the mouse press, never the pointer press, which in WebKit would end a tap in no click).

members.name: PANEL_LIST_ACTIVE
members.doc: The highlighted row, followed by the pointer and the arrows alike: its band, and a bar of the brand at its start edge. The band alone reads 1.05:1 against the panel, under the 3:1 a focus mark needs; the bar reads 5.5:1 against the band and moves no text. The bar is a border, as a notice row's edge (`TONE_ROW_EDGE`): forced colors drop the band's fill and keep a border. The row is `relative`.

members.name: ROW_FOCUS
members.doc: The same mark on a command row the focus is on (a menu's, a card's), the bar in the brand.

members.name: ROW_FOCUS_BAR_INK
members.doc: The bar on a toned command row the focus is on, in the row's own ink, beside its toned band.

members.name: PANEL_LIST_HEIGHT
members.doc: How tall the list grows before it scrolls; `relative` so a row's `offsetTop` counts from the list, which scrolls it.

members.name: PANEL_LIST_SEARCH
members.doc: The search row at the top: a glyph and a bare field over one line.

members.name: PANEL_LIST_SEARCH_INPUT
members.type: "h-9 min-w-0 flex-1 bg-transparent text-fg placeholder:text-placeholder focus:outline-hidden"

members.name: PANEL_LIST_NOTE
members.doc: Nothing found, loading, failed: one centered line with room around it.

members.name: NAV_ROW
members.type: "h-9 gap-3 rounded-control px-2 text-fg-muted [&:is(:enabled,a)]:hover:bg-surface-muted aria-[current=page]:bg-brand-subtle aria-[current=page]:hover:bg-brand-subtle [&>div:first-child]:aria-[current=page]:text-brand-subtle-fg"
members.doc: A place of the app in a sidebar: 36px, rounded, muted until it is the current page, which is lit. The tint reads 1.12:1 light and 1.00:1 dark, so UiAppShell sets the current place's label semibold too, on the label itself: the page is told by weight, not by color alone.

fields.name: items
fields.doc: The rows the keys walk, in order.

fields.name: disabled
fields.doc: A row the arrows and the letters pass over.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The words a typed letter is matched against.

fields.name: row
fields.doc: The element of a row by its index, to bring it into view or give it the focus.

fields.name: list
fields.doc: The list that scrolls inside its panel; unset, the row is brought into view where it stands (a list in a drawer).

fields.name: wrap
fields.doc: The arrows go round, from the last row to the first and back.

fields.name: focus
fields.doc: The highlight is the focus: a move focuses the row (a menu); else the caller points at it with `aria-activedescendant`.

fields.name: typeAhead
fields.doc: Letters: `first` gathers them for half a second and goes to the first row they start, the same letter again to the next row it starts; `next` takes one letter and goes to the next row it starts, after the highlight.

members.name: pick
members.type: <K extends string>(map: Record<K, string>, key: K | undefined | null, fallback: K) => string
members.doc: Read a class from a lookup map, falling back on an unknown key. `Object.hasOwn` matters: `map['constructor']` would return an inherited function, which is truthy, so `??` would not catch it and Vue would drop the class silently.

members.name: pluralCategory
members.doc: CLDR plural category for a count in a locale; `other` when the tag is malformed.

types.name: RadioGroupContext
types.doc: What a radio group tells the radios inside it.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Shared native name: the browser moves between the radios with arrows.

fields.name: required
fields.doc: The group's own `required`: each radio carries native `required`, so a form asks for one.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Step of the segmented bar: `sm` 36, `md` 44; segments follow.

fields.name: mark
fields.doc: Step of a plain radio's mark: 16, 18 or 20 px beside its text.

fields.name: block
fields.doc: A segmented bar that fills its row: segments share the width.

fields.name: claim
fields.doc: A radio holds its value; the first one set up is the `owner` when two share it.

fields.name: settled
fields.doc: Bumped after every pick, once the owner has had its turn: every radio puts its DOM back on the model.

members.name: LINK
members.doc: The link component an app gives `createGrani({ link })`; unset, its `RouterLink` if it has a router.

members.name: RouteLink
members.doc: The anchor UiLink, UiButton, UiListItem and UiAppShell draw for `to`: the app's link component for its own paths, a plain `<a href>` otherwise. Attributes, the class and the slot pass through, but an `href` among them, which the anchor would take over the address it computed: `to` is the only address. One that runs script or carries a document (`javascript:`, `data:`) is refused here, for every caller at once: the slot shows in a `<span>` read as a link that is not available, and dev warns once. An address may come from the app's data (a tenant's menu), so a caller that forgets the check must not open it; and the data may hold none (`null`, nothing, blank) or no string at all (a number) whatever the types say, which draws the same `<span>`, on a server too.

members.name: resetRows
members.doc: A surface of its own (a window, a drawer, a popover's panel) starts its rows afresh: the row of whatever opened it (a sidebar's footer) does not reach in through the teleport.

members.name: provideLooseRows
members.doc: A host whose rows are no list's (a sidebar's footer): a row there keeps its own height and inset, and is no row a list counts.

members.name: provideInList
members.doc: A UiList says its children are its items: a notice there is drawn as a row, not as a card. A row clears it for what it holds.

members.name: isFiniteNumber
members.doc: A number one can compute with: not NaN, not infinite. `null` from an API and `parseFloat('')` are not.

members.name: clamp01
members.doc: Clamped to 0..1; a non-number is 0, so `width: NaN%` never reaches the DOM (the browser drops the rule and the bar stays empty without a word).

members.name: scaleRampStep
members.doc: The ramp in five stops for a fill that carries numbers: danger, danger and warning half and half, warning, warning and success half and half, success. Between the stops neither a light nor a dark ink reaches 4.5:1, so a numbered segment takes the nearest stop and the ink that reads on it (`light` the status fg, `dark` the warning fg); `scripts/contrast.mjs` checks each.

members.name: scaleRamp
members.doc: Which half of the ramp a fraction 0..1 falls in and how much of its first token it takes.

members.name: SCALE_RAMP_CLASS
members.doc: The thermometer fill of a scale: the status tokens mixed by the mark's position, so the ramp follows the theme. Two halves, danger to warning and warning to success; `mix` is the share of the first token, set on the segment as `--ui-scale-mix`, and the class reads it.

members.name: SCALE_RAMP_INK
members.doc: The ink of a numbered ramp stop: the light status ink, or the warning's dark one.

members.name: searchText
members.doc: Text as a search compares it: lower case, with the accents of Latin and Cyrillic letters left out (the marks of U+0300 to U+036F), so "munchen" finds München and the Cyrillic yo (U+0451) reads as ie (U+0435). The breve that makes a letter of its own stays: the short i (U+0439) is never i (U+0438), nor the short u (U+045E) u (U+0443). The marks of other scripts (kana voicing, vowel signs) are part of their letters and stay too. Both the query and the text it is looked for in go through it.

members.name: withSeparators
members.type: (nodes: VNodeArrayChildren, section: Component, separator: () => VNode, lined?: (next: VNode) => boolean) => VNode[]
members.doc: The children of an overlay body, with a separator between two neighboring sections; none before a section `lined` says draws its own line (a UiHeader legend first). Fragments (v-for, v-if) are opened; a section inside a component of the caller's own is not seen.

members.name: flatSections
members.doc: The children of a slot as the sections they render: fragments (v-for, v-if) opened, comments dropped.

members.name: renders
members.doc: Whether a slot draws anything: comments (a `v-if` that is off) and blank text are nothing. Read it at render.

members.name: firstNode
members.doc: The first node a list draws: comments and blank text skipped, fragments opened.

members.name: leadsWith
members.type: (nodes: unknown, match: (v: VNode) => boolean, depth?: number) => boolean
members.doc: Whether what a slot draws opens with a node `match` takes, looking through the first child of plain elements and of a layout that draws nothing before its slot (UiStack, marked `layout`): any other component draws what it likes before its slot, and its slot may want props.

members.name: sanitizeSharedSeed
members.doc: The seed `createGrani({ shared })` takes, narrowed to what `sharedSnapshot` writes: a key it writes, with the shape it writes. A key or a value outside that is dropped, said once in development by its key alone, never by its value.

members.name: SEEDS
members.doc: What `sharedSnapshot` writes into the page, key by key, and the one shape each has: the store's plain values. Everything else the store holds (toasts, a question, the hosts) never leaves the server and never comes back: a seed is read from the page, which anything on it may have written, and a toast, a question or a crashed calendar must not come from it. A new plain value in the store joins this list, or `sharedSnapshot` leaves it out and names it in development (`test/plugin.spec.ts`); `test/ssr/render.ssr.spec.ts` renders a page and takes its snapshot back whole.

members.name: useSlotsSeen
members.doc: Which slots the component is given, read again before every render. Slots are not reactive: a `computed` that reads `slots.picks` keeps its first answer when the slot comes or goes later (`<template v-if="…" #picks>`). Read `seen.picks` where it would read `slots.picks`.

members.name: STEPPER
members.doc: The count UiStepper draws: the number field under it shows minus and plus at its edges.

members.name: stylesMissing
members.doc: What keeps grani's components from their styles on this page, or nothing. Each stylesheet marks itself on `:root` (`--grani-styles`: `all` from `grani-ui/style.css`, `theme` from `grani-ui/theme.css`), and with `all` a class only Tailwind's reading of grani's files writes, `z-toast`, must be in the sheet too. `theme.css` brings classes by component, so nothing is asked of it. A page with no stylesheet at all is not judged: nothing of the app is styled either, and that is not grani's to say.

members.name: checkStyles
members.doc: In development, once per page: warn when grani's components will show unstyled, which the app's build never says (a forgotten import, Tailwind's `prefix()`, a scan that did not reach grani's files). Yarn Plug'n'Play is not among them: grani asks it to unpack the package (`preferUnplugged`), and kept in a zip it would cost only the production build, where nothing runs this. Read after the page has loaded and painted a frame, so a stylesheet still on its way is not taken for a missing one. Never on a server and never in production.

members.name: NO_STYLESHEET
members.doc: Said when the app's stylesheet does not bring grani's: the line it lacks.

members.name: NO_CLASSES
members.doc: Said when grani's stylesheet came but Tailwind wrote none of its components' classes.

members.name: FLAT_CARD
members.doc: A card inside an overlay body is a section of it: no frame, no padding of its own.

members.name: CARD_TITLE_ID
members.doc: The id of the enclosing card's heading: a group inside the card can be named by it.

members.name: CARD_DEPTH
members.doc: The nesting depth of cards: a card's heading is `h2` at depth 0, `h3` below.

members.name: SURFACE_GUTTER
members.doc: The gutter of the surface, a `--space-*` token: a separator and a list in it bleed to its edges.

members.name: BLEED
members.type: { readonly overlay: "-mx-overlay"; readonly surface: "-mx-surface"; readonly 'surface-md': "-mx-surface-md"; readonly drawer: "-mx-drawer"; readonly field: "-mx-3"; }
members.doc: The side margins that run a row or a chart to the edges of a surface with this gutter.

members.name: LEGEND_DASH
members.type: { readonly overlay: "before:w-[calc(var(--space-overlay)-0.5rem)]"; readonly surface: "before:w-[calc(var(--space-surface)-0.5rem)]"; readonly 'surface-md': "before:w-[calc(var(--space-surface-md)-0.5rem)]"; readonly drawer: "before:w-[calc(var(--space-drawer)-0.5rem)]"; readonly field: "before:w-1"; }
members.doc: The dash before a legend's title: with the `gap-2` after it, it puts the title on the gutter, where the fields start.

members.name: ROW_INSET
members.doc: The inset of a surface whose body runs edge to edge (a card of rows): a row pads its text to it, nothing bleeds.

members.name: GUTTER_PAD
members.type: { readonly overlay: "px-overlay"; readonly surface: "px-surface"; readonly 'surface-md': "px-surface-md"; readonly drawer: "px-drawer"; readonly field: "px-3"; }
members.doc: The padding that puts a row's text on the gutter.

members.name: CHART_BLEED
members.doc: A chart that runs to its card's sides: the gutter its words keep to, `null` when it stays inside.

members.name: FLOOR
members.doc: The bottom margin that runs a chart to the floor of a surface with this gutter.

members.name: FLOOR_PAD
members.type: { readonly overlay: "pb-overlay"; readonly surface: "pb-surface"; readonly 'surface-md': "pb-surface-md"; readonly drawer: "pb-drawer"; readonly field: "pb-3"; }
members.doc: The padding a chart's legend keeps above the card's floor: the gutter, under it.

members.name: CHART_FLOOR
members.doc: A chart bled to the card's floor as well (`bleed="full"`, no footer): its last row keeps the gutter above the card's edge.

members.name: CHART_EMPTY
members.doc: A chart card with nothing to draw: a chart inside holds its first load's shape, so the card keeps its height; the card hides it under its words.

members.name: CHART_SKELETON
members.doc: A chart card's first load: a chart inside draws a skeleton in its own shape in place of its marks.

members.name: TABLE_FLOOR
members.doc: A list that searches (UiDataTable): its table stands on a floor its empty, failed and loading states share.

types.name: DrawerPattern
types.doc: A pattern laid over UiDrawer (a record) leads what the side panel cannot know: where Escape, the backdrop and the cross go (a level up, a refusal), what stands before and beside the title, the form round the body and the footer, and the body of each level. The drawer keeps the panel, the stack, the page held still and the focus. One way: the pattern gives, the drawer calls and reads; it never writes into it. It reaches only the drawer the pattern renders: the drawer clears it for what it holds.

fields.name: onOpen
fields.doc: Each time the drawer opens, before the focus goes in.

fields.name: exit
fields.doc: Escape or a press on the backdrop that is the drawer's.

fields.name: cross
fields.doc: The cross.

fields.name: shaking
fields.doc: The pattern's own refusal: the panel shakes while it is true.

fields.name: said
fields.doc: Why it last refused, said inside the panel.

fields.name: opensWithLegend
fields.doc: The body opens with a legend: the header draws no line of its own.

fields.name: lead
fields.doc: Before the title: the way up a level.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Beside the title: a status.

fields.name: form
fields.doc: Round the body and the footer: the record's form.

fields.name: body
fields.type: () => { key: number; class: string; onFocusin: () => void; }
fields.doc: The body of a level: its key (a new level is a new body, sliding in), its class, the focus entering it.

types.name: DrawerParts
types.doc: What a drawer gives what it renders inside it: a pattern's form finds the panel and the body here.

members.name: toneTextClass
members.doc: Color of a value itself: a big number, a delta, an amount cell.

members.name: toneSubtleClass
members.doc: Soft plate: badge, pill, icon box. Fill and text as one pair.

members.name: toneFillClass
members.doc: The saturated fill alone, without its label color: a ring or a glow in the tone.

members.name: toneSolidClass
members.doc: Saturated fill with its label color: a count that calls for attention.

members.name: toneOutlineClass
members.doc: Soft plate with a colored border.

members.name: toneDotClass
members.doc: Indicator dot next to a label, on the page and on the plate alike.

members.name: TONE_GLYPH
members.doc: The glyph of a toast in a tone.

members.name: TONE_GLYPH_INK
members.doc: The glyph's ink: the border role, graded for a mark on the surface; a message without a tone draws it muted.

members.name: TONE_EDGE
members.doc: The start edge of a message in a tone, 3px and round with its card: a toast and a notice.

members.name: TONE_ROW_EDGE
members.doc: The same edge on a notice drawn as a row of a UiList: a border on a pseudo-element over the row's start, so the text keeps the rows' inset and the edge runs the item's full height, clipped by the card's corners. A border survives forced colors, where a shadow would not. It stands on the list item (`.ui-list > li` is positioned): a positioned row would paint over the list's line.

members.name: truncateMiddle
members.doc: Shortens a string to about `max` characters by cutting the middle: an id keeps its head and its tail (`613aa1…4510e0`), and ids that share a prefix stay apart. Unchanged when it already fits.

members.name: visualizeControl
members.doc: A copy of `text` with every line break and other control character turned into a visible mark (`⏎`, the Unicode picture of the character, or `�` where it has none), one mark for one character: a value cut in the middle still lands where it reads. Takes text that is shown, never what is sent to the clipboard, which carries the character itself.

useAddItems.name: useAddItems
useAddItems.doc: One way in for every item of a list you add to, typed or pasted: split, trimmed, tidied by `fix`, checked by `check`, matched against `existing` in any case, fitted into `limit`. What cannot go in stays in the field with the reason; a repeat is pointed at; while a request is on its way a second add sends nothing, typing goes on and a pasted list waits for it, and a failure gives the text back unless something new was typed, its line offering Enter only when it did.

members.name: note
members.type: Ref<{ text: string; danger?: boolean | undefined; invalid?: boolean | undefined; } | null, AddNote | { text: string; danger?: boolean | undefined; invalid?: boolean | undefined; } | null>

fields.name: existing
fields.doc: The names already in the list, matched in any case.

fields.name: split
fields.doc: `lines`: a paste splits by line. `lists`: also by commas and semicolons, typed or pasted.

fields.name: fix
fields.doc: Tidies an item on its way in.

fields.name: check
fields.doc: Why an item cannot be, in the product's words, or nothing when it can.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: The most the list holds, counted from `existing`.

fields.name: maxLength
fields.doc: The longest item; a paste is cut to it as typing is.

fields.name: onAdd
fields.doc: Sends the items; a returned promise holds the next add until it settles, a rejection gives the text back.

fields.name: onTaken
fields.doc: A repeat was refused: the name as the list has it.

fields.name: disabled
fields.doc: Nothing goes in: a pasted list waiting for the request is dropped.

fields.name: danger
fields.doc: A refusal or a failure: the danger ink. A repeat or a tidied item is only said.

fields.name: invalid
fields.doc: The field holds what cannot go in.

members.name: rect
members.type: Ref<{ top: number; left: number; placement: "below" | "above" | "left" | "right"; room?: number | undefined; } | null, AnchorResult | { top: number; left: number; placement: "below" | "above" | "left" | "right"; room?: number | undefined; } | null>

types.name: AnchoredPanelOptions
types.doc: The plumbing of a floating panel: where it stands, when to recompute, and its layer on the overlay stack, which routes Escape and a press outside to it. The arithmetic lives in `utils/anchorPosition` because numbers are the only way to test it; happy-dom has no layout. Scroll repositions with `capture: true`: a scroll event does not bubble, so a window listener never sees the table or drawer body that scrolls under the trigger, and the panel would drift away from it.

fields.name: open
fields.doc: Whether the panel is open; the host drives it (hover for a tooltip, click for a select).

fields.name: trigger
fields.doc: The trigger element the panel stands under; a getter is read on every pass, once the trigger is in the page.

fields.name: panel
fields.type: Ref<HTMLElement | null | undefined, HTMLElement | null | undefined>

fields.name: close
fields.doc: Called on a pointer down outside every layer from this one up, and on Escape unless `onEscape` is given.

fields.name: onEscape
fields.doc: Escape while the panel is the top overlay, when it does more than `close` (a select gives the focus back).

fields.name: returnFocus
fields.doc: Whether the layer gives the focus back to what opened it on close, asked with how it closed; default no, the host does.

fields.name: geometry
fields.doc: Geometry: everything `anchorPosition` takes except what is measured.

fields.name: fallbackWidth
fields.doc: Panel width before the first measurement, when the host knows it.

fields.name: matchTriggerWidth
fields.doc: Panel as wide as the trigger (selects): `panelStyle` carries the width and the clamp uses it.

fields.name: capToRoom
fields.doc: The panel is capped to the room beside the trigger: `panelStyle` carries `--ui-panel-room`, for a `max-height` that reads it.

fields.name: layer
fields.doc: Takes a place in the overlay stack. A hint (a tooltip) does not: it is placed only, the stack knows it as a hint. Default true.

fields.name: opener
fields.doc: What opened the panel, when it is not `trigger` (a field's capsule anchors, its button opens): a window opened from an item of the panel gives the focus back here once the item is gone.

useChartCursor.name: useChartCursor
useChartCursor.doc: One point under the pointer and under the arrow keys. The plot is the one tab stop: focus shows the point last visited (the newest at first), Left and Right step, Home and End jump, and the point is said in `announcement` for a live region. The pointer shows a point while it is over the plot and leaves it to the keyboard when the plot has the focus. A touch has no hover: a tap shows the point under the finger and keeps it until the plot loses the focus, a tap elsewhere; the host lets the page scroll with `touch-action: pan-y` on the plot.

members.name: handlers
members.type: { pointermove: (event: PointerEvent) => void; pointerleave: (event?: PointerEvent) => void; pointerdown: (event?: PointerEvent) => void; focus: () => void; blur: () => void; keydown: (event: KeyboardEvent) => void; }
members.doc: Bind on the plot, the element the points are laid across: `v-on="handlers"` and `tabindex="0"`.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: How many points the axis has; the cursor stays inside them when data changes.

fields.name: describe
fields.doc: The point in words for a screen reader: "September 2026: spending 3,640 EUR".

fields.name: bands
fields.doc: Points stand in bands, as bars do: the pointer picks the band it is over, not the nearest center.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: Where the first focus starts: the `last` point, the newest on a time axis, or the `first`, as a ring is read.

useClipboard.name: useClipboard
