useClipboard.doc: Copy to the clipboard with an outcome flag that resets after `resetMs`: `copied` for the check that replaces a copy glyph, `failed` for the word that says it did not work. Without the Clipboard API (a page over plain HTTP) or with it refused, it copies the old way, through a selected field no one sees; it resolves `false` only when both fail, and never throws. `reset` drops both flags at once, for a new value.

members.name: copied
members.doc: True for `resetMs` after a write that reached the clipboard.

members.name: failed
members.doc: True for `resetMs` after the clipboard refused.

members.name: copy
members.doc: Writes `text`; resolves `true` on success, `false` on a refusal, never throws.

members.name: reset
members.doc: Drops both flags at once, and makes a write still in flight change nothing.

useConfirm.name: useConfirm
useConfirm.doc: Asks a question of the person: `if (await confirm({ message })) remove()`. The `<UiConfirm />` mounted once at the app root shows it and answers; a new question answers the open one `false`.

types.name: ConfirmOptions
types.doc: `if (await confirm({ message })) remove()`, answered by one `<UiConfirm />`; a new question answers the open one `false`.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The question in a few words; defaults to "Are you sure?".

fields.name: message
fields.doc: What happens, in a sentence: "The order and its payments are removed."

fields.name: confirmLabel
fields.doc: The confirm button's label: the action itself, "Delete", beats "Confirm".

fields.name: cancelLabel
fields.doc: The cancel button's label; defaults to "Cancel".

fields.name: tone
fields.doc: `danger` for what cannot be undone: the confirm button turns red.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: The request the answer sends. The window waits for it (the button loads, a second press sends nothing), then closes; a failure closes into an error toast whose Retry asks again. Every way out is refused while it runs, so give it a timeout of its own: a promise that never settles holds the window.

fields.name: success
fields.doc: The success toast, when the result is not in view (a row left a list below the window); without it the window only closes.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: The error toast's title; defaults to "It did not go through".

useControlSize.name: useControlSize
useControlSize.doc: A control's step: its own `size` when the caller gave one, the app's otherwise (`createGrani({ size })`, `sm` unless set; `grani.setSize` moves it and the page follows).

types.name: FocusTrapOptions
types.doc: Keeps keyboard focus inside a modal container while it is active: Tab and Shift+Tab go round its focusable elements, read afresh on every press (a form grows and shrinks). On activation focus goes to `initial()`, else to an element marked `data-autofocus` (a calendar's day), else to the first field, else to the container itself: never to the close button, which comes first in the DOM and would make every dialog open on "close". Focus that strays out while it is on top comes back where it was inside (a Tab that carried it out goes round to the first element). Where the focus goes when it closes is the layer's (`useOverlayStack`); a trap with no layer of its own (a sheet of the page) gives it back to what had it, by `returnFocus`.

fields.name: active
fields.doc: Whether the trap holds; the host binds it to its `open`.

fields.name: container
fields.type: Ref<HTMLElement | null | undefined, HTMLElement | null | undefined>
fields.doc: The element focus stays in. It needs `tabindex="-1"` to take focus itself.

fields.name: initial
fields.doc: The element to focus first, when the host knows better than "the first field".

fields.name: isTop
fields.doc: Whether the host is the top overlay. Focus outside the container is pulled back only then: a menu opened from inside keeps it while it is open.

fields.name: returnFocus
fields.doc: Whether focus goes back where it was on deactivation; default yes. A host on a layer says no: the layer gives it back.

useListAddress.name: useListAddress
useListAddress.signature: useListAddress(filters: F = {} as F, options: ListAddressOptions<F> = {})
useListAddress.doc: The view of a list, kept in the page's address. `filters` names the filters with their values when nothing is chosen: `[]` for several values, `null` for one. `options.sort` is the sort the list opens on and `options.sortKeys` the columns the address may sort by; without `sortKeys`, the app checks the key read from the address before it reaches its request.

types.name: ListAddress
types.doc: Where the address is read and written, for a router the library does not find by itself.

fields.name: read
fields.doc: The query now, read in a reactive scope so Back and Forward reach the list; `null` while the address is another page's.

fields.name: write
fields.doc: Writes the whole query: `push` adds a step to the history, `replace` changes the step in place. A promise that rejects, or resolves to an `Error` (a navigation refused), brings the view back to the address.

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc: Put before each key, so two lists on one page keep their own: `inv` writes `inv.page`.

fields.name: numbers
fields.doc: The filters whose values are numbers, such as ids: read back from the address as numbers.

fields.name: sort
fields.doc: The sort the list opens on, such as `{ key: 'issued', dir: 'desc' }`: an address with no `sort` reads it, and a sort equal to it stays out of the address. Unset, the list opens unsorted.

fields.name: sortKeys
fields.doc: The columns the address may sort by. A `sort` naming another reads as the default sort, so a link or a typed address cannot put a column the app did not offer into the view. Unset, any key is read: the app checks it before it asks.

fields.name: address
fields.doc: Where the address lives; unset, the app's router, else the browser's address and history.

useOverlayShell.name: useOverlayShell
useOverlayShell.doc: The shell a modal overlay stands in, shared by UiModal and UiDrawer so the two never drift: its layer on the overlay stack (painted above what opened before, Escape and a press on the backdrop routed to it only while it is on top, the focus given back on close), the page under it held still, the focus kept inside, and a refused close answered with a shake, since silence reads as a frozen page. What a press or an Escape does (close, go a level up, shake) stays the host's. A window opened over a window hides it (`covered`) until it closes, and the one under comes back on its panel (`returning`); the one that hid it comes and goes without its backdrop moving (`swap`), since the tint on the page stays the same.

members.name: zIndex
members.doc: The overlay's z-index on the stack.

members.name: shaking
members.doc: True for 400 ms after a refused close: the panel shakes.

members.name: said
members.doc: Why the last close was refused, for a status region inside the panel; empty until one is.

members.name: refuse
members.doc: Refuses a close with a shake.

members.name: covered
members.doc: Hidden by a window opened over it: out of sight and out of reach.

members.name: returning
members.doc: Seen again after a window over it closed: its panel rises back, once.

members.name: swap
members.doc: Came in over a window it hid, or leaves with one waiting under it: the backdrop stays as it is.

members.name: returned
members.doc: The panel has risen back.

members.name: arrived
members.doc: In: from now on the tint follows whether a window waits under it.

fields.name: open
fields.doc: Whether the overlay is open; the host's `open` model.

fields.name: panel
fields.doc: The panel: the stack paints it, the trap keeps the focus in it.

fields.name: backdrop
fields.doc: The backdrop, or what holds it and the panel: a press on it outside the panel is the press outside.

fields.name: initial
fields.doc: The element to focus first, when the host knows better than "the first field".

fields.name: onOpen
fields.doc: Runs each time the overlay opens, before the focus goes in.

fields.name: returnFocus
fields.doc: Whether the focus goes back where it was on close; default yes.

fields.name: onEscape
fields.doc: Escape while the overlay is on top: close, go a level up, or shake.

fields.name: onOutside
fields.doc: A press outside the panel (on the backdrop) while the overlay is on top.

fields.name: window
fields.doc: A window: a window opened over it hides it until it closes. A drawer is not one.

fields.name: question
fields.doc: A question about the window under it (`alertdialog`): it never takes that window's place.

fields.name: onReplace
fields.doc: A window that is not a question opened over this one: close and say `true`, or say `false` to stay under it.

useOverlayStack.name: useOverlayStack
useOverlayStack.doc: The layers of this app: the stack, the routing of Escape and a press outside, the focus on close. Acquire on the client only.

members.name: hintShown
members.doc: Whether a hint is on the screen in this app.

members.name: hintClosed
members.doc: When the last hint went away, by `Date.now()`.

members.name: byKeyboard
members.doc: Whether the last input was a key: a focus that follows it is the keyboard's.

members.name: tabbed
members.doc: Whether the last key was Tab and no press came after it.

useScrollRegion.name: useScrollRegion
useScrollRegion.doc: A body whose content runs past its height is a scroll region: it takes a Tab stop, so the arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down, Space and End scroll a long text that holds nothing to focus. A body that fits takes none. Measured when it appears, when it or what it holds changes size, when what it holds is added or taken away, and when the window changes size. A body that fits again while it holds the focus stays a stop until the focus leaves it: a box without its Tab stop would hold a focus the window's own Tab cycle no longer knows. `firstFocus(container)` is where a surface opens when it holds nothing to fill in and its body is long: on the body, so the arrows read the text at once (WAI-ARIA for long dialogs); else `null`, and the focus trap keeps its own order.

members.name: typed
members.doc: Whether the person typed while the last request was out.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The body: a submit that leaves a field `aria-invalid` in it puts the focus on the first one.

fields.name: form
fields.doc: The form: Cmd+Enter presses its own submit button.

fields.name: submitting
fields.doc: A request is out: no second one, and the lock opens when it ends.

fields.name: canSubmit
fields.doc: Whether a submit may go at all (not loading, not held, not read-only).

fields.name: send
fields.doc: Sends the submit; `another` is a "Save and add another".

fields.name: refused
fields.doc: A submit the host refused by marking a field: the surface shakes, as at a refused close.

useTableColumns.name: useTableColumns
useTableColumns.signature: useTableColumns(tableKey: string, columns: MaybeRef<TableColumn<T>[]>, options: TableColumnsOptions = {})

members.name: all
members.doc: Every column, in the given order; the menu lists them.

members.name: visible
members.doc: The columns to draw, in the given order.

members.name: hidden
members.doc: Keys of the hidden columns among the current ones.

members.name: canToggle
members.doc: Whether a column may be hidden: not a required one, and not the last one shown.

members.name: isRequired
members.doc: Whether a column is required: it is always shown.

members.name: toggle
members.doc: Hides a shown column or shows a hidden one; a column that may not be hidden is left as it is.

members.name: reset
members.doc: Back to the default, and the stored choice is forgotten: a later default reaches the person.

members.name: changed
members.doc: Whether the set differs from the default.

types.name: TableColumnsOptions
types.doc: Which columns a table shows, as one person prefers. The choice is personal, not a view of the data, so it lives in the browser's storage and never in the URL: a link sent to someone else must not rearrange their table. The key is the kind of table (`invoices`), not the page: the same records opened elsewhere keep the setting. One instance per kind at a time: two mounted at once in one app do not see each other's ticks, and in dev they warn. However many are hidden, one column stays: an empty table reads as a failed load. Storage. The choice is stored under `grani:columns:<tableKey>`, or `grani:columns:<scope>:<tableKey>` with a `scope`, in `localStorage` unless `createGrani({ storage })` gives the app's own (an object with `getItem`, `setItem` and `removeItem`). A choice made in another tab reaches a mounted table through the browser's `storage` event; the app's own storage sends none, and there the last tab to choose wins. In a browser app the stored choice is read before the first paint, so the table does not jump; on a page rendered by a server it lands once mounted, so hydration matches.

fields.name: required
fields.doc: Keys that cannot be hidden: usually the first column, the one that says what a row is.

fields.name: hiddenByDefault
fields.doc: Keys hidden on the first visit; `reset()` returns to them.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: Whose choice it is, such as the signed-in user's id: two people on one browser keep their own. A ref or a getter follows a sign-in.

fields.name: all
fields.doc: Every column, in the given order; the menu lists them.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: The columns to draw, in the given order.

fields.name: hidden
fields.doc: Keys of the hidden columns among the current ones.

fields.name: canToggle
fields.doc: Whether a column may be hidden: not a required one, and not the last one shown.

fields.name: isRequired
fields.doc: Whether a column is required: it is always shown.

fields.name: toggle
fields.doc: Hides a shown column or shows a hidden one; a column that may not be hidden is left as it is.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Back to the default, and the stored choice is forgotten: a later default reaches the person.

fields.name: changed
fields.doc: Whether the set differs from the default.

useToast.name: useToast
useToast.doc: The queue behind UiToaster. Components call `toast.success(...)` and the toaster at the app root shows it. Feedback on an action goes here: a save that failed, a copy that worked; a field's validation stays by the field and a load error stays inline with its retry. The same toast again while one stands, with no action, is that one card, back at the front with its id.

members.name: toasts
members.doc: Every toast in order of arrival, read-only.

members.name: stack
members.doc: The toasts in the stack, newest first; beyond the limit they wait, their clocks held.

members.name: show
members.doc: Shows a toast from full options and returns its id.

members.name: update
members.doc: Changes a toast by id in place; a new tone or duration restarts its clock.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes one toast by id, or all of them with no argument; an id that is `undefined` closes none.

members.name: promise
members.doc: A request as toasts: `loading` while it runs, then a new one with `success` or `error`; a message that throws gives way to "Done" or "Could not complete the action".

members.name: success
members.doc: `success(title, options?)`: a done action, "Invoice sent".

members.name: error
members.doc: `error(title, options?)`: a failed action, read out at once, a little longer on screen.

members.name: warning
members.doc: `warning(title, options?)`: done, with something to look at.

members.name: info
members.doc: `info(title, options?)`: a fact worth a glance.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The button's text: "Undo", "Open".

fields.name: onClick
fields.doc: Runs once, as the toast closes.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: One line, the fact: "Invoice sent".

fields.name: description
fields.doc: A second line with the detail, optional.

fields.name: tone
fields.doc: Meaning, and with it the glyph and its color: `neutral` (default), `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info`.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: A Lucide glyph in place of the tone's own; the tone still colors it.

fields.name: loading
fields.doc: A request in flight: a spinner instead of the glyph; `promise` sets it.

fields.name: duration
fields.doc: How long it stays once shown: 5 s by default, 7 s for `danger`, 13 s with an `action`.

fields.name: priority
fields.doc: How a screen reader hears it: `high` at once, `low` at a pause; `danger` is `high` by default.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: One button in the toast, "Undo" or "Open"; it never holds what the page needs to work.

fields.name: announce
fields.doc: `false` shows it unread: for an outcome the control has already announced where the focus is (a copy button's own live region).

useToday.name: useToday
useToday.doc: `ticking` says when the minute clock is worth running; without it, it always runs.

types.name: TriggerOptions

useVisibleRows.name: useVisibleRows
useVisibleRows.signature: useVisibleRows(list: Ref<HTMLElement | null | undefined>, rows: string, when: WatchSource, count = PANEL_LIST_ROWS)
useVisibleRows.doc: The height of a list in a panel: five rows and half of the sixth, so the cut says there is more (a hidden scrollbar says nothing). Measured, not computed from a row height: a row with a description or a group heading is taller than the others.
